Lobster meat tossed with mayo, lemon and chives, piled into small toasted brioche rolls with a pinch of paprika.
Wisconsin buffalo wings and blue cheese
Colin's trip to a bar in Wisconsin

Chicken wings baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in hot sauce melted with butter, with blue cheese dip. Pat 1.5kg chicken wings dry and toss with 1 tbsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt. Bake on a rack over a tray at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Melt 60g butter with 125ml hot sauce. Mix 100g crumbled blue cheese with 120g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayo, a squeeze of lemon and pepper for the dip. Toss the hot wings in the sauce and serve with the dip and celery sticks.
M: Turkey breast rolled with sage and onion stuffing, roasted at 180C for 90 minutes, with roast potatoes, sprouts and cranberry sauce.
Jamie's French cottage coq au vin
Jamie writing in his cottage in France

Coq au vin of chicken, bacon, mushrooms and red wine simmered 90 minutes, with crusty bread. Brown 1.2kg chicken thigh cutlets in a heavy pot and set aside. Fry 150g bacon lardons, 12 peeled pickling onions and 250g button mushrooms until golden. Stir in 1 tbsp plain flour, then 500ml red wine, 250ml chicken stock, 2 garlic cloves and thyme. Return the chicken, cover and simmer 90 minutes until very tender. Season, scatter with parsley and serve with a warm crusty baguette.
W: Sponge soaked in sherry, layered with raspberry jelly, custard and whipped cream, chilled overnight, topped with berries.
K: Red wine warmed with orange, cinnamon, cloves and honey, never boiled, ladled into mugs.
T: Christmas in London. Love all around.
D: Interlinked stories of love play out across London in the weeks before Christmas.
P: Serve the mains when everyone arrives for the school Christmas show.

title: Four Weddings and a Funeral
S: Charles racing in late to the first wedding

Blinis topped with crème fraîche, smoked salmon and dill, beside asparagus spears wrapped in prosciutto and grilled. Top 16 blinis with creme fraiche, smoked salmon and dill. Blanch a bunch of asparagus for a minute, wrap each spear in prosciutto and grill until crisp. Arrange both on trays for the first of several weddings.
the old pub where Charles and Carrie stay the night

Aged cheddar, thick-cut ham, sharp pickled onions, a jammy egg with mustard salt and tomato chutney, with crusty bread, cold butter and apple. Boil 4 eggs for 7 minutes, cool in iced water, peel, halve and sprinkle with salt mixed with a pinch of mustard powder. Cut 250g aged cheddar into thick wedges and fold 200g thick-cut ham onto a big board. Add 8 pickled onions, a bowl of tomato chutney, 1 sliced green apple tossed in lemon, a handful of watercress and the eggs. Slice a crusty loaf thickly and serve with a block of cold butter.

Oatcakes spread with cream cheese, topped with smoked salmon, dill and a squeeze of lemon. Spread oatcakes with cream cheese. Top with folds of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Squeeze over a little lemon and lay them out on a slate for a castle wedding in the Highlands.
M: Highland braised lamb, neeps and tatties

Lamb shoulder braised 3 hours with onion, carrots and barley, with mashed neeps and tatties. Season 1.5kg lamb shoulder and brown all over in a heavy pot. Add 2 chopped onions, 3 carrots in chunks, 75g pearl barley, rosemary and 750ml chicken stock. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours until it pulls apart. Boil 800g peeled potatoes and 600g swede separately until soft. Mash the potatoes with 50g butter and a splash of milk and the swede with 30g butter and pepper. Serve the lamb and barley over both with the juices.
Beef topside roasted at 200C to medium, rested, with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes and gravy made from the pan juices.
W: Two lemon butter sponges filled with lemon curd and whipped cream, iced white and finished with fresh flowers like a country wedding. Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and lemon zest, then fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Fill with lemon curd and whipped cream, ice white and decorate with fresh flowers.
K: Gareth's loud waistcoats and louder toasts

Elderflower cordial and lemon over cucumber ribbons, topped with cold sparkling wine. Peel 1 Lebanese cucumber into long ribbons and curl one into each of 4 flutes or wine glasses. Add 20ml elderflower cordial and a squeeze of lemon to each. Top slowly with cold sparkling wine from a 750ml bottle. For drivers, use sparkling water and a little extra cordial.
T: Four weddings. Lots of cake.
D: A charming Englishman keeps running into the same American woman at a run of weddings.
P: Serve the snacks when the guests pour into the first wedding reception.

title: Bridget Jones's Diary
S: Una Alconbury's New Year's Day turkey curry buffet

Leftover turkey or chicken tossed in a mild curry mayo with sultanas and spring onion, spooned onto crackers. Shred 300g cooked turkey breast or chicken. Mix 100g whole egg mayo with 2 tbsp Greek yoghurt, 2 tsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp mango chutney and a squeeze of lemon. Fold in the turkey, 40g sultanas and 2 sliced spring onions and season. Spoon onto 24 crackers or crisp poppadom pieces just before serving and scatter with chopped coriander and toasted flaked almonds.
Shortcrust tartlets baked at 190C for 12 minutes, filled with goat's cheese and caramelised onion.
Bridget's capers in her birthday menu
Baguette slices toasted and spread with cream cheese, topped with smoked salmon, capers and lemon zest.
M: the leek soup that turns blue from the string

Silky leek and potato soup finished with cream, topped with crispy fried leek and chive oil, with crusty bread. Definitely not blue. Slice 3 leeks and soften in 60g butter with 500g diced potatoes for 10 minutes without browning. Add 1L chicken stock and simmer 25 minutes until the potato is very soft. Blend until smooth, stir in 150ml cream and season with salt and white pepper. Fry thin strips of the green leek tops in hot oil until crisp, and blitz chives with 3 tbsp olive oil. Serve the soup with a swirl of cream, the chive oil, crispy leeks and buttered crusty bread. Tie the leeks with kitchen twine, not blue string.
Mark Darcy's gruyère and chive omelette
Mark Darcy rescuing the birthday dinner, reindeer jumper long gone

Three-egg omelettes cooked in butter, filled with gruyère and chives, folded onto warm plates with a green salad. Make one at a time. Beat 3 eggs with a pinch of salt. Melt 15g butter in a 20cm non-stick pan over medium-high heat until foaming. Pour in the eggs and stir quickly with a spatula for 20 seconds, then let it set for 30 seconds until just soft on top. Scatter 30g grated gruyère and chives over one half, fold and slide onto a warm plate. Repeat for 4. Serve with rocket dressed in lemon and oil.
W: the orange marmalade on Bridget's birthday menu
Steamed sponge pudding with orange marmalade in the bottom of the bowl, steamed 90 minutes and turned out with custard.
K: Bridget's diary, alcohol units counted daily

Chilled chardonnay with sliced peach, orange and a splash of peach nectar and soda, poured over ice. Sparkling apple and peach for non-drinkers. Slice 2 ripe peaches and 1 orange into a big jug. Add 750ml chilled chardonnay, 200ml peach nectar and 2 tbsp honey and stir. Chill for at least 1 hour. Fill 4 wine glasses with ice and fruit from the jug, pour in the sangria and top with a splash of soda water. For non-drinkers, swap the wine for sparkling apple juice.
T: Blue soup. Big knickers. Big heart.
D: A thirty-something Londoner keeps a diary of her love life as she falls between her boss and a stiff lawyer.
P: Serve the mains when Bridget cooks her birthday dinner and the soup turns blue.

title: The Proposal
S: Andrew's home town of Sitka, Alaska
Rye crispbread spread with cream cheese, topped with smoked salmon, dill and capers, finished with lemon.
the surprise welcome party at the Paxton house
Crab meat mixed with cream cheese, mayo and spring onion, baked at 190C for 20 minutes until golden, with crackers.
Grandma Annie's honey berries and cream
Grandma Annie's chant in the woods

Blueberries and blackberries tossed with honey and lemon zest, spooned into small bowls over whipped cream. Toss 250g blueberries and 250g blackberries with 2 tbsp honey and the zest of 1 lemon and stand 10 minutes so the juices run. Whip 300ml cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar to soft peaks. Crush 4 shortbread biscuits. Spoon the cream into 4 small bowls, pile the berries and juice on top and scatter with the shortbread crumbs.
M: dinner at the Paxton family house in Alaska
Salmon fillets brushed with maple syrup and grainy mustard, roasted at 200C for 15 minutes, with buttered baby potatoes and green beans.
Barn wedding pot roast and horseradish
the wedding set up in the family barn

Beef chuck braised for 3 hours with onion, carrots and stock, potatoes added late, sliced with pot gravy and a sharp horseradish cream. Season a 1.5kg beef chuck roast and brown all over in a heavy pot. Add 2 quartered onions, 3 carrots in chunks, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp tomato paste, thyme and 500ml beef stock. Cover and braise at 160C for 2 hours. Add 800g potatoes in chunks and braise 1 hour more. Lift out the beef and veg, thicken the liquid with 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with water and pour the gravy over the sliced beef. Mix 150g sour cream with 2 tbsp grated horseradish and a squeeze of lemon to serve on the side.
W: Two vanilla sponges baked at 175C for 25 minutes, sandwiched with strawberry jam and whipped cream, iced white and topped with fresh flowers.
K: Andrew always ordering two of the same coffee, just in case

Strong espresso poured over ice and cold milk with a vanilla bean syrup, served in takeaway cups for the walk into the office. Simmer 80g caster sugar with 80ml water and 1 split vanilla bean for 3 minutes, then cool. Make 4 double shots of espresso, or 300ml very strong coffee, and cool for 5 minutes. Fill 4 tall cups with ice, add 1 tbsp vanilla syrup and 200ml cold milk to each, then pour the espresso over the top. Stir and serve with lids and straws.
T: Marry the boss. Visit Alaska.
D: A pushy book editor facing deportation forces her assistant to marry her, then meets his family in Alaska.
P: Serve the snacks when the family throws the welcome party in Sitka.

title: Crazy Rich Asians
S: Rachel's first night at the hawker centre

Chicken thighs marinated in turmeric, lemongrass and coconut, threaded onto skewers and grilled, with a peanut sauce. Marinate 600g chicken thigh strips in coconut milk, turmeric and finely chopped lemongrass for 2 hours. Thread onto skewers and grill until charred. Warm peanut butter with more coconut milk, lime juice and a little sugar for a thick dipping sauce.
the family folding dumplings together at the Young house
Pork and cabbage dumplings with ginger and spring onion, folded and boiled until they float, with black vinegar and chilli oil.

Raw peanuts fried with crisp garlic, dried chilli and curry leaves, tossed with salt and a pinch of sugar, served warm in small bowls. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wok over medium heat and fry 300g raw peanuts for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until golden. Add 6 thinly sliced garlic cloves, 4 dried chillies broken up and a handful of curry leaves and fry 1 to 2 minutes more until the garlic is crisp. Drain on paper towel, toss with 1 tsp salt and half a teaspoon of sugar and cool slightly so they crunch.
M: Crab or big prawns cooked in a sweet, spicy sauce of tomato, chilli, garlic and ginger, finished with a beaten egg swirled through, with soft buns to mop up.
Wedding banquet prawn and chicken noodles

Egg noodles stir-fried with prawns, chicken and greens in oyster and soy sauce, piled high on a platter. Loosen 400g fresh egg noodles in hot water. Slice 300g chicken thigh and toss with 1 tsp soy and 1 tsp cornflour. Stir-fry in a smoking wok with oil for 3 minutes and set aside. Stir-fry 300g peeled green prawns for 2 minutes and set aside. Fry 3 garlic cloves, then add 2 bunches chopped choy sum stems and leaves and 60ml water. Add the noodles, chicken, prawns, 3 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy and 1 tsp sesame oil and toss. Pile high on a platter.
W: Rachel and Eleanor's game of mahjong

Pandan chiffon cake of whipped egg whites, coconut milk and pandan, baked at 170C for 45 minutes and cooled upside down. Whisk 6 yolks with 60g sugar, 120ml coconut milk, 80ml oil and a teaspoon of pandan paste, then fold in 150g flour. Whisk 6 whites with 100g sugar to stiff peaks and fold in. Bake in an ungreased tube tin at 170C for 45 minutes and cool upside down.
K: Goh family gold mansion iced kopi
Peik Lin's very gold family home

Strong coffee sweetened with condensed milk, poured over ice and served in a gold-rimmed glass, Goh family style. Brew strong coffee and stir 2 tbsp condensed milk into each cup while hot until dissolved. Cool slightly, then pour over glasses packed with ice. Stir well and drink it the way the hawker stalls serve it, sweet and strong.
T: Hawker centre first. Then the family.
D: A New York professor flies to Singapore to meet her boyfriend's family and finds out they're incredibly rich.
P: Serve the snacks when Rachel gets her first taste of the hawker centre.

title: How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days
S: Toasted baguette slices with lemony whipped ricotta, blistered roasted cherry tomatoes, torn basil and a drizzle of honey. Slice a baguette, brush with oil and toast at 200C for 8 minutes. Roast 250g cherry tomatoes with oil and salt for 15 minutes. Whip 250g ricotta with lemon zest and pepper, spread on the toasts and top with tomatoes, basil and a little honey.

Crumbed risotto balls with peas, ham and parmesan, fried golden and crisp, with a bowl of warm marinara for dunking. Make a firm risotto with 300g arborio rice and 1L stock, stir through 100g peas, 100g diced ham and 50g parmesan, then cool. Roll into 16 balls, crumb in flour, egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 180C for 4 minutes. Serve with 400g warm marinara.
Andie's job writing for Composure magazine

Mini bagels split and toasted, spread with cream cheese, topped with smoked salmon, capers and thin red onion. Split 8 mini bagels and toast until golden. Beat 200g cream cheese with the zest of 1 lemon, chopped dill and pepper. Spread thickly on the bagel halves. Top each with a fold of smoked salmon from 200g, a few capers and very thin slices of red onion. Finish with a squeeze of lemon and a dill sprig and serve on a board.
M: Ben's family dinner on Staten Island
Beef and pork meatballs simmered in tomato sauce, served over rigatoni with plenty of parmesan, family style.
Diamond ball eye fillet and red wine
the diamond ball where Andie wears the yellow dress

Beef eye fillet roasted to medium-rare with a red wine sauce, potato gratin and asparagus. Season a 1kg beef eye fillet, sear all over in a hot pan and roast at 200C for 20 to 25 minutes for medium-rare. Rest 10 minutes. Slice 1kg potatoes thinly, layer in a buttered dish with 300ml cream, garlic and salt and bake at 180C for 60 minutes. Deglaze the beef pan with 200ml red wine, add 200ml beef stock and reduce by half, then whisk in 20g butter. Serve with steamed asparagus.
W: Sweet pastry filled with a lemon curd of juice, zest, eggs, sugar and butter, baked at 150C for 20 minutes until just set.
K: Andie losing her voice courtside at the basketball

Cold lager topped with spicy ginger beer and lime in plastic cups, with a mint sprig standing in for the love fern. All ginger beer for non-drinkers. Chill 4 tall plastic cups or glasses. Squeeze a quarter of a lime into each. Pour in 200ml cold lager, tilting the cup, then top with 150ml cold ginger beer. Drop a lime wedge and a mint sprig in each and serve straight away. For non-drinkers, fill with ginger beer and a splash of soda water.
T: Ten days. One love fern.
D: A magazine writer tries to drive a man away in ten days while he tries to make her fall for him.
P: Serve the mains when Ben takes Andie home to meet his family on Staten Island.

title: The Wedding Singer
S: the wedding receptions Robbie sings at
Cocktail franks wrapped in puff pastry strips, egg washed and baked at 200C for 15 minutes, with mustard and tomato sauce.
Cheddar, cream cheese and spring onion rolled into a ball, coated in chopped walnuts, served with crackers.

Salted roasted peanuts set in a golden honey toffee with a little butter and bicarb so it shatters, broken into shards and bagged like airline snacks. Line a tray with baking paper. Heat 200g caster sugar, 60ml honey and 60ml water in a saucepan, stirring until dissolved, then boil without stirring until light golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in 200g salted roasted peanuts and 20g butter and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until amber. Take off the heat, stir in half a teaspoon bicarb and pour onto the tray. Cool 30 minutes, then smash into shards and bag up.
M: Robbie's singing lessons for Rosie, paid in meatballs
Beef and pork meatballs with parmesan, parsley and breadcrumbs, browned and simmered 40 minutes in tomato sauce, over spaghetti.
Reception stuffed chicken and lemon butter

Chicken breasts stuffed with spinach and ricotta, roasted at 200C for 20 minutes, with roast potatoes and beans. Mix 200g ricotta with 60g chopped baby spinach, 30g grated parmesan, lemon zest and pepper. Cut a pocket into the side of 4 chicken breasts and stuff. Sear in oil 3 minutes a side, then roast at 200C for 20 minutes. Roast 800g halved chat potatoes in oil at 200C for 40 minutes. Steam 2 bunches green beans. Melt 60g butter with the juice of 1 lemon and parsley and spoon over the sliced chicken.
W: Julia Gulia's jam and buttercream sponge

Two vanilla butter sponges sandwiched with strawberry jam, iced white with vanilla buttercream and scattered with silver cachous. Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Sandwich with strawberry jam, ice white with buttercream and scatter silver cachous over the top.
K: Pineapple and orange juice topped with lemonade in a big bowl, scoops of lime sherbet floating and fizzing on top, with orange slices. Chill everything well. Pour 1L pineapple juice and 500ml orange juice into a big punch bowl. Just before serving, top with 1.25L cold lemonade and add 1 sliced orange. Float 6 scoops of lime or orange sherbet on top so they foam as they melt. Ladle into cups with a bit of sherbet in each.
T: Somebody kiss me. Somebody feed me.
D: A heartbroken 1985 wedding singer falls for a waitress who's about to marry the wrong guy.
P: Serve the mains when Grandma Rosie hands Robbie her meatballs.

title: My Best Friend's Wedding
S: the seafood restaurant where everyone sings
Oysters on crushed ice with a shallot and red wine vinegar dressing and lemon wedges.
caramel and cheese together, the city's own

Fresh popcorn split in two: half tossed in bubbling caramel and baked crisp, half tossed in butter and cheddar powder, then mixed together in one big bowl. Pop 120g popcorn kernels in oil and split between 2 bowls. For the caramel half, boil 60g butter, 120g brown sugar and 2 tbsp golden syrup for 3 minutes, stir in a pinch of bicarb, toss through one bowl and bake on a tray at 120C for 30 minutes, stirring twice, then cool. For the cheese half, toss the other bowl with 40g melted butter and 3 tbsp cheddar cheese powder and a pinch of salt. Mix both together in one big bowl.
Kimmy singing badly at the karaoke bar
Chicken wings baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in a honey and soy glaze, with sesame.
M: Sirloin steak seared and rested, with a peppercorn sauce, thin fries and a green salad.

Deep pan pizza dough pressed into a tin, layered with mozzarella, Italian sausage and chunky tomato sauce, baked at 220C for 30 minutes. Mix 400g plain flour, 50g fine semolina, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp salt, 60ml olive oil and 250ml warm water, knead 5 minutes and rise 1 hour. Press into an oiled 25cm cake tin and up the sides. Layer 300g sliced mozzarella on the base, then 400g Italian sausage meat pressed flat and browned. Top with a 400g tin crushed tomatoes simmered 10 minutes with garlic and oregano. Sprinkle with parmesan and bake at 220C for 30 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
W: Jules saying Kimmy is crème brûlée and she's jelly
Vanilla crème brûlée baked in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes, chilled and torched, served beside a small cup of raspberry jelly.
K: the boat ride along the Chicago river

Fresh raspberries crushed with lemon and a touch of sugar, topped with cold sparkling wine in flutes. Sparkling grape juice for non-drinkers. Crush 125g raspberries with 1 tbsp caster sugar and the juice of half a lemon and push through a sieve. Spoon 1 tbsp of purée into each of 4 flutes. Slowly top with cold sparkling wine from a 750ml bottle and drop a whole raspberry in each. For non-drinkers, use sparkling grape juice.
T: She's crème brûlée. You're jelly.
D: A food critic realises she loves her best friend just as he's about to marry someone else.
P: Serve dessert when Jules compares Kimmy to crème brûlée.

title: Runaway Bride
S: Maggie's family hardware store in Hale

Popcorn coated in a buttery brown sugar caramel, baked crunchy, salted and scooped into brown paper bags like a shop counter treat. Pop 100g popcorn kernels in 2 tbsp oil in a lidded pot and tip into a large roasting tin. Boil 100g butter, 200g brown sugar, 60ml golden syrup and half a teaspoon salt for 4 minutes, then stir in half a teaspoon bicarb so it foams. Pour over the popcorn and toss. Bake at 120C for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, then spread out to cool. Sprinkle with flaky salt and scoop into paper bags.
the small Maryland town of Hale
Crab meat bound with mayo, mustard, spring onion and breadcrumbs, shaped into small cakes and pan-fried until golden, with lemon.
the town diner where Ike watches Maggie
Grated potato and onion squeezed dry, fried in butter in small cakes until crisp, served with sour cream and chives.
M: Maggie working out she likes her eggs Benedict
Eggs poached 3 minutes, set on toasted English muffins with ham, covered in hollandaise of yolks whisked with melted butter and lemon.
yet another rehearsal dinner for Maggie

Chicken rubbed with butter, lemon and thyme, roasted at 200C for 75 minutes, with roast potatoes and a pan gravy. Rub a 1.8kg chicken with 40g soft butter, lemon zest, thyme and salt and put the halved lemon inside. Roast at 200C for 75 minutes. Parboil 1kg potatoes in chunks for 8 minutes, rough them up and roast in hot oil alongside for 50 minutes. Rest the chicken 10 minutes. Stir 1 tbsp plain flour into the pan juices, whisk in 300ml chicken stock and simmer into gravy. Carve and serve with the potatoes and gravy.
W: all the wedding cakes Maggie has left behind
Two vanilla sponges baked at 175C for 25 minutes, sandwiched with strawberry jam and whipped cream, iced white.
K: breakfast at the diner in Hale

Fresh orange juice blended with vanilla ice cream, cold milk and orange zest into a creamy old-school diner shake. Squeeze 4 oranges to get about 300ml juice and zest one of them. Blend the juice and zest with 6 scoops vanilla ice cream, 200ml cold milk and 1 tbsp honey until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 tall glasses and finish each with a thin orange slice on the rim and a straw.
T: Find out how you like your eggs.
D: A newspaper columnist heads to a small Maryland town to write about a woman who keeps leaving men at the altar.
P: Serve the mains when Maggie finally works out how she likes her eggs.

title: Sweet Home Alabama
S: Melanie's home town of Pigeon Creek
Green tomatoes sliced thick, dipped in egg and cornmeal, fried until golden, served with a lemony remoulade.

Cornmeal, flour, buttermilk, egg and melted butter mixed briefly, baked in a hot cast iron pan at 220C for 20 minutes, with honey butter. Put a 25cm cast iron pan with 20g butter into the oven at 220C to heat. Mix 150g cornmeal, 120g plain flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder and half a teaspoon salt. Whisk in 300ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g melted butter until just combined. Pour into the hot pan so it sizzles and bake 20 minutes until golden. Beat 80g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of salt and serve with warm wedges.
the local bar where Jake drinks
Pecans tossed with melted butter, brown sugar and a pinch of cayenne, roasted at 170C for 12 minutes until glossy.
M: Pigeon Creek cornmeal fish and slaw

Flathead fillets dipped in buttermilk and crunchy cayenne cornmeal, fried crisp, with a tangy buttermilk slaw, hot sauce and lemon. Mix 100g cornmeal, 50g plain flour, 1 tsp paprika, half a teaspoon cayenne and salt. Dip 700g flathead fillets in 200ml buttermilk, then press into the cornmeal. Shallow fry in 1cm of oil at 180C for 2 to 3 minutes a side until crisp. For slaw, toss a quarter each of green and red cabbage, finely shredded, and 1 grated carrot with 100ml buttermilk, 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp cider vinegar and 1 tsp sugar. Serve with lemon wedges and hot sauce.
dinner back home with the Smooters

Chicken drumsticks soaked in buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour, fried at 170C until crisp, with mash and gravy. Soak 8 chicken drumsticks in buttermilk overnight. Dredge in flour seasoned with smoked paprika and salt, then fry at 170C for 12 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Serve with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and gravy made with chicken stock.
W: Jake's glass from lightning strikes on the beach

Pecans in a filling of golden syrup, brown sugar, eggs and butter, baked in shortcrust at 170C for 45 minutes, with cream. Line a pie dish with shortcrust and blind bake. Whisk 3 eggs with 250g golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 60g melted butter. Scatter 200g pecans in the case and pour over the filling. Bake at 170C for 45 minutes until set and serve with cream.
K: sitting on the porch back home in Alabama

Black tea brewed strong, sweetened while hot, cooled and poured over ice with lemon. Brew 6 black tea bags in 1L boiling water for 5 minutes and remove the bags. Stir in 150g sugar while hot, then add 1L cold water. Cool and pour over plenty of ice in tall glasses with lemon slices. Sit on the porch and drink slowly.
T: Lightning glass. Sweet tea.
D: A New York fashion designer goes home to Alabama to divorce the husband she never told anyone about.
P: Serve the mains when Melanie sits down at her parents' table back home.

title: 50 First Dates
S: Lucy building little houses out of her waffles
Mini waffles cooked in a waffle iron, stacked into small houses with a dab of butter and drizzled with maple syrup.
Sushi-grade tuna cubed and tossed with soy, sesame oil and spring onion, served in small cups over rice.
Marine park chilli lime grilled pineapple
Henry's job at the marine park with Jocko the walrus

Pineapple spears grilled until caramelised and charred, finished with lime juice and a little chilli salt. Peel and core 1 ripe pineapple and cut into 12 long spears. Mix 2 tbsp brown sugar with the zest of 1 lime. Brush the spears with a little melted butter and sprinkle with the lime sugar. Grill on a hot barbecue or grill pan for 2 to 3 minutes a side until caramelised and charred. Squeeze over lime juice and sprinkle with a mix of 1 tsp salt and half a teaspoon chilli powder. Serve warm.
M: Beef patties seared on rice, topped with a fried egg and smothered in a brown onion gravy cooked down with stock for 15 minutes.

Chicken thighs marinated in pineapple juice, soy, ginger and brown sugar, grilled until sticky, with rice and slaw. Mix 125ml pineapple juice, 80ml soy, 60g brown sugar, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tbsp grated ginger and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Marinate 1kg chicken thigh in half of it for 4 hours. Simmer the rest for 5 minutes until syrupy. Grill the chicken over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes a side, basting with the glaze, until sticky and charred. Serve with 1.5 cups steamed rice and a slaw of cabbage, carrot and lime.
W: Coconut milk, sugar and cornflour cooked until thick, set in a tray and cut into squares.
K: Sue running the Hukilau Café and keeping an eye on Lucy

Fresh pineapple blended with ginger, lime and mint, strained and poured over ice, topped with soda water and a pineapple wedge. Blend 600g fresh pineapple chunks with 1 tbsp grated ginger, the juice of 1 lime, a few mint leaves and 250ml cold water until smooth. Strain through a sieve into a jug, pressing on the pulp. Fill 4 glasses with ice, divide the juice between them and top each with a splash of soda water. Finish with a pineapple wedge.
T: Waffle houses every morning.
D: A Hawaii vet falls for a woman with no short-term memory and has to win her over again every day.
P: Serve the mains when Lucy builds her waffle house at the Hukilau Café.

title: Forgetting Sarah Marshall
S: Sashimi tuna cubed and tossed with soy, sesame oil and spring onion, spooned onto rice crackers just before serving.

Pineapple spears brushed with honey and lime, grilled until caramelised and charred at the edges. Cut a pineapple into long spears. Brush with honey mixed with lime juice. Grill over high heat, turning, until caramelised and charred at the edges. Serve warm with extra lime. Do less, and the pineapple does more.
Dracula's Taste for Love beetroot dip

Roast beetroot blitzed blood red with feta, garlic, walnuts and lemon, served with oven-baked pita crisps dusted in smoked paprika. Wrap 3 medium beetroot in foil and roast at 200C for 50 minutes until tender, then peel. Blitz with 100g feta, 1 garlic clove, 40g walnuts, the juice of 1 lemon and 3 tbsp olive oil until smooth and season. Cut 4 pita breads into wedges, brush with oil, sprinkle with smoked paprika and salt and bake at 180C for 10 minutes until crisp. Serve the dip with crumbled feta on top.
M: Resort fish tacos with mango salsa
lunch by the pool at the resort

White fish dusted in chilli and cumin, pan-fried, tucked into warm corn tortillas with mango salsa, lime and coriander. Cut 600g firm white fish fillets into strips and toss with 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp cumin, salt and oil. Dice 1 mango, half a red onion and 1 red chilli and mix with coriander and the juice of 1 lime. Pan-fry the fish over high heat for 2 minutes a side until just cooked. Mix 120g sour cream with lime zest. Warm 12 small corn tortillas and fill with shredded cabbage, fish, salsa and lime crema.
the Hawaiian luau at the resort
Pork shoulder rubbed with smoked salt, wrapped in banana leaves and slow cooked at 150C for 5 hours, shredded and served with rice.
W: Ripe mango blended with lime juice and sugar syrup, frozen in a tray and scraped every hour until set, scooped into glasses. Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Blend the flesh of 3 ripe mangoes with the syrup and the juice of 2 limes until smooth. Freeze in a tray, scraping with a fork every hour for 4 hours. Scoop into glasses.
K: Aldous Snow holding court at the resort bar

Dark rum shaken with orange juice, lime and a little orgeat or sugar syrup, poured over crushed ice with a mint sprig. For each drink, shake 45ml dark rum with 60ml orange juice, 20ml lime juice and 15ml sugar syrup over ice. Strain over crushed ice and top with a sprig of mint. Make an orange and lime version without rum for anyone not drinking.
T: Dumped. Go to Hawaii.
D: A TV composer gets dumped by his star girlfriend, flees to Hawaii, and finds her there with her new rock star boyfriend.
P: Serve the snacks when Peter checks into the resort and spots Sarah.

title: The Devil Wears Prada
S: Runway crudités with whipped feta and dill
the Runway office, where nobody admits to eating

Baby carrots, snow peas, radishes and cucumber spears around a whipped feta, lemon and dill dip finished with olive oil and chilli flakes. Blitz 200g feta with 100g Greek yoghurt, the zest and juice of half a lemon and 2 tbsp olive oil until smooth. Stir through 2 tbsp chopped dill. Spread into a shallow bowl, drizzle with more oil and scatter with chilli flakes. Trim 1 bunch baby carrots, 150g snow peas and 1 bunch radishes, cut 1 continental cucumber into spears, and stand everything in ice water for 10 minutes to crisp up. Drain well and arrange neatly around the dip.
Sourdough buttered on the outside, filled with gruyère and cheddar, grilled in a pan until golden and melting, cut into fingers.
Blinis topped with crème fraîche, smoked salmon and chives, beside halved figs with goat's cheese and honey.
M: Andy rushing out to get Miranda's steak for lunch
Sirloin steak seared hard in a smoking pan, butter basted, rested and sliced, with creamed spinach and crispy potatoes.
Nate's birthday, the one Andy misses for work

Chicken thighs browned in butter, braised with white wine and leeks, finished with cream and fresh tarragon, with crusty baguette to mop the sauce. Season 8 skin-on chicken thighs and brown skin side down in a large pan with 20g butter over medium heat for 8 minutes. Turn and remove. Soften 2 sliced leeks and 2 garlic cloves in the fat for 5 minutes. Add 200ml white wine and boil 2 minutes, then 250ml chicken stock. Return the chicken skin side up, cover and simmer 25 minutes. Stir 150ml cream and 2 tbsp chopped tarragon into the sauce and bubble 3 minutes. Serve with warm baguette.
W: Sweet pastry blind baked, filled with vanilla custard and topped with blueberries brushed with warm apricot glaze.
K: Andy racing the coffee back before Miranda arrives

Freshly pulled espresso shaken hard with vodka, coffee liqueur and a touch of sugar syrup, strained into chilled coupes under a thick crema with three coffee beans. Chill 4 coupe glasses in the freezer. Pull 4 shots of espresso, about 120ml, and let them cool for 5 minutes. For each drink, fill a shaker with ice and add 45ml vodka, 30ml coffee liqueur, 30ml espresso and 10ml sugar syrup. Shake as hard as you can for 15 seconds so it foams. Strain into a chilled coupe and float 3 coffee beans on the crema. Serve straight away, on time.
T: Get the coffee. Get the steak. Get it now.
D: A young journalist lands a job as assistant to a terrifying fashion magazine editor.
P: Serve the mains when Andy gets sent out for Miranda's steak.

title: Legally Blonde
S: Popcorn tossed with melted white chocolate tinted pink and a pinch of salt, set and broken into clusters.
Bruiser's pork and sage sausage rolls
Bruiser, Elle's chihuahua, who goes everywhere in her handbag

Pork mince with onion, sage and a little apple rolled in flaky puff pastry, sesame on top, baked golden and served with tomato relish. Heat the oven to 200C. Mix 500g pork mince with 1 finely chopped onion, 1 grated apple, 1 tbsp chopped sage, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 egg, salt and pepper. Cut 2 thawed puff pastry sheets in half, lay a sausage of filling along each, roll up and seal with beaten egg. Cut into 4cm pieces, brush with egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Bake on a lined tray for 20 to 25 minutes until golden. Serve warm with tomato relish.
Strawberries dipped in melted white chocolate, rolled in pink sprinkles and set on baking paper.
M: Elle's first term at Harvard Law
Chicken strips seared, garlic and sun-dried tomatoes added with cream, spinach wilted through, tossed with penne and parmesan.
Harvard clam chowder in cob loaves
Elle's move to Boston for Harvard Law

Bacon, onion and potato simmered with clams, milk and cream into a thick New England chowder, ladled into hollowed cob loaves with crackers. Fry 150g diced bacon in a pot until crisp. Add 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml fish stock, 400ml milk and 500g diced potato. Simmer 15 minutes until the potato is tender. Add 1kg clams (vongole) and cook covered for 5 minutes until open, then pick out the shells. Stir in 150ml cream, thyme and pepper. Hollow out 4 small cob loaves and ladle the chowder in.
W: Lemon cupcakes baked at 175C for 18 minutes, cooled and piped with pink buttercream made with crushed raspberries.
K: Elle Woods and her love of all things pink
Fresh lemon juice and sugar syrup stirred with crushed raspberries and cold water, strained and poured over ice.
T: Pink, positive and prepared.
D: A sorority queen follows her ex to Harvard Law School and turns out to be very good at law.
P: Serve the snacks when Elle shows Paulette the bend and snap at the salon.

title: 13 Going on 30
S: Jenna's thirteenth birthday party in the basement

Popcorn bound in a sticky marshmallow and butter glaze, packed with chopped sour straps and jelly beans, rolled into balls and wrapped like party favours. Pop 100g popcorn kernels and tip into a big bowl, discarding unpopped kernels. Melt 50g butter in a saucepan over low heat, add 250g marshmallows and stir until smooth. Pour over the popcorn with 100g chopped sour straps and 80g jelly beans and fold quickly. With buttered hands, press into 12 tennis ball sized rounds. Set on baking paper for 30 minutes, then wrap in cellophane.
the wishing dust from Matt's dream house
Sugar cookies baked at 180C for 10 minutes, iced pale pink and dusted with edible glitter.
Poise party salmon blinis and melon
the Poise magazine party where Jenna gets the room dancing

Warm blinis with dill crème fraîche, smoked salmon and salmon roe, beside rockmelon wedges wrapped in prosciutto and cracked pepper, served on silver trays. Warm 16 blinis at 180C for 4 minutes. Mix 150ml crème fraîche with 1 tbsp chopped dill and a squeeze of lemon. Top each blini with a spoon of the cream, a fold of smoked salmon (200g total) and a few beads of salmon roe. Cut half a rockmelon into 12 thin wedges, peel and wrap each in half a slice of prosciutto (6 slices). Grind over pepper and arrange both on trays.
M: Mum's lemon and thyme roast chook
Jenna going home to her parents' house

Whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and thyme until the skin crackles, with crunchy roast potatoes, buttered green beans and pan gravy. Heat the oven to 200C. Rub a 1.8kg chicken with 30g soft butter, salt and pepper. Stuff with 1 halved lemon, 4 garlic cloves and a bunch of thyme. Parboil 1kg quartered potatoes for 8 minutes, drain, rough up and toss in oil. Roast the chicken 75 minutes and the potatoes alongside for 60 minutes. Rest the chicken 10 minutes. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices with 300ml stock for gravy. Boil 300g green beans 4 minutes and toss with butter.

Egg noodles stir-fried with chicken, broccoli and capsicum in a sticky soy and honey sauce, in takeaway boxes. Stir-fry 500g sliced chicken thighs until browned. Add broccoli florets and a sliced red capsicum and cook 3 minutes. Toss through 400g cooked egg noodles with soy sauce and honey until sticky. Pack into takeaway boxes.
W: the cake at Jenna's thirteenth birthday

Two layers of vanilla butter sponge filled with raspberry jam, covered in pink buttercream and rolled in rainbow sprinkles, thirteen candles on top. Heat the oven to 175C. Beat 200g soft butter and 200g caster sugar until pale, then 4 eggs one at a time and 1 tsp vanilla. Fold in 250g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Divide between two lined 20cm tins and bake 30 minutes. Cool. Beat 250g butter with 450g icing sugar, 2 tbsp milk and a drop of pink colouring. Sandwich the layers with 150g raspberry jam, ice all over and press sprinkles around the sides.
K: Pineapple juice blended with coconut cream and ice, with a splash of white rum for the adults. Blend 500ml pineapple juice with 200ml coconut cream and a big handful of ice until thick and smooth. Pour into glasses for the kids. Add 30ml white rum to each glass for the grown-ups who turned thirty overnight.
T: Thirty, flirty and hungry.
D: A thirteen-year-old makes a birthday wish and wakes up as a thirty-year-old magazine editor.
P: Serve the snacks when Jenna gets the whole party dancing.

title: Breakfast at Tiffany's
S: Holly eating a pastry and coffee outside the jewellery store at dawn
Puff pastry squares filled with cream cheese and apricot jam, folded, egg washed and baked at 200C for 15 minutes.
Holly's cat, who she just calls Cat

Devilled eggs dusted with paprika, and celery stuffed with cream cheese and chives, on silver trays. Boil 8 eggs, halve, mash the yolks with mayonnaise and pipe back, then dust with paprika. Beat cream cheese with chives and fill short celery sticks. Lay both out on silver trays for a crowded apartment party.
cocktails at Holly's crowded apartment party

Big green olives stuffed with blue cheese, crumbed in panko and fried until crunchy, served hot on picks with a lemon and chive mayo. Drain 24 large pitted green olives and pat dry. Push a little blue cheese (80g total) into each. Roll in 40g plain flour, then 1 beaten egg, then 60g panko crumbs. Heat 5cm oil in a saucepan to 180C and fry the olives in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes until golden. Drain on paper towel. Stir the zest of 1 lemon and 1 tbsp chopped chives into 100g mayonnaise. Serve the olives hot on toothpicks with the mayo.
M: Holly's Thursday visits to Sing Sing, $100 a time

Sirloin steak seared and rested, with a peppercorn sauce, thin fries and a green salad. Cut 1kg potatoes into thin fries and fry twice until crisp. Sear 4 sirloin steaks and rest. Toast cracked peppercorns in the pan, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Serve with fries and a green salad.
Day out chicken, bacon and avocado club
Holly and Paul's day of doing things they've never done

Toasted triple-decker with poached chicken, crisp bacon, avocado, cos and tomato, a lemon mayo through every layer, cut into triangles and pinned. Poach 2 chicken breasts in simmering salted water for 15 minutes, rest 10 minutes and slice. Grill 8 bacon rashers until crisp. Toast 12 slices of white sandwich bread. Mix 100g mayo with the juice of half a lemon. For each sandwich, spread 3 slices with mayo and layer chicken, sliced avocado (2 total) and cos on the first, bacon and sliced tomato on the second, and top with the third. Pin with 4 toothpicks and cut into triangles.
W: Puff pastry rounds filled with custard and topped with berries, baked at 200C for 15 minutes and glazed.
K: A sugar cube soaked in bitters at the bottom of a chilled coupe, a splash of brandy, topped with cold champagne and a long twist of lemon. Chill 4 coupes and a bottle of champagne or other dry sparkling wine. Drop a sugar cube into each glass and shake 3 dashes of aromatic bitters over it. Add 15ml brandy to each. Tip the glass and pour the sparkling slowly down the side so it doesn't foam over, about 120ml each. Peel 4 long strips of lemon zest, twist them over the drinks to spray the oil and drop them in.
1 bottle champagne or dry sparkling wine@Bottle shop
T: Breakfast at the window. Pastry and coffee.
D: A free-spirited New York socialite befriends the struggling writer who moves into her building.
P: Serve the snacks when Holly eats her breakfast outside the jewellery store window.

title: Roman Holiday
S: the princess's day out in Rome
Risotto balls with a mozzarella centre, crumbed and fried at 180C until golden, served with a little tomato sauce.
Whipped ricotta, fig and honey crostini
Ann ordering champagne at the pavement café

Toasted baguette spread with lemony whipped ricotta, topped with fresh fig, a drizzle of honey, crushed pistachios and a few thyme leaves. Slice 1 baguette into 20 thin rounds, brush with olive oil and toast at 200C for 8 minutes. Beat 250g fresh ricotta with the zest of 1 lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt until fluffy. Spread on the toasts. Cut 5 fresh figs into quarters and press one onto each. Drizzle with 2 tbsp honey, then scatter 30g crushed pistachios and a few thyme leaves. Serve with a glass of something sparkling.
the wild Vespa ride through Rome
Ciabatta sliced, toasted with olive oil and rubbed with garlic, topped with chopped tomato, basil and salt.
M: Spaghetti tossed with pecorino, cracked black pepper and a splash of the pasta water until creamy.
the dance on the barge by the Tiber

Chicken thighs browned and braised in tomato, red wine, olives, capers and rosemary until falling apart, with crusty bread for the sauce. Season 8 bone-in chicken thighs and brown well in 2 tbsp olive oil for 8 minutes. Remove. Cook 1 sliced onion, 1 sliced red capsicum and 3 garlic cloves for 5 minutes. Add 125ml red wine and reduce by half, then 800g tinned tomatoes, 2 rosemary sprigs, 80g kalamata olives and 1 tbsp capers. Return the chicken, cover and simmer 40 minutes, uncovering for the last 10 to thicken. Scatter with parsley and serve with ciabatta.
W: Ann eating gelato on the Spanish Steps
Vanilla ice cream and lemon sorbet scooped into cones or glasses, finished with crushed amaretti biscuits on top.
K: Hot espresso shaken hard over ice with a little sugar syrup until frothy, strained into chilled martini glasses with a twist of lemon. Chill 4 martini glasses. Pull 4 double shots of espresso, about 240ml. Working in two batches, fill a cocktail shaker with ice, add half the espresso and 20ml sugar syrup, and shake hard for 20 seconds until thick and foamy. Strain into two glasses. Repeat. Twist a strip of lemon peel over each glass and serve immediately while the foam is still standing.
T: One day in Rome. Gelato on the steps.
D: A runaway princess spends a day in Rome with an American reporter who knows exactly who she is.
P: Serve dessert when Ann sits on the Spanish Steps with her gelato.

title: Some Like It Hot
S: Speakeasy devilled eggs with crispy pancetta
the speakeasy hidden behind Mozzarella's funeral parlour

Boiled eggs with yolks whipped with mayo, mustard and smoked paprika, piped back in and topped with shards of crispy pancetta and chives. Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water, peel and halve. Mash the yolks with 80g mayonnaise, 2 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp white vinegar, salt and a pinch of smoked paprika until smooth. Pipe or spoon back into the whites. Bake 8 slices of pancetta on a tray at 200C for 8 minutes until crisp, cool and break into shards. Top each egg with pancetta, a dusting of paprika and snipped chives.
the Seminole Ritz hotel on the Florida coast
Prawns poached in salted water with lemon, chilled and served on ice with cocktail sauce.
the midnight party in Daphne's upper berth

Sharp cheddar beaten with roasted capsicum, mayo and cayenne into a spread, piled on crackers with thin salami and a slice of cornichon. Grate 250g vintage cheddar. Finely chop 100g drained roasted red capsicum. Mix the cheese and capsicum with 100g mayonnaise, 50g soft cream cheese, a pinch of cayenne and a few drops of hot sauce until spreadable. Chill 30 minutes. Spread generously on 32 water crackers, top each with a fold of salami (100g total) and a slice of cornichon, and stack them on a tray.
M: Lobster tails split and grilled with garlic butter for 6 minutes, with buttered baby potatoes, green beans and lemon.
Friends of Italian Opera meatball spaghetti
the gangsters' banquet for the Friends of Italian Opera

Beef and pork meatballs with parmesan and parsley, browned and simmered in a rich tomato and basil sugo, piled over spaghetti on one big platter. Mix 300g beef mince, 300g pork mince, 50g breadcrumbs soaked in 60ml milk, 1 egg, 40g grated parmesan, 2 tbsp chopped parsley, 1 garlic clove and salt. Roll into 20 balls and brown in olive oil. Remove. Soften 1 onion and 2 garlic cloves, add 1.4kg passata and simmer 10 minutes. Return the meatballs, cover and simmer 30 minutes, adding basil at the end. Cook 500g spaghetti, toss with some sauce and pile onto a platter with the meatballs and more parmesan.
W: the giant birthday cake at the gangsters' banquet
Vanilla sponge baked in three tins at 175C for 25 minutes, stacked with jam and cream, iced white and topped with candles.
K: the girls mixing Manhattans in a hot water bottle
Bourbon stirred with sweet vermouth and bitters over ice, strained with a cherry. Use a jug, not a hot water bottle.
T: Nobody's perfect. Dinner is.
D: Two musicians on the run from the mob disguise themselves as women in an all-girl band.
P: Serve the drinks when the girls throw a party in Daphne's sleeper berth on the train.

title: It Happened One Night
S: Peter handing Ellie a raw carrot by the road
Young carrots peeled and served raw, standing in a glass, with a creamy dip of sour cream, chives, dill and lemon.
the long overnight bus north from Miami
Buttered white bread with ham, cheddar and yellow mustard, cut in halves and wrapped in wax paper for the trip.
the auto camp cabin with the blanket hung between the beds

Dill pickle chips in a crisp cornmeal crust, fried hot and salted, with a cold buttermilk ranch dip on the side. Drain 400g dill pickle slices and pat very dry. Whisk 1 egg with 125ml buttermilk. Mix 75g plain flour, 75g fine cornmeal, 1 tsp paprika and salt. Dip the pickles in the buttermilk, then the flour mix. Fry in batches in oil at 180C for 2 minutes until golden, drain and salt. For the dip, mix 100g sour cream, 60ml buttermilk, 2 tbsp mayo, chopped dill, chives and a crushed garlic clove.
M: Peter cooking breakfast in the auto camp cabin
Soft scrambled eggs, crisp bacon and buttered toast, served on tin plates with chives scattered over the eggs.
Roadside diner pot roast with gravy
the long trip north to New York by bus, car and foot

Beef chuck seared hard and braised for hours with onion, carrot and stock until it pulls apart, with potatoes cooked in the juices and a thick gravy. Heat the oven to 160C. Season 1.5kg beef chuck and brown all over in oil in a casserole. Remove. Fry 2 onions and 3 carrots in chunks for 5 minutes, stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tbsp plain flour, then 750ml beef stock, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and thyme. Return the beef, cover and cook 2 hours. Add 800g halved potatoes and cook 1 hour more. Lift out the beef and vegetables and simmer the liquid until it thickens to gravy.
W: Peter's lesson on how to dunk a doughnut
Yeasted doughnuts fried at 175C until golden, rolled in cinnamon sugar and served with hot coffee for dunking.
K: Peter showing Ellie how to dunk a doughnut properly

Strong coffee whisked with melted dark chocolate, hot milk and cinnamon, poured into thick mugs and topped with whipped cream and grated chocolate. Brew 500ml strong coffee. In a saucepan, heat 500ml milk with 100g chopped dark chocolate, 2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tsp ground cinnamon, whisking until the chocolate melts and it steams, about 5 minutes. Whisk in the coffee. Whip 150ml cream to soft peaks. Pour the mocha into 4 thick mugs, spoon over the cream and grate a little more chocolate on top. Serve with the doughnuts for dunking.
T: Dunk the doughnut properly.
D: A runaway heiress travels by bus from Miami to New York with a reporter who wants her story.
P: Serve dessert when Peter shows Ellie how to dunk a doughnut.

title: Amélie
S: the crates outside Monsieur Collignon's grocery
Crisp radishes with their leaves on, served with soft butter and flaky salt for dipping, beside a pile of baby carrots.
the Café des 2 Moulins in Montmartre
Baguette slices toasted and topped two ways: brie with fig jam, and ham with Dijon, laid out on a wooden board.
Amélie skipping stones on the Canal Saint-Martin

Potatoes sliced paper thin on a mandoline, fried until crisp and tossed with thyme salt and lemon zest, with a garlicky aioli for dipping. Slice 3 large washed potatoes 1 to 2mm thick on a mandoline. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes, drain and dry very well on tea towels. Heat oil in a deep saucepan to 170C and fry in small batches for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden. Drain on paper towel. Crush 1 tsp sea salt with 1 tsp thyme leaves and the zest of half a lemon and toss through. Stir a crushed garlic clove into 150g mayonnaise for the aioli.
M: Chicken thighs browned and braised with white wine and mushrooms for 40 minutes, finished with cream, served with buttery mash.
the café in Montmartre where Amélie waits tables

Ham and gruyère between slices of white bread, spread with béchamel, grilled until bubbling and blistered, topped with a runny fried egg and chives. Make béchamel: melt 30g butter, stir in 30g plain flour for 1 minute, whisk in 300ml milk and simmer 3 minutes until thick, then add nutmeg, salt and 40g grated gruyère. Spread 8 slices of white bread with Dijon, fill 4 sandwiches with 200g ham and 120g gruyère. Toast in a buttered pan 3 minutes a side. Spread the tops thickly with béchamel, add more gruyère and grill at 220C for 4 minutes until blistered. Top each with a fried egg and chives.
W: Amélie cracking the burnt sugar with her spoon
Vanilla custard baked in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes, chilled, sugar scattered on top and torched until it sets hard.
K: the regulars at the Café des 2 Moulins

Crème de cassis poured into chilled flutes and topped slowly with cold dry sparkling wine, finished with a fresh raspberry or blackberry dropped in. Chill 4 champagne flutes and a bottle of dry sparkling wine for at least 2 hours. Pour 15ml crème de cassis into each flute. Tilt the glass and top slowly with the sparkling wine, about 120ml each, so the cassis rises through it and turns the glass a deep pink. Drop a raspberry or blackberry into each and serve straight away. For non-drinkers, top cassis cordial with soda water instead.
T: Crack the crème brûlée.
D: A shy Paris waitress secretly sets out to improve the lives of the people around her.
P: Serve dessert when Amélie cracks the top of her crème brûlée with a spoon.

title: Silver Linings Playbook
S: Pat Sr's crabby snacks for the Eagles game
Crab meat mixed with cream cheese, mayo, lemon and spring onion, spread on small toasts and grilled until golden at the edges.
the homemade snacks Pat Sr swears bring the Eagles luck
Mini meatballs of beef and pork with parmesan, baked at 200C for 15 minutes, tossed in a sticky tomato glaze, served on toothpicks.
Philly soft pretzels with beer mustard
the Eagles game on the TV in Philadelphia

Chewy yeasted pretzels dipped in a bicarb bath, scattered with rock salt and baked deep brown, with a hot honey and beer mustard for dunking. Mix 500g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sugar and 320ml warm water, knead 8 minutes and rest 1 hour. Heat the oven to 220C. Roll into 8 long ropes and twist into knots. Simmer 2L water with 70g bicarb soda and dip each pretzel for 30 seconds. Place on lined trays, brush with egg, sprinkle rock salt and bake 12 to 14 minutes. Mix 80g wholegrain mustard, 2 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp lager for dipping.
M: Rib eye frozen 30 minutes, shaved thin, seared on a hot plate with onions, provolone melted over, piled into long rolls.
Pat's mum Dolores cooking for the family on game day

Pork ribs, Italian sausages and meatballs browned and simmered for hours in a garlicky tomato sauce, tossed through rigatoni with parmesan and basil. Brown 600g pork ribs and 4 Italian sausages in olive oil in a large pot. Roll 400g beef mince with 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs and 30g parmesan into 16 meatballs and brown. Remove all the meat. Fry 4 sliced garlic cloves for 1 minute, add 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1.4kg passata and 250ml water. Return the meat, cover partly and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, stirring often. Cook 500g rigatoni, toss with sauce and serve with the meat, basil and parmesan.
W: Pat and Tiffany's awkward date at the diner
Bran muffins with raisins, buttermilk and brown sugar, baked at 190C for 20 minutes, served warm with butter.
K: watching the Eagles with Pat Sr and his lucky handkerchief

Cold lager topped with crisp green apple juice and a squeeze of lime, poured into frosty pint glasses with thin apple slices floating on top. Put 4 pint glasses in the freezer for 30 minutes. Juice 2 limes. Pour 200ml cold lager into each glass, then top with 150ml chilled cloudy green apple juice and a squeeze of lime. Slice 1 green apple very thin and float 2 slices in each glass. For non-drinkers, use ginger beer in place of the lager.
T: Crabby snacks and homemades.
D: A man fresh out of a psychiatric hospital forms an unlikely bond with a young widow who needs a dance partner.
P: Serve the snacks when Pat Sr lays out his crabby snacks and homemades for the game.

title: The Big Sick
S: Crisp oven fries tossed hot with chaat masala, chilli and lime, scattered with coriander and red onion, a cool mint yoghurt for dipping. Heat the oven to 220C. Cut 1kg potatoes into thin chips, soak 20 minutes, drain and dry well. Toss with 3 tbsp oil and roast 35 minutes on lined trays, turning once, until crisp. Toss hot with 2 tsp chaat masala, half a tsp chilli powder, salt and the juice of half a lime. Scatter with chopped coriander and finely diced red onion. Blend 200g Greek yoghurt with a handful of mint and a pinch of salt for dipping.
the women who just happen to drop by for dinner

Spiced potato, peas and onion folded into pastry triangles, fried at 180C until crisp, with mint and coriander chutney. Boil and crush 600g potatoes with 150g peas, fried onion and a spoon of garam masala. Cut spring roll pastry into strips, fill and fold into triangles. Fry at 180C until crisp. Blitz mint and coriander with a little water, lemon and salt for chutney.
Hospital cafeteria toasties with tomato soup
Kumail stuck in the hospital cafeteria with Emily's parents

Cheddar and mozzarella toasties grilled crisp in butter and cut into dippers, with shots of roasted tomato and basil soup on the side. Roast 1kg halved tomatoes, 1 onion in wedges and 4 garlic cloves with oil and salt at 200C for 35 minutes. Blitz with 400ml stock and a handful of basil, simmer 5 minutes and season. Fill 8 slices of white bread with 120g grated cheddar and 80g grated mozzarella, butter the outsides and cook in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side. Cut into fingers and serve with the soup in small cups.
M: the family dinners Kumail's mum keeps setting up
Chicken thighs marinated in yoghurt and spices, layered with par-cooked basmati, fried onions and saffron milk, sealed and baked at 170C for 45 minutes.

A thick, buttery crust pressed up the sides of a deep tin, layered with mozzarella, fennel sausage and chunky garlic tomato sauce, baked until bubbling. Mix 400g plain flour, 7g yeast, 1 tsp salt, 60g melted butter and 230ml warm water, knead 5 minutes and rest 1 hour. Heat the oven to 220C. Press into an oiled 28cm cake tin and up the sides. Layer 300g sliced mozzarella, then 400g Italian sausage meat in flat patches. Simmer 400g crushed tomatoes with 2 garlic cloves and oregano for 10 minutes and spread over the top. Scatter 40g parmesan and bake 30 to 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
W: Rice simmered slowly in milk with cardamom and sugar until creamy, served warm or chilled with pistachios.
K: Black tea simmered with milk, ginger, cardamom and cinnamon, sweetened and strained into cups. Bring 500ml water to the boil with sliced ginger, a few crushed cardamom pods and a cinnamon stick. Add 4 black tea bags and simmer 2 minutes. Pour in 500ml milk and raw sugar to taste, simmer 5 minutes more and strain into cups.
T: Family dinner. Surprise guest.
D: A Pakistani-American comic falls for a grad student who falls seriously ill, and gets to know her parents at the hospital.
P: Serve the mains when Kumail's mum sits him down to family dinner with yet another surprise guest.

title: Palm Springs
S: Nyles floating in the pool on a pizza float, forever
Pizza dough rolled thin, cut into rounds, topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni, baked at 220C for 10 minutes.
the wedding reception in the desert, the same one every day

Mini tostadas topped with raw tuna dressed in lime, soy and sesame, smashed avocado, pickled jalapeño and a squeeze of chipotle mayo. Cut 8 small corn tortillas into rounds with a 7cm cutter, brush with oil and bake at 200C for 8 minutes until crisp. Dice 250g sashimi-grade tuna and toss with 1 tbsp soy, the juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp sesame oil and sliced spring onion. Mash 1 avocado with salt and lime. Mix 3 tbsp mayo with 1 tsp chipotle in adobo. Top each tostada with avocado, tuna, a slice of pickled jalapeño and a dot of mayo.
Nyles and Sarah's dance at the desert bar
Halved jalapeños filled with cream cheese and cheddar, wrapped in bacon and baked until crisp.
M: Tala and Abe's wedding fish tacos
another day at Tala and Abe's wedding

White fish dusted in chilli and cumin, pan-fried, in warm tortillas with slaw, lime crema and pickled onion. Dust 600g white fish in chilli, cumin and salt and pan-fry until just cooked. Quickly pickle sliced red onion in lime juice. Mix sour cream with lime for a crema. Fill warm corn tortillas with shredded cabbage, fish, crema and pickled onion.
Reception chicken with spinach and ricotta
the wedding dinner Nyles has eaten more times than he can count

Chicken breasts stuffed with spinach, ricotta and lemon, roasted golden, with a lemon caper butter sauce and crushed baby potatoes. Heat the oven to 200C. Boil 800g baby potatoes 15 minutes. Mix 150g ricotta, 60g wilted chopped spinach, 30g parmesan and lemon zest. Cut a deep pocket in 4 chicken breasts and fill. Sear in oil 3 minutes a side, then roast 18 minutes. Crush the potatoes with butter and salt. In the pan, melt 60g butter with the juice of 1 lemon and 1 tbsp capers and spoon over the chicken.
W: the same wedding cake, every day
Lemon sponge baked in two tins at 175C for 30 minutes, filled with lemon curd and cream, iced white.
K: Cold Mexican-style lager over ice with lime, hot sauce, a dash of Worcestershire and tomato juice, in a glass rimmed with chilli salt. Mix 2 tbsp salt with 1 tsp chilli powder on a plate. Rub the rims of 4 tall glasses with lime and dip into the salt. Fill with ice. Into each glass add 30ml lime juice, 60ml tomato juice, 4 dashes hot sauce and a dash of Worcestershire. Top slowly with 250ml cold lager, stir gently and add a lime wedge. Use soda water instead of beer for anyone not drinking.
T: Same wedding. Same day. Different snacks.
D: Two strangers get stuck reliving the same wedding day in Palm Springs over and over.
P: Serve the snacks when Nyles floats in the pool on his pizza float.

title: Set It Up
S: Harper and Charlie sharing pizza in the empty office
Pizza dough stretched thin, topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni, baked at 250C for 10 minutes, eaten straight from the box.

Franks grilled until split, in soft buns with mustard and fried onions, wrapped in paper. Fry 2 sliced onions slowly until soft and golden. Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split. Tuck into soft buns with the onions and yellow mustard and wrap in paper. Hand them to the bosses as the kiss cam swings around.
Stadium pretzel bites with cheese sauce
the baseball game where Harper and Charlie set up the kiss cam

Bite-sized soft pretzels boiled in a bicarb bath, salted and baked golden, served warm with a smooth cheddar and beer cheese sauce. Make a dough with 375g plain flour, 7g yeast, 1 tsp salt and 250ml warm water, knead 5 minutes and rest 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 220C. Roll into ropes and cut into 3cm pieces. Boil in 2L water with 60g bicarb soda for 20 seconds, drain, brush with egg, sprinkle with salt and bake 12 minutes. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp flour, whisk in 200ml milk and 60ml lager, then 150g grated cheddar until smooth.
M: the assistants playing matchmaker for their bosses

Sirloin steaks seared and rested, sliced with a cream and peppercorn sauce, crispy roast potatoes and buttered asparagus. Roast 1kg potato chunks at 220C for 45 minutes. Sear 4 sirloin steaks and rest. Toast cracked peppercorns in the pan, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Steam asparagus and toss with butter. Serve on white plates.
the assistants working past midnight in New York

Egg noodles wok-tossed with crispy chicken, broccolini and capsicum in a sticky soy, honey and garlic sauce, sesame and spring onion on top, served in takeaway boxes. Slice 500g chicken thighs and toss with 1 tbsp cornflour and 1 tbsp soy. Mix 3 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Soak 400g fresh egg noodles in hot water for 2 minutes and drain. Stir-fry the chicken in a hot wok with oil for 5 minutes until crisp. Add 1 bunch broccolini and 1 sliced red capsicum for 2 minutes, then the noodles and sauce. Toss 2 minutes and top with sesame seeds and spring onion.
W: the office parties the assistants have to organise
Vanilla cupcakes baked at 175C for 18 minutes, cooled and piped with vanilla buttercream and sprinkles.
K: Iced salted caramel latte for the boss
Harper and Charlie fetching coffee for their bosses

Double espresso poured over ice and cold milk, swirled with homemade salted caramel and topped with lightly whipped cream and a pinch of sea salt. Make the caramel: melt 100g caster sugar in a saucepan until amber, take off the heat and whisk in 60ml cream and 20g butter, then half a tsp sea salt. Cool. Pull 4 double shots of espresso. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, add 2 tbsp caramel and 200ml cold milk to each, then pour the espresso over. Top with whipped cream (100ml whipped) and a pinch of salt.
T: Order the pizza. Set up the bosses.
D: Two overworked assistants plot to set up their demanding bosses so they can finally get some free time.
P: Serve the mains when Harper and Charlie share a late-night pizza in the empty office.

title: To All the Boys I've Loved Before
S: Peter learning to love Lara Jean's Korean yoghurt drinks

Tangy yoghurt blended with milk, honey and lemon, swirled with strawberry purée and frozen into ice blocks, the yoghurt drink flavour on a stick. Blend 300g plain yoghurt with 200ml milk, 3 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp lemon juice until smooth and pourable. Blitz 150g strawberries with 1 tbsp caster sugar. Half fill 8 ice block moulds with the yoghurt, add a spoon of strawberry purée to each, then top up with yoghurt and swirl with a skewer. Insert sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours. Run the moulds under warm water to release.
Ski trip hot tub choc bites
the hot tub on the school ski trip

Marshmallows dipped in melted dark chocolate, rolled in crushed peppermint lollies and set on baking paper. Melt 150g dark chocolate. Dip 20 marshmallows halfway and roll the chocolate end in crushed peppermint lollies. Set on baking paper for 20 minutes. Pack them for the school ski trip, especially the hot tub bit.
Lara Jean's little sister Kitty, who started it all

Freshly popped corn tossed in a sweet and salty Korean-style honey butter glaze, baked until crunchy and finished with flaky salt. Heat the oven to 150C. Pop 100g popcorn kernels in 2 tbsp oil in a large covered pot over medium heat, shaking often, and tip into a big bowl. Melt 60g butter with 3 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp brown sugar and bubble for 1 minute. Pour over the popcorn, add half a tsp salt and toss well. Spread on lined trays and bake 10 minutes, stirring once. Cool, break up and sprinkle with flaky salt.
M: Dad giving Korean cooking a red hot go

Beef rump sliced thin and marinated in soy, pear, garlic and sesame, seared hot, served with rice and quick cucumber kimchi. Slice 600g beef rump thin and marinate in soy, grated pear, crushed garlic and sesame oil for an hour. Sear hot in batches. Serve with jasmine rice and cucumbers tossed with salt, chilli and a little vinegar as quick kimchi.
Lara Jean and Peter's fake relationship

Smashed beef patties with double cheddar, pickles, lettuce and a tangy burger sauce in toasted brioche buns, with crunchy shoestring fries. Roll 600g beef mince into 8 balls. Mix 4 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tbsp mustard and 1 tbsp chopped pickles for the sauce. Bake 750g frozen shoestring fries at 220C for 20 minutes. Heat a heavy pan very hot, smash the balls flat and cook 2 minutes, flip, add a slice of cheddar to each and cook 1 minute. Toast 4 brioche buns, spread with sauce and stack 2 patties each with lettuce and pickles.
W: Hatbox love letter choc chip cookies
the five letters hidden in Lara Jean's hatbox

Chewy cookies made with nutty browned butter, brown sugar and chunks of dark and milk chocolate, sprinkled with flaky salt while warm. Melt 170g butter in a saucepan and cook until it smells nutty and turns golden brown. Cool 10 minutes. Whisk with 150g brown sugar, 100g caster sugar, 1 egg, 1 egg yolk and 2 tsp vanilla. Stir in 250g plain flour, half a tsp bicarb and half a tsp salt, then 200g chopped dark and milk chocolate. Chill 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 180C. Roll into 16 balls and bake 10 to 11 minutes. Sprinkle with flaky salt and cool on the tray.
K: Mashed fresh strawberries and syrup at the bottom of the glass, topped with cold milk.
T: The letters are out. The snacks are in.
D: A teenager's secret love letters are mailed out, and she starts a fake relationship to cover it up.
P: Serve the snacks when Peter brings Lara Jean a Korean yoghurt drink.

title: Always Be My Maybe
S: Sasha growing up eating at Marcus's house
Rice topped with sautéed spinach, carrot and beef mince cooked in soy and garlic, a fried egg and gochujang.
Marcus's band, Hello Peril, playing gigs around town
Chicken wings fried twice until crackly, tossed in a sticky glaze of gochujang, honey and garlic, scattered with sesame.
Tiny tasting menu salmon cucumber cups
the absurd fancy dinner with the tiny plates and Keanu

Thick cucumber rounds hollowed into cups, filled with yuzu crème fraîche and cured salmon, finished with salmon roe and a single chive. Cut 2 continental cucumbers into 2cm thick rounds and scoop a hollow from each with a melon baller, leaving a base. Mix 100g crème fraîche with 1 tsp yuzu or lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Dice 150g smoked salmon finely. Spoon or pipe the cream into each cup, top with salmon, a few beads of salmon roe (40g total) and a short piece of chive. Serve on a long plate, deliberately small.
M: the kimchi stew Marcus's mum taught Sasha to make
Pork belly and kimchi simmered with gochugaru, garlic and stock, tofu and spring onion added at the end, served with rice.

Salmon roasted under a sticky white miso and honey glaze, over sushi rice with quick pickled cucumber, edamame, nori strips and chilli mayo. Rinse and cook 2 cups sushi rice, then season with 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar and salt. Mix 3 tbsp white miso, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp mirin and 1 tsp soy. Heat the oven to 200C. Brush over 4 salmon fillets and roast 12 minutes. Slice 1 cucumber thin and toss with 2 tbsp rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar. Boil 200g frozen edamame 3 minutes. Build bowls with rice, salmon, cucumber, edamame, sliced nori and mayo mixed with chilli sauce.
W: the sweet snacks of Sasha's childhood
Small pancakes of flour, egg and milk cooked in butter, filled with sweet red bean paste, folded and pan-fried until golden.
K: Roasted barley tea steeped in hot water for 10 minutes, served hot in small cups or chilled and poured over ice.
T: Kimchi stew. Tiny fancy dinners.
D: A celebrity chef reconnects with her childhood best friend when she comes home to San Francisco.
P: Serve the mains when Sasha cooks the kimchi stew Marcus's mum taught her.

title: Anyone But You
S: Huntsman in the pants harbour prawns
the spider that ends up in Ben's pants

Cooked king prawns piled on ice with lemon wedges and a seafood sauce of mayo, tomato sauce and a dash of hot sauce. Pile crushed ice onto a platter and arrange 500g cooked prawns on top with lemon wedges. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce and a dash of hot sauce. Serve in a bowl beside the prawns for a Sydney Harbour wedding.
the wedding party taking in Sydney
Mini beef pies of mince and gravy in shortcrust with puff lids, baked at 200C for 20 minutes, with tomato sauce.
Opera House oysters with eschalot dressing
the wedding party taking in the Sydney Harbour views

Freshly shucked Sydney rock oysters on crushed ice with a sharp red wine vinegar and eschalot dressing, cracked pepper and lemon wedges. Finely dice 2 eschalots and mix with 80ml red wine vinegar, a pinch of sugar and plenty of cracked black pepper. Leave 15 minutes. Pile crushed ice onto a large platter. Check 24 freshly shucked oysters for shell grit and loosen each from its shell. Sit them on the ice with the dressing in a small bowl and a teaspoon, plus 2 lemons cut into wedges. Serve straight away.
M: Rosemary lamb cutlets with potato salad

Frenched lamb cutlets marinated in garlic, rosemary and lemon, grilled pink over high heat, with a warm potato salad of mustard, capers and herbs. Marinate 12 lamb cutlets in 3 tbsp olive oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp chopped rosemary and lemon zest for 30 minutes. Boil 1kg halved chat potatoes 15 minutes until tender. Whisk 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 2 tsp wholegrain mustard and 1 tbsp capers. Toss through the warm potatoes with parsley and sliced spring onion. Grill the cutlets on a very hot barbecue 2 to 3 minutes a side, rest 3 minutes and serve with lemon.
the destination wedding by the water
Barramundi fillets pan-fried skin side down until crisp, with lemon butter and capers, and crushed potatoes.
W: the Sydney wedding that throws them together

Meringue baked at 120C for 90 minutes and cooled in the oven, topped with whipped cream, passionfruit, kiwifruit and strawberries. Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, passionfruit, kiwifruit and strawberries.
K: toasting the couple at the Sydney wedding

Fresh passionfruit pulp and a splash of elderflower cordial in chilled flutes, topped with cold Australian sparkling wine and a sprig of mint. Chill 4 flutes and a bottle of Australian sparkling wine. Scoop the pulp from 4 passionfruit and spoon 1 tbsp into each glass with 15ml elderflower cordial. Top slowly with about 120ml sparkling wine, stirring once to lift the pulp. Finish with a small sprig of mint. For non-drinkers, use sparkling apple juice or soda water instead of the wine.
T: Sydney wedding. Harbour prawns.
D: Two people who can't stand each other pretend to be a couple at a destination wedding in Sydney.
P: Serve the snacks when the wedding party heads out on the harbour.

title: Ticket to Paradise
S: Chicken thighs marinated in turmeric, lemongrass and coconut milk, grilled on skewers until charred, with a lime and peanut sauce.
Seaweed farm nori crisps with sesame salt

Nori sheets sandwiched with rice paper, brushed with sesame oil, fried until shatteringly crisp and dusted with toasted sesame, chilli and salt. Brush 6 rice paper sheets lightly with water and press a nori sheet onto each. Cut into 5cm strips. Heat 3cm vegetable oil in a wok to 180C and fry a few strips at a time for 10 to 15 seconds until they puff and crisp. Drain on paper towel. Toast 2 tbsp sesame seeds in a dry pan and crush with 1 tsp salt and half a tsp chilli flakes. Brush the crisps with a little sesame oil and dust with the sesame salt.
David and Georgia's beer pong comeback
Prawn crackers fried in hot oil for a few seconds until they puff, drained and served with sweet chilli sauce.
M: dinner with Gede's seaweed farming family

Day-old rice fried hot with chicken, garlic, chilli and kecap manis until smoky, topped with a fried egg and cucumber. Stir-fry 400g diced chicken thighs with crushed garlic and chopped red chilli in a very hot wok. Add 4 cups cold cooked jasmine rice and 3 tbsp kecap manis and toss until smoky. Serve topped with a fried egg and cucumber slices.
Banana leaf snapper with sambal matah
the beach in Bali where Lily falls for Gede

Snapper fillets rubbed with turmeric, chilli, garlic and lime, grilled in banana leaves, topped with a raw lemongrass and eschalot sambal, with coconut rice. Pound 2 garlic cloves, 2 red chillies, 2cm turmeric and the juice of 1 lime into a paste and rub over 4 snapper fillets. Wrap each in a softened banana leaf and grill or barbecue 10 minutes, turning once. Cook 1.5 cups jasmine rice with 200ml coconut milk and water. For the sambal, finely slice 4 eschalots, 2 lemongrass stalks, 2 chillies and 3 makrut lime leaves, mix with 3 tbsp oil, lime juice and salt. Spoon over the fish.
W: Black sticky rice soaked overnight, simmered with water and palm sugar until thick, topped with salted coconut cream.
K: David and Georgia's plan to stop the wedding

Coconut water and pineapple juice with lime and mint over ice. Fill tall glasses with ice and mint leaves. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice, then squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir and serve cold, watching the sun go down on a beach in Bali.
T: Stop the wedding. Eat first.
D: A divorced couple team up to stop their daughter from marrying a man she just met in Bali.
P: Serve the mains when both families sit down together in Bali.

title: Leap Year
S: Soda bread of flour, buttermilk, bicarb and salt, baked at 200C for 35 minutes until it sounds hollow, served warm with salted butter.
the rugged west coast of Ireland
Brown bread spread thickly with butter, topped with smoked salmon, capers, black pepper and a squeeze of lemon.
Potato farls with butter and chives
the long trip across the Irish countryside

Soft potato cakes of buttery mash and flour, cut into wedges and fried in butter until golden, served hot with salted butter and chives. Boil 750g floury potatoes until soft, drain and mash smooth with 40g butter and 1 tsp salt. While warm, mix in 120g plain flour and 2 tbsp chopped chives to a soft dough. Halve and pat each into a 1cm thick round on a floured bench, then cut into quarters. Cook in a dry or lightly buttered pan over medium heat for 4 minutes a side until golden and speckled. Serve hot with butter and more chives.
M: dinner at the pub in Dingle
Lamb neck simmered 2 hours with potatoes, carrots, onion and thyme until the potatoes break down and thicken the stew.

Chuck steak slow cooked in stout with onions, carrots and thyme until dark and rich, baked under a flaky puff pastry lid, with buttery mash. Toss 1.2kg diced chuck in 3 tbsp flour and brown in batches in oil. Fry 2 sliced onions and 2 carrots for 5 minutes, add 1 tbsp tomato paste, 440ml stout, 300ml beef stock and thyme. Return the beef, cover and simmer 2.5 hours until tender, then cool slightly. Heat the oven to 200C. Spoon into a pie dish, cover with a puff pastry sheet, brush with egg and bake 25 minutes. Serve with mash.
W: Apples cooked with butter and cinnamon under an oat crumble, baked at 180C for 35 minutes, with custard. Peel and slice 5 green apples and cook with 30g butter and cinnamon for 5 minutes. Spoon into a dish. Rub 70g butter into oats, flour and 80g brown sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes and serve with warm custard.
K: Hot strong coffee with brown sugar and a splash of whiskey, topped with lightly whipped cream. Stir a spoon of brown sugar into a cup of hot strong coffee until dissolved. Add 30ml whiskey for the grown-ups. Lightly whip cream until just thick and pour it gently over the back of a spoon so it floats on top.
T: Propose on the twenty-ninth. Eat stew on the thirtieth.
D: A woman travels to Ireland to propose to her boyfriend on Leap Day and ends up crossing the country with a grumpy innkeeper.
P: Serve the mains when Declan serves dinner at his pub in Dingle.

title: Bull Durham
S: Hit Bull Win Steak ballpark franks
the bull sign out past the outfield

Franks grilled until split, tucked into soft buns with yellow mustard and pickle relish, wrapped in paper like at the stand. Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split and blister. Tuck each into a soft bun with a stripe of yellow mustard and a spoon of pickle relish. Wrap tightly in paper so the bun steams, then hand them out like the stand behind home plate.
Crash and Nuke killing time in the dugout
