Melt 200g soft caramels with 2 tbsp cream until smooth and spread over the nougat. Chill 30 minutes. Melt 250g milk chocolate with 1 tsp oil and pour over the top. Chill 1 hour until set, then cut into 12 bars with a hot knife.
K: rationing the last of the water

Fresh watermelon blitzed with lime and mint, strained and topped with ice-cold water so every drop goes a long way. Cut 1.5kg seedless watermelon into chunks and blend with the juice of 3 limes, a small handful of mint leaves and 2 tbsp caster sugar until smooth. Strain through a sieve into a big jug, pressing on the pulp. Stir in 500ml cold water and chill for 30 minutes. Pour over ice into 4 glasses and garnish with lime wheels and mint sprigs.
T: The end of the world. The last of the snacks.
D: A group of actors are trapped in a Hollywood house party when the apocalypse hits.
P: Serve the sweets when they fight over the last chocolate bar.

title: Idiocracy
S: the giant warehouse store of the future

A huge bowl of pretzels, corn chips, crackers and peanuts tossed in butter, ranch seasoning and smoked paprika and oven-toasted until crunchy. Melt 60g butter with 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tsp dried ranch seasoning, 1 tsp smoked paprika and 1/2 tsp garlic powder. Toss with 150g pretzels, 150g corn chips, 150g cheese crackers and 150g roasted peanuts in a large roasting tin. Bake at 150C for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. Cool on the tray so it crisps, then tip into a very big bowl.
Future cheese fries with chicken salt

Crisp chips tossed in chicken salt, covered in a smooth cheddar cheese sauce and finished with crispy bacon and spring onion. Bake 1kg frozen chips at 220C for 25 minutes and toss with 2 tsp chicken salt. Grill 4 rashers bacon until crisp and chop. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp flour, whisk in 250ml milk and simmer until thick. Stir in 150g grated cheddar and 1/2 tsp mustard until smooth. Pile the chips on a platter, pour over the cheese sauce and scatter with bacon and sliced spring onion.
M: Joe teaching them to water the crops

Grilled lemon herb chicken over crisp cos, avocado, corn, cherry tomatoes and cucumber with a creamy buttermilk ranch dressing. Marinate 600g chicken breast in 2 tbsp olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1 crushed garlic clove and 1 tsp dried oregano for 20 minutes. Grill 6 minutes a side, rest and slice. Grill 2 corn cobs and cut off the kernels. Whisk 100ml buttermilk, 3 tbsp mayonnaise, chopped chives and dill. Toss 2 chopped cos lettuces, 250g halved cherry tomatoes, 1 sliced cucumber and 1 avocado. Top with chicken and corn and drizzle with dressing.
W: waking up 500 years in the future

Vanilla cupcakes with a hidden raspberry jam centre, topped with swirls of bright blue raspberry buttercream and silver sprinkles. Beat 125g butter with 150g caster sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 120ml milk. Divide between 12 cupcake cases and bake at 180C for 18 minutes. Cool, cut a small hole in each and fill with 1 tsp raspberry jam. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar, 50g mashed raspberries and a few drops of blue colouring until fluffy. Pipe on top and finish with silver sprinkles.
K: Brawndo, it's got what plants crave

A bright green lime, cucumber and mint cooler with orange and a pinch of salt, topped with soda for a fizzy homemade electrolyte drink. Blend 1 Lebanese cucumber, a handful of mint leaves, the juice of 4 limes, the juice of 2 oranges, 3 tbsp honey and a pinch of salt until smooth. Strain into a jug and chill for 30 minutes. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour in the green mix to halfway and top up with 600ml cold soda water. Stir and garnish with lime wheels.
T: It's got electrolytes.
D: An average army librarian wakes up 500 years in the future to find he is now the smartest man alive.
P: Serve the drink when the electrolytes come up.

title: Mr. Deeds
S: Soft pizza dough knots baked golden and brushed with garlic parsley butter and parmesan, served with warm marinara for dipping. Cut 500g pizza dough into 12 strips, roll each into a 20cm rope and tie into a knot. Lay on a lined tray and rest 15 minutes. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes until golden. Melt 60g butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves and 2 tbsp chopped parsley. Brush the hot knots all over and scatter with 40g finely grated parmesan. Serve with 300ml warmed marinara sauce.
Greeting card cheese and tomato pinwheels
the greeting card poems Deeds writes

Flaky puff pastry rolled with sundried tomato pesto, ham, basil and cheese, sliced into pinwheels and baked golden. Lay 2 sheets thawed puff pastry flat. Spread each with 2 tbsp sundried tomato pesto, then top with 4 slices of ham, a few basil leaves and 60g grated tasty cheese. Roll up tightly, chill for 15 minutes, then cut each roll into 12 slices. Lay cut-side down on a lined tray, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 18 minutes until puffed and golden.
M: A hand-stretched pizza with rich tomato sauce, mozzarella, pepperoni and garlic mushrooms, finished with oregano and chilli oil. Divide 750g pizza dough into 2 and stretch each into a 30cm round on oiled trays. Spread each with 100ml pizza sauce. Fry 200g sliced mushrooms with 1 crushed garlic clove in 1 tbsp oil for 4 minutes. Top the bases with 300g grated mozzarella, 120g pepperoni and the mushrooms. Bake at 240C for 12 to 14 minutes until blistered. Scatter with dried oregano and drizzle with chilli oil.
W: New York baked cheesecake with berries
Deeds's time in New York City

A dense, creamy baked vanilla cheesecake on a buttery biscuit base, topped with a glossy mixed berry sauce. Crush 200g plain sweet biscuits and mix with 80g melted butter. Press into a lined 20cm springform tin and chill. Beat 500g soft cream cheese with 150g caster sugar, then beat in 3 eggs, 150g sour cream, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tsp vanilla. Pour over the base and bake at 150C for 55 minutes until just set. Cool in the oven with the door ajar, then chill 4 hours. Simmer 300g frozen berries with 50g sugar for 5 minutes and spoon over.
K: the small-town spot back in Mandrake Falls

Ice-cold cola poured over scoops of vanilla ice cream so it foams up, served in tall glasses with a cherry and a long spoon. Chill 4 tall glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Add 2 scoops vanilla ice cream to each glass. Slowly pour cold cola down the side of each glass until it foams to the top, letting it settle and topping up, about 300ml per glass. Finish with a spoon of whipped cream from 100ml thickened cream and a cocktail cherry. Serve with straws and long spoons.
T: Mandrake Falls' finest pizza.
D: A small-town pizzeria owner inherits a fortune and moves to New York, where he stays exactly himself.
P: Serve the pizza when Deeds is back at his shop in Mandrake Falls.

title: Uncle Buck
S: Sticky golden caramel popcorn shaped into balls with a pinch of salt, rolled in rainbow sprinkles for a proper kids' birthday party. Pop 100g popcorn kernels in 2 tbsp oil and tip into a big bowl, removing unpopped kernels. Melt 60g butter with 200g marshmallows and 80g brown sugar over low heat, stirring until smooth, then add a pinch of salt. Pour over the popcorn and stir quickly to coat. Let it cool for 2 minutes, then with buttered hands squeeze into 12 balls. Roll in 50g rainbow sprinkles and set on baking paper for 20 minutes.
Buck's night at the bowling alley

Hot crunchy chips smothered in rich beef gravy and melted cheddar, finished with chopped chives and a sprinkle of chicken salt. Bake 1kg frozen chips at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, and toss with 1 tsp chicken salt. Melt 30g butter, stir in 2 tbsp plain flour for 1 minute, then whisk in 400ml beef stock and 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce and simmer 5 minutes until thick and glossy. Pile the chips onto a platter, scatter with 150g grated cheddar and pour over the hot gravy so the cheese melts. Finish with chopped chives.
M: Uncle Buck cooking for the kids

A big breakfast plate of crispy bacon, pork sausages, fluffy scrambled eggs, hash browns and baked beans with hot buttered toast. Bake 8 frozen hash browns at 220C for 20 minutes. Fry 8 pork sausages over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning. Fry 8 rashers bacon until crisp. Warm a 420g tin baked beans. Whisk 8 eggs with 60ml milk and salt, then cook in 30g butter over low heat, stirring gently, until just set. Toast 8 slices of bread and butter them. Pile everything onto 4 big plates with tomato sauce.
W: Buck flipping a pancake the size of a hubcap

One huge fluffy buttermilk pancake cooked in your biggest pan, piled with butter, maple syrup, sliced banana and crispy bacon bits. Whisk 300g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar and a pinch of salt. Whisk in 2 eggs, 400ml buttermilk and 40g melted butter until just combined. Heat a large 28cm non-stick pan over low heat and grease with butter. Pour in all the batter, cover with a lid and cook 10 minutes until bubbles set on top. Slide onto a plate, flip back in and cook 5 minutes more. Top with butter, 100ml maple syrup, 2 sliced bananas and crumbled crisp bacon.
K: Ice-cold milk shaken up with chocolate malt powder and a scoop of ice cream until frothy, served in big glasses with straws. Put 1L cold full cream milk, 6 tbsp chocolate malt powder, 2 tbsp cocoa, 2 tbsp honey and 4 scoops vanilla ice cream in a blender. Blend for 30 seconds until smooth and very frothy. Pour into 4 big glasses. Sprinkle a little extra malt powder over the froth and serve straight away with straws.
T: Pancakes the size of a hubcap.
D: A lovable slob uncle looks after his brother's three kids for the week.
P: Serve the sweets when Buck flips the giant pancake.

title: The Great Outdoors
S: Lakeside crumbed fish bites with tartare

Bite-size pieces of flathead in crisp panko crumbs, fried golden and served with a homemade caper and pickle tartare and lemon wedges. Cut 500g flathead fillets into 3cm pieces. Toss in 50g plain flour, dip in 2 beaten eggs, then coat in 120g panko crumbs. Shallow fry in oil at 180C for 2 minutes a side until golden, then drain. For the tartare, mix 150g mayonnaise with 1 tbsp chopped capers, 2 tbsp chopped dill pickles, 1 tbsp chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon. Serve hot with the tartare and lemon wedges.
the campfire at the lake cabin

Toasted marshmallows and squares of milk chocolate sandwiched between crunchy graham-style biscuits, with a dark chocolate and salted caramel version too. Lay 16 plain sweet wheatmeal biscuits on a lined tray. Top 8 of them with a square of milk chocolate and the other 8 with dark chocolate and a little caramel sauce. Thread 16 large marshmallows onto skewers and toast over a fire or gas flame until golden, or grill on the tray for 1 to 2 minutes. Put 2 marshmallows on each chocolate biscuit and press another biscuit on top. Eat while warm and melting.
M: Chet taking on the 96 ounce steak

A huge chargrilled rump sliced to share, with garlic butter, crispy roast potatoes, onion rings and a wedge salad with ranch. Rub a 1.5kg piece of rump steak with oil and salt. Toss 1kg halved potatoes in oil and roast at 220C for 40 minutes. Grill the steak over high heat for 8 minutes a side for medium rare, then rest 10 minutes. Melt 60g butter with 2 crushed garlic cloves. Bake 400g frozen onion rings for 15 minutes. Cut 1 iceberg lettuce into wedges and drizzle with ranch. Slice the steak thickly, pour over the garlic butter and serve.
W: the bear left with a bald head

A jammy blueberry pie with lemon zest in a golden flaky crust, sprinkled with sugar and served warm with vanilla ice cream. Toss 750g frozen blueberries with 120g caster sugar, 3 tbsp cornflour and the zest and juice of 1 lemon. Line a 23cm pie dish with 1 sheet shortcrust pastry and fill with the berries. Cover with a second sheet, crimp the edges and cut 4 slits on top. Brush with 1 beaten egg and sprinkle with 1 tbsp sugar. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes, then 180C for 35 minutes until bubbling. Cool 30 minutes and serve with ice cream.
K: Chet's wild ride behind the boat

Ice-cold root beer poured over vanilla ice cream until it foams up, served in frosty mugs with a cherry on top. Chill 4 large mugs or glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Add 2 scoops vanilla ice cream to each. Slowly pour cold root beer down the side until it foams to the top, letting it settle and topping up, about 300ml per mug. Add a cocktail cherry to each and serve straight away with straws and long spoons.
T: The 96 ounce challenge.
D: A family's quiet lake holiday is wrecked when the rich, loud brother-in-law and his family turn up.
P: Serve the main when Roman takes on the Old 96er.

title: Stripes
S: Boot camp crackers with pimento cheese

Crisp crackers with a sharp, creamy pimento cheese spread of vintage cheddar, roasted capsicum and a kick of cayenne. Grate 250g vintage cheddar finely. Mix with 120g mayonnaise, 80g chopped roasted red capsicum from a jar, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper and black pepper until well combined but still a little chunky. Chill for 30 minutes so the flavours settle. Spoon into a bowl, dust with a pinch of paprika and serve with 250g crackers and celery sticks.

Cocktail frankfurts tossed in a sticky honey, mustard and tomato glaze until shiny, served on toothpicks with a mustard dipping pot. Score 30 cocktail frankfurts diagonally a few times each. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan and fry the franks for 3 minutes until the cuts open up. Add 3 tbsp tomato sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp American mustard and 1 tbsp Worcestershire and toss for 2 minutes until sticky and glazed. Serve on toothpicks with a little pot of wholegrain mustard.
M: the drill sergeant they drive up the wall

A hearty beef meatloaf with a tangy tomato glaze, sliced thick and served with buttery mash, peas and a rich brown onion gravy. Mix 800g beef mince, 1 grated onion, 1 egg, 60g breadcrumbs, 2 tsp Worcestershire and salt. Press into a lined loaf tin and spread with 4 tbsp tomato sauce mixed with 1 tbsp brown sugar. Bake at 180C for 1 hour. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and milk. Fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes, stir in 1 tbsp flour, then 400ml beef stock and simmer to a gravy. Serve with 300g peas.
W: A dark, moist chocolate layer cake filled and covered with fudgy chocolate icing, served in thick slices with cream. Mix 300g self-raising flour, 300g caster sugar, 60g cocoa and 1 tsp bicarb. Whisk in 2 eggs, 250ml milk, 125ml oil and 250ml boiling water. Divide between two lined 20cm tins and bake at 180C for 30 minutes. Cool. Melt 150g dark chocolate with 100g butter, then beat in 250g icing sugar and 4 tbsp milk until thick and glossy. Sandwich and cover the cakes with the icing and serve with whipped cream.
K: the armoured RV they borrow without asking

Strong hot coffee sweetened with brown sugar and spiked with Irish whiskey, with a thick layer of lightly whipped cream floating on top. Brew 800ml strong coffee. Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water, then tip it out. Stir 2 tsp brown sugar and 40ml Irish whiskey into each glass, then fill with hot coffee to 2cm from the top. Lightly whip 150ml thickened cream until it just thickens but still pours. Slowly pour the cream over the back of a spoon so it floats on top. Leave out the whiskey for anyone not drinking.
T: That's the fact, dinner.
D: A cab driver who has lost everything joins the army with his best mate.
P: Serve the mains when the platoon finally comes together.

title: Fletch
S: Country club Bloody Mary prawn cocktail

Chilled king prawns over shredded cos with a spicy Bloody Mary cocktail sauce of tomato, horseradish, Worcestershire and lemon. Peel 600g cooked king prawns, leaving the tails on. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 3 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tbsp horseradish cream, 1 tsp Worcestershire, a few drops of hot sauce, 1/2 tsp celery salt and a squeeze of lemon. Shred 1 baby cos lettuce into 4 glasses. Spoon over some sauce, then hang the prawns around the rim. Dust with paprika and serve with lemon wedges and a celery stick.
Beach kiosk fish bites with lime aioli
Fletch undercover on the LA beach

Bite-size snapper pieces in a light, crisp batter, fried golden and served with a garlicky lime aioli and a sprinkle of chilli salt. Cut 500g snapper fillets into 3cm pieces. Whisk 120g plain flour, 30g cornflour, 1 tsp baking powder and 220ml cold soda water into a batter. Dip the fish and fry at 180C for 3 minutes until crisp and golden, then drain. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 1 crushed garlic clove and the zest and juice of 1 lime. Sprinkle the fish with sea salt and a pinch of chilli flakes and serve with the aioli.
M: Steak sandwich and a steak sandwich
the order put on the Underhills' tab

Thin seared rump on toasted Turkish bread with caramelised onions, melted Swiss cheese, rocket, tomato and hot English mustard mayo. Slowly fry 3 sliced onions in 30g butter and 1 tbsp brown sugar for 20 minutes until jammy. Bat 4 rump steaks to 1cm thick, season and sear in a very hot pan for 1 minute a side. Lay a slice of Swiss cheese on each and cover for 30 seconds to melt. Toast 4 halved Turkish rolls. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 2 tsp hot English mustard. Build each with mayo, rocket, tomato, steak and onions. Make two each.
W: the country club Fletch talks his way into

Vanilla ice cream with homemade hot fudge sauce, whipped cream, toasted salted peanuts and a maraschino cherry in tall glasses. Heat 150ml thickened cream with 60g brown sugar and 30g butter until bubbling. Take off the heat and stir in 120g chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of salt until smooth and glossy. Toast 60g salted peanuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes and chop. Scoop 1L vanilla ice cream into 4 tall glasses. Pour over the warm fudge, top with whipped cream from 150ml cream, peanuts and a cherry.
K: the drinks charged to the Underhills

Vodka and tomato juice spiked with horseradish, Worcestershire, hot sauce and lemon, in a celery salt rimmed glass with a crunchy celery stick. Mix 1 tbsp celery salt with 1 tsp cracked pepper on a saucer, wet the rims of 4 tall glasses with lemon and dip. Fill with ice. In a jug, stir 800ml tomato juice with 180ml vodka, the juice of 1 lemon, 2 tsp horseradish cream, 2 tsp Worcestershire and 6 dashes hot sauce. Pour into the glasses and add a celery stick and a lemon wedge. Leave out the vodka for a Virgin Mary.
T: Put it on the Underhills' tab.
D: An undercover reporter investigating drug dealing gets a very strange offer from a millionaire.
P: Serve the mains when Fletch orders at the club on the Underhills' tab.

title: Meet the Fockers
S: Jack's circle of trust, still very small

Crisp crumbed Cuban croquettes with a creamy ham béchamel centre, fried golden and served with a garlicky lime aioli. Melt 60g butter, stir in 80g plain flour for 2 minutes, then slowly whisk in 500ml milk until very thick. Stir in 200g finely chopped leg ham, a pinch of nutmeg and pepper. Spread on a tray, cover and chill 3 hours. Shape into 16 small logs, roll in flour, dip in 2 beaten eggs and coat in 120g breadcrumbs. Fry at 180C for 3 minutes until golden. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 1 crushed garlic clove and lime juice.
the Fockers' laid-back home in Coconut Grove

Crisp Florida-style fritters packed with chopped prawns, capsicum and spring onion, served with a tangy key lime and chilli dipping sauce. Chop 400g peeled green prawns. Mix 150g self-raising flour, 1 egg, 150ml soda water, 1/2 diced red capsicum, 2 sliced spring onions, 1/2 tsp Cajun seasoning and salt into a thick batter, then fold in the prawns. Drop heaped tablespoons into oil at 180C and fry 3 minutes, turning, until golden. Drain. For the sauce, mix 100g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp sweet chilli sauce and the juice of 2 limes.
M: Wall of Gaylord mojo roast pork
Bernie and Roz's shrine to their son

Pork shoulder marinated in garlic, orange, lime and cumin, slow-roasted until tender, with black beans, rice and fried sweet plantain or banana. Blitz 8 garlic cloves, the juice of 2 oranges and 2 limes, 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp dried oregano, 60ml olive oil and salt. Rub over a 1.5kg boneless pork shoulder and marinate overnight. Roast covered at 160C for 3 hours, then uncovered at 200C for 30 minutes. Fry 1 onion and 1 capsicum, add 2 drained tins black beans and 1 tsp cumin and simmer 10 minutes. Serve with 300g rice and 2 sliced bananas fried in butter.
W: Jinx and Moses key lime pie
the cat and the dog who never got along

A sharp, creamy lime custard set in a crunchy biscuit base, topped with whipped cream and fresh lime zest. Crush 200g plain sweet biscuits and mix with 80g melted butter. Press into a 23cm pie dish and bake at 180C for 8 minutes. Whisk 4 egg yolks with a 395g tin condensed milk, then whisk in 150ml lime juice and the zest of 2 limes. Pour into the base and bake at 160C for 15 minutes until just set. Cool, then chill 3 hours. Top with 300ml whipped cream and more lime zest.
K: White rum muddled with fresh mint, lime and sugar, topped with soda over crushed ice. Leave out the rum for a virgin mojito. In each of 4 tall glasses, muddle 8 mint leaves with half a lime cut into wedges and 2 tsp caster sugar until the sugar dissolves. Fill with crushed ice. Pour 45ml white rum into each, then top with 120ml soda water. Stir from the bottom with a long spoon to pull the mint up through the ice. Garnish with a big mint sprig and a lime wheel.
T: Welcome to the family. Dinner's on.
D: The Byrnes family travel to Florida to meet the Focker parents before the wedding.
P: Serve the mains when the two families sit down together.

title: Strange Brew
S: Peameal back bacon on a bun
Bob and Doug's Canadian back bacon

Thick slices of back bacon rolled in cornmeal, fried crisp and stacked in soft buns with maple mustard and fried onions. Cut 600g piece of back bacon into 8 thick slices and press both sides into 60g fine cornmeal. Fry in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden and cooked through. Fry 2 sliced onions in the same pan for 8 minutes. Mix 3 tbsp wholegrain mustard with 2 tbsp maple syrup. Split and toast 8 soft white buns, spread with the maple mustard and fill with bacon and onions.
the doughnut shop Bob and Doug love

Light, eggy twisted choux crullers fried golden and dipped in a thin honey glaze that sets crackly on the ridges. Bring 250ml water, 100g butter and a pinch of salt to the boil. Beat in 150g plain flour until it forms a ball, then cool 5 minutes. Beat in 3 eggs one at a time. Pipe 10 rings with a star nozzle onto squares of baking paper. Lower into oil at 180C, paper side up, peel off the paper and fry 3 minutes a side. Drain. Whisk 150g icing sugar, 2 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp water and dip the warm crullers.
M: Bob and Doug's Great White North

Crisp chips topped with squeaky fresh cheese curds or torn mozzarella and smothered in a rich, peppery beef gravy. Bake 1.2kg frozen thick-cut chips at 220C for 30 minutes until crisp. Melt 40g butter, stir in 3 tbsp plain flour and cook 2 minutes until nutty. Whisk in 600ml beef stock, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 1 tsp cracked pepper and simmer 5 minutes until glossy. Tear 300g fresh cheese curds or bocconcini into pieces. Pile the hot chips into 4 bowls, scatter the cheese over and pour the very hot gravy on top.
W: Flaky little pastry tarts filled with a gooey maple, brown sugar and butter filling with raisins and pecans, baked until just set. Cut 12 rounds from 2 sheets shortcrust pastry and press into a greased muffin tin. Whisk 100g brown sugar, 80ml maple syrup, 60g melted butter, 1 egg, 1 tsp vanilla and a pinch of salt. Put a few raisins and chopped pecans from 40g each into each case. Pour the filling two-thirds of the way up. Bake at 190C for 15 to 18 minutes until the filling bubbles and is just set. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes.
K: Ice-cold lager topped with fresh lemonade and a splash of maple syrup and lemon, served by the stubby glass with a lemon wedge. Stir 3 tbsp maple syrup with the juice of 2 lemons in a jug until combined. Chill 4 beer glasses. Pour 1 tbsp of the maple lemon mix into each glass, then half fill with cold lager, about 180ml. Top with 120ml cold lemonade, pouring slowly down the side to keep the head. Add a lemon wedge. Swap the lager for ginger beer for anyone not drinking.
T: Take off, eh. Then dinner.
D: Two hosers try to get free beer and stumble onto a plot at the Elsinore brewery.
P: Serve the beer when Bob and Doug try to get their free case.

title: Dirty Work
S: the doc who needs the cash as much as they do

Oven-crisped wings tossed in buttery hot sauce with a chunky blue cheese and sour cream dip for payback with a kick. Toss 1.2kg chicken wings with 2 tsp baking powder and salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once. Toss in 100ml hot sauce melted with 50g butter. For the dip, mash 100g blue cheese into 150g sour cream with a squeeze of lemon. Serve the wings hot with the dip and celery sticks.
Mitch losing one job after another

Warm, salty soft pretzel bites with a sharp hot mustard and honey dipping sauce, snacks for the next job interview. Cut 500g pizza dough into 32 small pieces. Simmer 2L water with 60g bicarb, drop in the pieces for 20 seconds and drain. Lay on a lined tray, brush with 1 beaten egg and sprinkle with sea salt flakes. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes until deep brown. Stir 3 tbsp American mustard, 1 tbsp hot English mustard and 2 tbsp honey together for dipping and serve the bites warm.
M: Pops, Sam's dad, who needs the operation
A patty melt on rye with Swiss cheese and fried onions, old-school diner food Pops would order.
W: the revenge plan on the crooked developer

Vanilla ice cream piled with warm homemade fudge sauce, salted peanuts, whipped cream and a cherry on top. Heat 150ml thickened cream with 60g brown sugar and 30g butter until it bubbles. Off the heat, stir in 120g chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of salt until glossy. Roughly chop 80g salted roasted peanuts. Scoop 1L vanilla ice cream into 4 sundae glasses. Pour over the warm fudge, top with whipped cream from 150ml cream, scatter with the peanuts and finish each with a cherry.
K: a drink with Pops, Sam's old man

Rye whiskey over ice topped with spicy ginger ale, a squeeze of lime and a dash of bitters. Ginger ale and lime alone for non-drinkers. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice. Pour 45ml rye whiskey into each. Add a squeeze of lime juice and 2 dashes of aromatic bitters. Top each with 150ml cold ginger ale and stir once gently so it keeps the fizz. Garnish with a lime wedge. For anyone not drinking, make it with ginger ale, lime and bitters only.
T: Revenge served hot.
D: Two lifelong mates start a revenge-for-hire business to raise money for a heart operation.
P: Serve the mains when Mitch and Sam open Dirty Work for business.

title: Screwed
S: Crisp breadsticks wrapped in prosciutto, served with marinated olives and cubes of aged cheddar, fancy snacks for the back of the limo. Wrap 12 grissini breadsticks with half a slice of prosciutto each, from 100g, spiralling it around the top half. Warm 200g mixed olives in a small pan with 2 tbsp olive oil, the zest of 1 orange, 1 crushed garlic clove and a sprig of rosemary for 3 minutes, then cool slightly. Cut 150g vintage cheddar into cubes. Stand the grissini in a tall glass and serve with the olives and cheese.
Rusty, the best mate with the bad ideas

Crisp chips with chicken salt and a jug of hot homemade beef gravy for pouring over, diner style. Bake 1kg frozen chips at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, and toss with 2 tsp chicken salt while hot. Melt 30g butter in a small pan, add 1 finely chopped small onion and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour for 1 minute, then whisk in 400ml beef stock and 1 tsp Worcestershire and simmer 5 minutes. Strain into a jug. Serve the chips in a big basket with the gravy for pouring.
M: waiting by the phone for the ransom call

A loaded meat lovers pizza with smoky barbecue base, pepperoni, ham, bacon, Italian sausage and mozzarella, baked until crisp and blistered. Stretch 750g pizza dough into two 30cm rounds on oiled trays. Mix 100ml pizza sauce with 3 tbsp barbecue sauce and spread over the bases. Scatter with 300g grated mozzarella. Top with 100g pepperoni, 100g chopped ham, 3 rashers chopped bacon and 2 Italian sausages, squeezed from the skins in small pieces. Bake at 240C for 12 to 14 minutes until the crust is golden and the meat is crisp.
W: the cookie fortune Miss Crock sits on
Big homemade chocolate chip cookies, the kind that built the Crock family fortune and made her so mean about sharing.
K: Thick vanilla milkshakes blended with crushed chocolate chip cookies, topped with whipped cream and a whole cookie on the rim. Chill 4 tall glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Blend 600ml cold full cream milk, 8 scoops vanilla ice cream and 6 crushed chocolate chip cookies until thick but still a little chunky. Pour into the glasses, top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream and sprinkle with 2 more crushed cookies. Sit a whole cookie on the rim of each glass.
T: Kidnap the dog. Keep the cookies.
D: A fed-up chauffeur and his best mate kidnap his stingy cookie-baron boss's dog, and it goes wrong fast.
P: Serve the cookies when Willard and Rusty hatch the plan.

title: White Christmas
S: Midnight liverwurst on rye and buttermilk
Bob and Betty's midnight snack in the inn kitchen

Rye sandwiches of smooth liverwurst with mustard, pickles and red onion, cut into fingers and served with little glasses of cold buttermilk. Spread 8 slices of rye bread with 30g soft butter and a thin layer of wholegrain mustard. Slice 250g liverwurst or smooth pork pâté and lay it over 4 of the slices. Top with thinly sliced dill pickles and a few rings of red onion, then the other slices of bread. Press down, trim the crusts and cut each sandwich into 4 fingers. Pour 400ml well-chilled buttermilk into 4 small glasses and serve together.
Warm cheddar choux puffs straight from the oven, the kind of welcome snack a country lodge puts out for guests.
M: Roast turkey breast with sage stuffing, cranberry sauce and crisp roast potatoes, a proper country inn Christmas dinner.
W: the snow that finally falls on the inn
White coconut layer cake covered in cream cheese icing and coconut like fresh snow on Christmas Eve.
K: Spiced eggnog with nutmeg, with brandy on the side for the adults.
T: Dreaming of a white Christmas dinner.
D: Two army mates turned song-and-dance stars put on a show to save their old general's struggling Vermont inn.
P: Serve the snacks when the show at the Columbia Inn begins.

title: Holiday Inn
S: Heart-shaped sourdough toasts topped with melted gruyère, sweet tomato chutney and thyme, grilled until golden and bubbling. Cut 8 hearts from 8 slices of sourdough with a heart cutter. Brush both sides with 30g melted butter and toast under the grill for 1 minute a side. Spread each with 1 tsp tomato chutney, then top with 150g grated gruyère and a few thyme leaves. Grill for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling with brown spots. Finish with cracked pepper and serve hot.
the inn's Fourth of July firecracker show

Grilled corn cobs brushed with smoked paprika and chilli butter, rolled in crumbled feta and finished with lime and coriander. Mash 60g soft butter with 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes, 1 crushed garlic clove and a pinch of salt. Grill 4 husked corn cobs over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred in places. Brush the hot cobs all over with the butter, then roll in 80g finely crumbled feta. Scatter with chopped coriander and serve with lime wedges.
M: the cartoon turkey that can't settle on a date

Herb-butter roast turkey breast with buttery mash, sage gravy, garlic green beans and a spoon of cranberry sauce. Mash 60g soft butter with chopped sage, thyme and 1 crushed garlic clove and push it under the skin of a 1.5kg turkey breast. Roast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes, then rest 15 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, add 400ml chicken stock and simmer to a gravy. Blanch 300g green beans and toss with garlic butter. Serve with cranberry sauce.
W: Christmas plum pudding with brandy custard

Rich steamed fruit pudding served hot in wedges with warm brandy custard poured over and a spoon of thick cream. Steam an 800g Christmas pudding in its basin over simmering water for 1 hour, or follow the packet. For the custard, warm 500ml milk and 100ml cream until steaming. Whisk 4 egg yolks with 60g caster sugar and 1 tbsp cornflour, pour in the hot milk while whisking, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it thickens. Stir in 40ml brandy and 1 tsp vanilla. Turn out the pudding and pour over the custard.
K: Connecticut inn hot buttered rum cider
Jim's farmhouse inn, open only on holidays

Warm cloudy apple juice simmered with cinnamon, cloves and orange, finished with a spoon of spiced brown sugar butter and dark rum. Simmer 1.2L cloudy apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 2 strips orange peel and 2 slices fresh ginger for 15 minutes without boiling. Mash 40g soft butter with 2 tbsp brown sugar and a pinch of nutmeg. Strain the cider into 4 mugs, add 30ml dark rum to each and drop in a teaspoon of the spiced butter to melt on top. Leave out the rum for anyone not drinking.
T: Open only on holidays. Dinner every one of them.
D: A singer opens a country inn that only does business on holidays, and his old partner wants his girl.
P: Serve the main when the inn opens for Thanksgiving and the turkey shows up.

title: The Santa Clause 2
S: the elves' workshop at the North Pole
Iced Christmas sugar cookies cut into stars and trees, the kind the elves keep piled up all over the workshop.

A creamy cheddar and cream cheese ball studded with dried cranberries, rolled in toasted walnuts and parsley, with crackers for the party. Beat 250g soft cream cheese with 150g grated vintage cheddar, 60g chopped dried cranberries, 1 tbsp chopped chives and 1/2 tsp garlic powder. Shape into a ball, wrap in cling film and chill for 1 hour until firm. Toast 70g walnuts in a dry pan for 4 minutes, chop finely and mix with 2 tbsp chopped parsley. Roll the ball in the mix until coated. Serve with 200g crackers.
M: Golden roast chicken with herbs, potatoes and carrots, a warm Christmas dinner fit for the future Mrs. Claus.
W: Toy Santa running riot at the North Pole

Fudgy dark chocolate brownies with a layer of peppermint white chocolate and crushed candy canes on top. Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g caster sugar, then 3 eggs, 1/2 tsp peppermint extract and a pinch of salt. Fold in 100g plain flour and 30g cocoa. Spread into a lined 20cm square tin and bake at 170C for 25 minutes until just set. Cool completely. Melt 120g white chocolate and spread over the top, then scatter with 4 crushed candy canes. Chill 20 minutes and cut into 16 squares.
K: the elves' famous North Pole cocoa

Rich hot chocolate made with real dark and milk chocolate and a hint of peppermint, topped with whipped cream and a candy cane to stir. Heat 1L full cream milk with 2 tbsp caster sugar until steaming but not boiling. Whisk in 100g chopped milk chocolate, 50g chopped dark chocolate and 1 tbsp cocoa until smooth and frothy. Stir in 1/4 tsp peppermint extract. Pour into 4 mugs and top each with a big spoon of whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream. Hang a candy cane on each mug to stir.
T: Santa needs a Mrs. And a menu.
D: Scott Calvin has to find a Mrs. Claus before Christmas Eve or stop being Santa for good.
P: Serve the cocoa when Scott takes Carol on their first date.

title: Fred Claus
S: Fred's repo job on the Chicago streets

Beef frankfurts in poppy seed buns dragged through the garden: mustard, green relish, onion, tomato, a pickle spear, peppers and celery salt. Simmer 8 beef frankfurts in water for 5 minutes, then grill 2 minutes for colour. Steam or warm 8 hot dog buns and sprinkle the tops with poppy seeds. Put a frankfurt in each bun. Add a line of yellow mustard and a spoon of green relish, then diced white onion, 2 tomato wedges, a dill pickle spear and 2 pickled peppers. Finish with a pinch of celery salt.

Little gingerbread men with white icing, the kind the elves churn out while Fred upsets the whole workshop. Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar, then mix in 300g self-raising flour and 2 tsp ginger. Roll, cut out men and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Pipe on icing once cool.
M: Claus family honey mustard glazed ham
the Claus family together at Christmas

A leg ham scored and glazed with honey, mustard and orange until sticky and caramelised, served with roast potatoes and buttery greens. Remove the rind from a 2.5kg half leg ham, score the fat in a diamond pattern and stud with cloves. Simmer 120ml honey, 3 tbsp Dijon mustard, 60g brown sugar and the juice of 1 orange for 3 minutes. Bake the ham at 180C for 45 minutes, brushing with glaze every 15 minutes. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in oil alongside. Toss 300g green beans and broccolini in butter. Slice the ham thickly to serve.
W: Mother Claus making sure Nick is well fed

Big chewy brown butter choc chip cookies with crisp edges and a sprinkle of sea salt, served warm with cold milk. Melt 125g butter and cook until golden brown and nutty, then cool 10 minutes. Beat in 150g brown sugar, 50g caster sugar, 1 egg and 1 tsp vanilla. Stir in 220g plain flour, 1/2 tsp bicarb and 150g chopped milk chocolate. Roll into 12 balls and chill 20 minutes. Bake at 180C for 11 minutes until golden at the edges. Sprinkle with sea salt flakes and serve warm with 1L cold milk.
K: Thick milk chocolate hot chocolate topped with marshmallows toasted under the grill until golden, with a dusting of cinnamon. Heat 1L full cream milk until steaming, then whisk in 150g chopped milk chocolate and 1 tbsp cocoa until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 heatproof mugs. Pile 4 large marshmallows on each and place the mugs on a tray under a hot grill for 1 minute, watching closely, until the marshmallows are puffed and golden. Dust with a pinch of cinnamon and serve.
T: Santa's brother brings the snacks.
D: Santa's troublemaking older brother has to help out at the North Pole in the busy week before Christmas.
P: Serve the snacks when Fred arrives at the North Pole.

title: Christmas with the Kranks
S: the Frosty the whole street wants on the Kranks' roof

Two cheese balls of cream cheese and cheddar stacked into a snowman, rolled in grated mozzarella, with olive buttons and a carrot nose. Beat 375g soft cream cheese with 150g grated cheddar, 2 tbsp chopped chives and 1/2 tsp garlic powder. Chill 30 minutes, then shape into one large and one small ball. Roll both in 100g finely grated mozzarella and stack on a platter. Press in sliced black olives for eyes and buttons, a small carrot stick for the nose and 2 pretzel sticks for arms. Chill until serving and surround with 250g crackers.
the Caribbean cruise Luther was saving for

Chilled king prawns on crisp lettuce with a lime and chilli Marie Rose sauce, avocado and a sprinkle of paprika. Peel 600g cooked king prawns, leaving the tails on. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 3 tbsp tomato sauce, the juice of 1 lime, a few drops of hot sauce and 1 tsp Worcestershire. Shred 1 baby cos lettuce into 4 glasses and add a few cubes of avocado. Spoon over the sauce, then hang the prawns around the rims. Dust with paprika and serve with lime wedges.
M: Nora's race for the last ham in town

A smoked leg ham with a sticky honey, brown sugar and pineapple glaze, served with crunchy roast potatoes and a pineapple salsa. Remove the rind from a 2.5kg half leg ham, score the fat and stud with cloves. Simmer 120ml honey, 60g brown sugar, 2 tbsp Dijon mustard and 100ml pineapple juice until syrupy. Bake the ham at 180C for 45 minutes, brushing with glaze every 15 minutes. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in oil alongside. Dice half a pineapple with 1 red chilli, mint and lime juice for the salsa. Slice the ham and serve.
W: the Christmas Eve party thrown together in hours

Sponge soaked in orange juice, layered with raspberry jelly, mixed berries, thick custard and whipped cream, topped with toasted almonds. Make 1 packet raspberry jelly with 500ml boiling water. Break a 300g sponge cake into a large glass bowl and drizzle with 100ml orange juice. Scatter over 250g mixed berries, then pour the cooled jelly over and chill 2 hours until set. Spoon 600ml thick vanilla custard on top. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and spread over. Finish with 30g toasted flaked almonds and a few berries.
K: the whole street pitching in for the party

Cranberry and orange juice with lime, fresh rosemary and ginger ale, poured over ice with frozen cranberries and orange wheels. In a big punch bowl, mix 1L cranberry juice, 500ml orange juice and the juice of 2 limes. Add 2 sprigs rosemary and chill for 30 minutes. Just before serving, add 1L cold ginger ale, 1 sliced orange, 100g frozen cranberries or raspberries and plenty of ice. Stir gently and ladle into glasses with a little rosemary in each.
T: Skipping Christmas? Not with this ham.
D: A couple try to skip Christmas for a cruise until their daughter says she is coming home after all.
P: Serve the main when Nora finally gets her hands on the last ham.

title: The Night Before
S: Christmas Eve on the streets of New York

Toasted mini bagels spread with chive cream cheese, topped with smoked salmon, capers, red onion and fresh dill. Split 12 mini bagels and toast until golden. Beat 200g cream cheese with 2 tbsp chopped chives and a squeeze of lemon. Spread thickly on each bagel half. Top with a ribbon of smoked salmon from 200g, a few capers, a sliver of red onion and a sprig of dill. Finish with cracked black pepper and serve on a board with lemon wedges.
Nutcracka hunt hot honey buffalo wings
the long night hunting for the Nutcracka Ball

Crisp oven-baked wings tossed in buttery hot sauce with a cool ranch dip, carrot and celery sticks. Pat 1.2kg chicken wings dry and toss with 2 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt. Bake on a rack at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 100ml hot sauce and 1 tbsp honey, then toss the wings through. For the ranch, mix 100g sour cream, 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 3 tbsp buttermilk, chopped chives and dill and garlic powder. Serve with carrot and celery sticks.
M: Little beef sliders and mac and cheese cups, the kind of party food you would hope to find at the most famous party in town.
W: the end of the night with the three friends
Soft sticky gingerbread cake with lemon icing, something sweet for when the night finally winds down.
K: a cold New York Christmas Eve

Red wine gently warmed with orange, cinnamon, star anise and cloves, sweetened with honey and served steaming in mugs with an orange slice. Pour 750ml red wine into a saucepan with 250ml orange juice, 3 tbsp honey, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 star anise, 6 cloves and 1 sliced orange. Heat gently for 15 minutes, keeping it below a simmer so the alcohol stays. Ladle into 4 mugs with an orange slice each. For anyone not drinking, warm sparkling apple juice with the same spices.
T: Christmas Eve, one last time.
D: Three lifelong friends spend one last wild Christmas Eve in New York hunting for a legendary party.
P: Serve the snacks when they head out into New York on Christmas Eve.

title: Office Christmas Party
S: Office party beef and onion sausage rolls
the catering table at the office party

Flaky sausage rolls of beef and pork mince with caramelised onion and thyme, glazed with egg and sesame and served with tomato relish. Fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes until golden, then cool. Mix 300g beef mince and 200g pork mince with the onions, 1 tsp thyme, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 egg and salt. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each, roll and seal. Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with sesame and cut each into 4. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 200g tomato relish.
Clay throwing one party to save the branch

A whole camembert baked with garlic, rosemary and honey until oozing, on a board with crusty bread, grapes and fig jam. Unwrap a 250g camembert, sit it back in its wooden box or a small dish and cut slits in the top. Push in slivers of 1 garlic clove and small rosemary sprigs and drizzle with 1 tbsp honey. Bake at 180C for 15 minutes until soft in the middle. Slice 1 baguette, brush with oil and toast 8 minutes. Serve the cheese hot on a board with the toasts, 300g grapes and 4 tbsp fig jam.
M: the Zenotek branch party that gets out of control

Little beef patties with melted cheddar, pickles, caramelised onion and burger sauce in soft brioche slider buns, eaten with one hand. Slowly fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp mustard and 1 tbsp chopped pickles. Roll 600g beef mince into 12 balls, smash flat in a very hot oiled pan, season and cook 2 minutes. Flip, add half a cheese slice each and cook 1 minute. Toast 12 brioche slider buns and fill with sauce, patty, onions and pickles.
W: Vanilla cupcakes with red and green buttercream, the Christmas colours the office goes all in on.
K: the CEO sister out to close the branch

Homemade cooked eggnog with vanilla, cinnamon and fresh nutmeg, chilled and spiked with dark rum and brandy for the adults. Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g caster sugar. Heat 600ml milk, 200ml cream, 1 cinnamon stick and 1 tsp vanilla until steaming. Slowly whisk into the yolks, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon, about 5 minutes. Strain and chill 2 hours. Stir in 60ml dark rum and 60ml brandy, or serve those on the side. Pour into glasses and grate fresh nutmeg over the top.
T: The party that saves the branch.
D: A branch manager throws an epic office Christmas party to save his staff from being sacked.
P: Serve the snacks when the party gets out of hand.

title: The Grinch
S: Grinch green spinach and herb dip
the Grinch himself, green and grumpy

A bright green dip of spinach, avocado, Greek yoghurt and fresh herbs, served with crunchy pita chips and cucumber sticks. Blanch 100g baby spinach in boiling water for 20 seconds, drain and squeeze dry. Blitz with 1 avocado, 200g Greek yoghurt, a handful each of basil and parsley, 1 small garlic clove, the juice of 1 lemon and salt until smooth and very green. Cut 4 pita breads into wedges, brush with oil and bake at 190C for 8 minutes until crisp. Serve the dip with the pita chips and cucumber sticks.
the Grinch's cave up on Mount Crumpit

A crusty cob loaf cut into a grid and stuffed with garlic butter, mozzarella and chives, baked until gooey for pulling apart. Cut a 500g cob loaf in a criss-cross pattern every 2cm, without cutting through the base. Melt 80g butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves and 2 tbsp chopped chives. Spoon the butter into the cuts, then stuff with 200g grated mozzarella and 40g grated parmesan. Wrap in foil and bake at 180C for 15 minutes, then unwrap and bake 10 minutes more until golden and melted. Pull apart at the table.
M: Whoville roast beast with crispy potatoes

Garlic and herb crusted roast beef carved at the table, with crunchy duck fat potatoes, honey roast carrots and a rich red gravy. Rub a 1.5kg beef sirloin roast with 2 crushed garlic cloves, chopped rosemary, oil and salt. Parboil 1.2kg quartered potatoes for 8 minutes, drain, rough up and toss in 3 tbsp duck fat. Roast the potatoes at 200C for 50 minutes and the beef for 50 minutes for medium rare, adding 4 carrots tossed in honey for the last 35. Rest the beef 15 minutes. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices with 400ml beef stock to make gravy.
W: the Who pudding the whole town sits down to

Warm steamed Christmas pudding in wedges with vanilla custard, a scoop of vanilla ice cream and a sprinkle of red and green sprinkles. Steam an 800g Christmas pudding in its basin over simmering water for 1 hour, or follow the packet. Warm 500ml milk and 100ml cream. Whisk 4 egg yolks with 60g caster sugar and 1 tbsp cornflour, pour in the hot milk while whisking, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until thick. Add 1 tsp vanilla. Turn out the pudding, cut into wedges and serve with custard, ice cream and a few Christmas sprinkles.
K: Max running the Grinch's morning brew

Frothy hot chocolate made with real chocolate, topped with whipped cream, green sprinkles and a dusting of cocoa. Heat 1L full cream milk with 1 tbsp caster sugar until steaming. Whisk in 150g chopped milk chocolate and 1 tbsp cocoa until melted and frothy, or blitz with a stick blender for extra froth. Pour into 4 mugs. Whip 150ml thickened cream with 1 tsp icing sugar, spoon on top and finish with green sprinkles and a little cocoa dusted over.
T: Roast beast for everyone.
D: The Grinch plans to steal Christmas from Whoville after the town decides to make it three times bigger.
P: Serve the main when the Grinch sits down at the Whos' table.

title: A Christmas Carol
S: Fezziwig's ball pork and sage rolls

Little puff pastry sausage rolls filled with pork, sage and apple, glazed golden and served warm with a sharp mustard and apple chutney. Mix 500g pork mince with 1 grated apple, 1 grated onion, 2 tbsp chopped sage, 40g breadcrumbs, salt and pepper. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry in half. Lay a log of filling along each strip, roll and seal underneath. Brush with 1 beaten egg and cut each into 5 small rolls. Bake at 200C for 22 minutes until golden. Serve warm with 150g apple chutney stirred with 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard.
the snowy streets of Victorian London

Hot roasted chestnuts tossed in nutty brown butter, rosemary and sea salt, served in paper cones like a London street stall. Cut a cross through the shell on the flat side of 600g fresh chestnuts. Soak in water for 10 minutes, then drain. Roast on a tray at 200C for 20 to 25 minutes until the shells peel back. Wrap in a tea towel for 5 minutes, then peel while warm. Melt 40g butter until golden brown and nutty, add a sprig of chopped rosemary and toss the chestnuts through with sea salt. Serve in paper cones.
M: Scrooge's prize turkey with sage stuffing
the prize turkey Scrooge sends to the Cratchits

Butter-roasted turkey breast with sage and onion stuffing, apple sauce, roast potatoes and a rich gravy, a feast for the Cratchits. Rub a 1.5kg turkey breast with 40g butter, salt and pepper and roast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Mix 150g breadcrumbs, 1 diced onion fried in 30g butter, 2 tbsp chopped sage and 1 egg, press into a dish and bake for the last 30 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes in oil alongside. Simmer 3 peeled diced apples with 2 tbsp sugar and water until soft. Make gravy from the pan juices with 1 tbsp flour and 400ml stock.
W: A rich steamed fruit pudding with a sprig of holly on top, served in wedges with thick homemade custard and brandy butter cream. Steam an 800g Christmas pudding over simmering water for 1 hour, or follow the packet. Warm 500ml milk with 100ml cream. Whisk 4 egg yolks, 60g caster sugar and 1 tbsp cornflour, pour in the milk while whisking, return to the pan and stir until thick. Add 1 tsp vanilla. Whip 200ml cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and 1 tsp orange zest. Turn out the pudding, top with a holly sprig and serve with both.
K: Scrooge promising Bob a bowl of smoking bishop

An alcohol-free take on Dickens's hot punch: roasted clove-studded oranges warmed with red grape juice, cinnamon and honey. Stud 2 oranges with 6 cloves each and roast at 200C for 20 minutes until browned. Slice them into a saucepan with 1L red grape juice, 250ml apple juice, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 tbsp honey and 3 slices fresh ginger. Heat gently for 15 minutes without boiling. Ladle into heatproof glasses or mugs with an orange slice in each.
T: Bah humbug. Pass the goose.
D: Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve in this motion-capture take on the Dickens story.
P: Serve the main when Scrooge sends the prize turkey to the Cratchits.

title: Krampus
S: Omi's pretzels with obatzda cheese dip
Omi, the only one who knows what is coming

Warm salted soft pretzels with obatzda, a punchy Bavarian dip of camembert, butter, paprika, caraway and beer, plus pickles for crunch. Roll 500g pizza dough into 8 ropes and twist into pretzels. Dip each in 2L simmering water with 60g bicarb for 30 seconds. Brush with egg, sprinkle with sea salt flakes and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Mash 200g ripe camembert with 50g soft butter, 50g cream cheese, 2 tbsp lager, 1 tsp sweet paprika, 1/2 tsp caraway seeds and finely diced red onion. Serve the pretzels warm with the dip and cornichons.

Deeply caramelised onion dip with sour cream and chives, topped with crispy fried shallots and served with kettle chips. Slowly cook 3 thinly sliced brown onions in 30g butter and 1 tbsp oil over low heat for 35 minutes until jammy and deep brown. Add 1 tsp Worcestershire and a splash of water and scrape the pan, then cool. Mix with 250g sour cream, 100g cream cheese, 2 tbsp chopped chives and salt. Chill 30 minutes. Top with 3 tbsp crispy fried shallots and more chives and serve with 200g kettle chips.
M: the tense family dinner before the storm
Beef lasagne with a bubbling cheesy top, comfort food for the night before everything goes wrong.
W: Krampus gingerbread men with jagged grins
the gingerbread men that come to life

Dark, spicy gingerbread men with a pinch of chilli, piped with jagged white icing grins and red eyes, crisp at the edges and chewy inside. Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g dark brown sugar. Mix in 300g plain flour, 1 tsp bicarb, 2 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp chilli powder and 1 egg to a soft dough. Chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm, cut gingerbread men and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool. Mix 150g icing sugar with 1 tbsp water and pipe jagged teeth, then add red eyes with a little tinted icing.
K: a freezing night snowed in with the power out

Red wine and cloudy apple juice warmed with cinnamon, cloves, star anise and orange, served steaming in mugs. Plain spiced apple for non-drinkers. Pour 750ml red wine and 500ml cloudy apple juice into a saucepan. Add 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 2 star anise and 1 sliced orange. Heat gently for 15 minutes without letting it simmer. Ladle into mugs with an orange slice each. For non-drinkers, warm 1L apple juice with the same spices in a second pan.
T: Gingerbread with teeth.
D: A family Christmas goes so badly that a young boy's lost spirit summons the dark shadow of St. Nicholas.
P: Serve the gingerbread when the gingerbread men come to life.

title: Violent Night
S: Gertrude Lightstone's Christmas Eve at the mansion

Warm blinis with crème fraîche, hot-smoked salmon, glistening salmon roe, chives and lemon, rich-family canapés with a pop of brine. Warm 16 cocktail blinis on a tray at 180C for 4 minutes. Mix 150g crème fraîche with the zest of 1 lemon and a pinch of salt. Flake 150g hot-smoked salmon. Top each blini with a spoon of crème fraîche, a few flakes of salmon and 1/2 tsp salmon roe from a 50g jar. Finish with snipped chives and cracked pepper and serve with lemon wedges.
Santa working through cookie plates house to house

Crumbly brown butter shortbread fingers with flaky salt, half dipped in dark chocolate and scattered with crushed candy cane. Melt 250g butter and cook until golden brown and nutty, then chill until firm but soft. Beat with 110g caster sugar, then mix in 300g plain flour, 60g cornflour and a pinch of salt. Press into a lined 20 x 30cm tin, prick with a fork and bake at 160C for 35 minutes. Cut into 20 fingers while warm and cool. Dip one end in 150g melted dark chocolate and sprinkle with crushed candy cane and sea salt.
M: A garlic and pepper crusted beef rib roast, cooked pink, with crisp duck fat potatoes, red wine jus and a sharp horseradish cream. Rub a 2kg beef rib roast with 3 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp cracked pepper, oil and salt. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 50 minutes for medium rare. Rest 20 minutes. Parboil 1.2kg potatoes, rough up, toss in 3 tbsp duck fat and roast 50 minutes. Simmer the pan juices with 200ml red wine and 300ml beef stock until reduced by half. Mix 150g sour cream with 2 tbsp horseradish cream and lemon.
W: Chocolate cake soaked in cherry syrup, layered with dark cherries, chocolate custard and whipped cream, finished with shaved dark chocolate. Drain a 680g jar pitted cherries, keeping the syrup. Break a 400g chocolate cake into a glass bowl and drizzle with 100ml of the syrup. Scatter over the cherries. Whisk 2 tbsp cocoa into 600ml thick vanilla custard and pour over. Chill 1 hour. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla, spread on top, then shave 50g dark chocolate over with a peeler.
K: Santa drinking at the pub before his shift

A cold pint of rich stout with a shot of whisky on the side, plus a spiced cola and lime for anyone not drinking. Chill 4 pint glasses. Pour 440ml cold stout into each glass at an angle, then straighten up to build a creamy head and let it settle for a minute before topping up. Pour 30ml whisky into 4 shot glasses and serve alongside. For non-drinkers, fill glasses with ice, add a squeeze of lime and 2 dashes of bitters and top with cola.
T: Santa's had a few. Dinner's still on.
D: A worn-out Santa has to save a rich family when mercenaries take over their mansion on Christmas Eve.
P: Serve the drinks when Santa stops at the pub.

title: Noelle
S: Chipotle chicken thigh tacos with charred corn, cotija-style feta, pickled red onion, lime crema and coriander in warm corn tortillas. Slice 1 red onion and soak in the juice of 2 limes with a pinch of salt and sugar. Toss 600g chicken thigh with 1 tbsp chipotle sauce, 1 tsp cumin and 1 tbsp oil and grill 5 minutes a side, then slice. Char 2 corn cobs and cut off the kernels. Mix 150g sour cream with lime juice. Warm 12 small corn tortillas and fill with chicken, corn, crumbled feta, crema, onion and coriander.
the North Pole, home of the candy canes

Layers of dark and white chocolate swirled together with peppermint, crushed candy canes and a pinch of sea salt, snapped into shards. Line a tray with baking paper. Melt 200g dark chocolate and spread into a 25 x 30cm rectangle. Chill 10 minutes. Melt 200g white chocolate with 1/4 tsp peppermint extract and spread over the dark layer, then drag a skewer through to swirl. Scatter with 5 crushed candy canes and a pinch of sea salt flakes. Chill 30 minutes until set and snap into shards.
M: the Kringle family Christmas once Nick is home

Golden roast chicken glazed with maple, mustard and thyme, with crispy potatoes, honey roasted carrots and a rich pan gravy. Rub a 1.8kg chicken with 40g soft butter, salt and thyme leaves. Roast at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes, brushing with 3 tbsp maple syrup mixed with 1 tbsp Dijon for the last 20 minutes. Toss 1kg halved potatoes in oil and roast alongside for 50 minutes, adding 4 carrots tossed in 1 tbsp honey for the last 35. Rest the chicken 10 minutes. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices with 350ml chicken stock for gravy.
W: Elf Polly keeping the North Pole in line

Vanilla butter sugar cookies cut into stars, trees and reindeer, iced in red, green and white with a little edible glitter. Beat 200g butter with 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk and 1 tsp vanilla, then mix in 300g plain flour. Chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm, cut out stars, trees and reindeer and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Cool. Mix 250g icing sugar with 2 to 3 tbsp water, divide into 3 bowls and tint red and green, leaving one white. Ice the cookies and dust with edible glitter.
K: A bright icy slushie of frozen raspberries, lemon and blue cordial blended with lemonade, topped with a puff of whipped cream for desert Christmas. Blend 150g frozen raspberries, the juice of 2 lemons, 80ml blue raspberry cordial and 3 cups ice until slushy. Add 600ml cold lemonade and pulse twice to mix. Pour into 4 cups. Top each with a little whipped cream from 100ml thickened cream and a few freeze-dried or fresh raspberries. Serve with spoons and straws.
T: Santa's daughter takes the sleigh.
D: Santa's daughter heads to Phoenix to find her brother, who has run off before Christmas.
P: Serve the snacks when Noelle lands in Phoenix.

title: Last Christmas
S: Covent Garden cevapi rolls with ajvar
Kate's family roots and the Covent Garden markets

Charred Balkan beef and lamb cevapi in soft rolls with smoky red capsicum ajvar, sour cream, raw onion and parsley. Mix 300g beef mince, 200g lamb mince, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp sweet paprika, 1/2 tsp bicarb and 1 tsp salt and knead 2 minutes. Roll into 16 short fingers and chill 30 minutes. Grill over high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until charred. Split 4 soft rolls and toast. Spread with 4 tbsp ajvar, add 4 cevapi each and top with sour cream, finely diced onion and parsley.
Santa's shop mince pies with orange cream

Buttery little mince pies with star lids, warmed and dusted with icing sugar, served with orange zest and brandy whipped cream. Cut 12 rounds from 2 sheets shortcrust pastry and press into a greased patty pan tin. Fill each with 1 heaped tbsp fruit mince from a 400g jar. Cut 12 stars from a third sheet and lay on top. Brush with beaten egg and bake at 190C for 18 minutes until golden. Whip 200ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar, the zest of 1 orange and 1 tbsp brandy. Dust the pies with icing sugar and serve warm.
M: Kate's mum Petra and the family table

Red capsicums stuffed with paprika-spiced beef and rice, baked in a rich tomato sauce and served with garlic yoghurt and crusty bread. Fry 1 diced onion and 2 garlic cloves, add 500g beef mince and brown. Stir in 100g long grain rice, 2 tsp sweet paprika, 1 tsp smoked paprika, salt and 150ml water and cook 5 minutes. Cut the tops off 4 large red capsicums, remove the seeds and fill. Stand in a dish, pour around 700g passata mixed with 200ml water and bake covered at 180C for 50 minutes. Mix 200g Greek yoghurt with 1 crushed garlic clove.
W: the Christmas shop where Kate works as an elf

Soft spiced gingerbread biscuits with golden syrup and orange zest, iced with lemon glaze in snowflakes and little stars. Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar. Mix in 300g self-raising flour, 2 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon, the zest of 1 orange and 1 egg. Chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm, cut into stars and snowflakes and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool. Mix 150g icing sugar with the juice of half a lemon and pipe on snowflake patterns.
K: Red wine slowly warmed with orange, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and a little brown sugar, served steaming with an orange wheel. Pour 750ml red wine into a saucepan with 200ml orange juice, 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 2 star anise and 1 sliced orange. Warm gently for 15 minutes, keeping it under a simmer. Ladle into heatproof glasses with an orange wheel. For anyone not drinking, warm 1L cloudy apple juice with the same spices.
T: One more Christmas in London.
D: A struggling London actress working as an elf in a year-round Christmas shop meets someone who changes everything.
P: Serve the sweets when Kate clocks on at the Christmas shop.

title: The Holdovers
S: Mary's grilled cheese and tomato soup
Mary Lamb's school kitchen at Barton

Golden grilled cheese of vintage cheddar and mozzarella on buttered sourdough, cut into fingers for dunking in a smoky tomato soup. Fry 1 diced onion and 2 garlic cloves in 2 tbsp olive oil for 5 minutes. Add 2 x 400g tins crushed tomatoes, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp sugar and 300ml chicken stock and simmer 15 minutes, then blitz smooth and stir in 50ml cream. Butter 8 slices sourdough on the outside and fill with 150g cheddar and 100g mozzarella. Fry over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden. Cut into fingers.
the trip into Boston over the break

Creamy New England clam chowder with smoky bacon, potato, thyme and fresh clams, served in mugs with oyster crackers. Fry 3 diced rashers bacon until crisp, add 1 onion and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml fish stock, 300g diced potato and a few thyme sprigs and simmer 12 minutes. Add 1kg cleaned clams, cover and cook 4 minutes until open, then remove the shells. Stir in 300ml cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers.
M: Christmas for the three left behind at Barton

Roast chicken with bread and herb stuffing, crunchy roast potatoes, glazed carrots and gravy, a small Christmas dinner done properly. Fry 1 diced onion in 40g butter, mix with 150g fresh breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp chopped sage, the zest of 1 lemon and 1 egg, and stuff a 1.8kg chicken. Rub with butter and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in oil for 50 minutes. Glaze 4 carrots with 20g butter and 1 tbsp honey. Rest the chicken, then make gravy from the juices with 1 tbsp flour and 350ml stock.
W: the cherries jubilee at the restaurant

Dark cherries simmered in a buttery orange and brandy sauce, flamed at the table and spooned hot over vanilla ice cream. Drain a 680g jar pitted cherries, keeping 150ml syrup. Melt 30g butter with 60g brown sugar in a wide pan, add the syrup and the zest and juice of 1 orange and simmer 3 minutes. Stir in 1 tsp cornflour mixed with water, then add the cherries and warm through. Off the heat, pour in 60ml brandy, then carefully light it with a long match and let the flames die down. Spoon over 1L vanilla ice cream.
K: the bottle Mr Hunham keeps close

Bourbon with hot water, honey, lemon and a cinnamon stick, a warming nightcap for a New England winter. Plain honey lemon for non-drinkers. Boil 800ml water. In each of 4 heatproof mugs, put 1 tbsp honey, the juice of half a lemon, 45ml bourbon and a cinnamon stick. Top each with 200ml hot water and stir until the honey dissolves. Stud a lemon slice with 3 cloves and float it on top. Leave out the bourbon for anyone not drinking.
T: Stuck at school for Christmas.
D: A grumpy teacher, a grieving cook and a troubled student are stuck at a New England boarding school over Christmas 1970.
P: Serve dessert when Mr Hunham orders the cherries jubilee.

title: Red One
S: MORA command centre loaded potato skins
the North Pole security operation hunting for Santa

Crispy twice-baked potato skins loaded with cheddar, bacon and spring onion, topped with sour cream, pickled jalapeño and hot honey. Prick 6 medium potatoes and bake at 200C for 1 hour. Halve, scoop out most of the flesh and brush the skins inside and out with 30g melted butter and salt. Bake skin-side up for 10 minutes, then flip. Fill with 150g grated cheddar and 4 rashers chopped cooked bacon and bake 8 minutes until melted. Top with 150g sour cream, sliced spring onion, pickled jalapeños and a drizzle of 2 tbsp honey mixed with 1 tsp chilli flakes.
the elves on the North Pole security detail

Maple-glazed pecans and almonds roasted with pretzels and cinnamon, tossed with dark chocolate chunks and dried cranberries. Toss 150g pecans and 100g almonds with 3 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tsp cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Spread on a lined tray with 100g mini pretzels and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring once. Cool completely so the glaze crisps. Toss with 100g chopped dark chocolate and 80g dried cranberries and tip into a big bowl.
M: Red One's training day steak plate
Santa training hard for the big night

Chargrilled rump with chimichurri, smoky sweet potato wedges and charred broccolini, a high protein dinner for a very fit Santa. Cut 2 large sweet potatoes into wedges, toss with 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp smoked paprika and salt, and roast at 220C for 30 minutes. Blitz 1 bunch parsley, 2 garlic cloves, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes, 3 tbsp red wine vinegar and 100ml olive oil. Season 800g rump steak and grill over high heat for 4 minutes a side, then rest 5 minutes and slice. Grill 2 bunches broccolini for 4 minutes. Spoon chimichurri over the steak.
W: getting Red One back in time for Christmas Eve

Soft, fudgy red velvet cookies rolled in icing sugar so they crack as they bake, with white chocolate chunks inside. Beat 115g soft butter with 150g caster sugar, then add 1 egg, 1 tbsp milk, 1 tsp vanilla and 1 tsp red colouring paste. Mix in 200g plain flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, 1 tsp baking powder and a pinch of salt, then fold in 100g chopped white chocolate. Chill 1 hour. Roll into 16 balls, roll each in 60g icing sugar and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool on the tray.
K: Callum Drift on the cold night search for Santa

Dark hot chocolate with cinnamon, a pinch of chilli and vanilla, topped with whipped cream and grated chocolate. Heat 1L full cream milk with 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 cinnamon stick and a pinch of chilli powder until steaming. Remove the cinnamon and whisk in 100g chopped dark chocolate, 50g milk chocolate and 1 tsp vanilla until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 mugs and top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream and a little grated chocolate.
T: Find Santa. Then dinner.
D: After Santa is kidnapped, the head of North Pole security teams up with a hacker to get him back.
P: Serve the snacks when the search for Santa begins.

title: The Christmas Chronicles
S: Stakeout salted caramel choc chip cookies
Kate setting up the camera to catch Santa

Chewy brown sugar cookies loaded with milk chocolate and pockets of salted caramel, left on the plate as bait for Santa. Beat 125g soft butter with 150g brown sugar, 50g caster sugar, 1 egg and 1 tsp vanilla. Mix in 220g plain flour, 1/2 tsp bicarb and 120g chopped milk chocolate. Roll into 12 balls, press a soft caramel into the centre of each from a 100g bag and close the dough around it. Chill 20 minutes. Bake at 180C for 11 minutes, sprinkle with sea salt flakes and cool on the tray.

Thin-sliced roast beef dipped in garlic oregano jus and piled into soft slider buns with mild pickled vegetables and a cup of jus for dunking. Simmer 500ml beef stock with 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp Worcestershire for 10 minutes. Drop in 400g thinly sliced deli roast beef for 1 minute to warm through. Split 8 slider buns and dip the cut sides quickly in the jus. Pile in the beef and top with 150g chopped mild pickled vegetables. Serve with little cups of jus for dunking.
M: the Pierce family's first Christmas without Dad

Juicy beef meatloaf wrapped in streaky bacon and glazed with sticky tomato and brown sugar, served with creamy mash and gravy. Mix 800g beef mince with 1 grated onion, 1 egg, 60g breadcrumbs soaked in 80ml milk, 2 tsp Worcestershire and salt. Shape into a loaf on a lined tray and wrap with 8 rashers streaky bacon. Bake at 180C for 45 minutes, brush with 4 tbsp tomato sauce mixed with 1 tbsp brown sugar and bake 15 minutes more. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and milk. Make gravy from the tray juices with 1 tbsp flour and 300ml beef stock.
W: the wild sleigh ride across the sky

Vanilla butter cookies cut into reindeer and stars, iced white with a red nose here and there and a scatter of gold sprinkles. Beat 200g butter with 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk and 1 tsp vanilla, then mix in 300g plain flour. Chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm, cut reindeer and stars and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Cool. Mix 250g icing sugar with 2 to 3 tbsp water. Ice the cookies white, tint a little red for noses and finish with gold sprinkles.
K: Sleigh ride salted caramel hot chocolate

Rich milk chocolate hot chocolate stirred with salted caramel, topped with whipped cream, a caramel drizzle and toasted marshmallows. Heat 1L full cream milk until steaming, then whisk in 120g chopped milk chocolate and 4 tbsp salted caramel sauce until smooth. Pour into 4 heatproof mugs. Top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream, drizzle with more caramel and add 2 marshmallows each, browned quickly with a kitchen torch or under the grill.
T: Catch Santa. Save Christmas.
D: Two kids trying to catch Santa on camera crash his sleigh and have to help him save Christmas.
P: Serve the cookies when the kids set up the camera to catch Santa.

title: Jack Frost
S: Snow day toastie fingers with tomato soup
Charlie's snow days in the Colorado mountains

Golden ham, cheddar and mustard toasties cut into fingers for dunking into little cups of creamy tomato soup. Fry 1 diced onion in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, add 2 x 400g tins crushed tomatoes, 300ml chicken stock and 1 tsp sugar and simmer 15 minutes. Blitz smooth and stir in 50ml cream. Spread 8 slices bread with mustard and make 4 sandwiches with 150g ham and 150g grated cheddar. Butter the outsides and fry 3 minutes a side until golden. Cut into fingers and serve with cups of soup.

Smoky frankfurts in soft pretzel buns with sweet fried onions, mild mustard, crunchy pickles and a little shredded cheddar. Slowly fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes until golden. Simmer 8 frankfurts in water for 5 minutes, then grill 2 minutes for colour. Warm 8 pretzel buns or soft rolls in the oven for 4 minutes. Split, add a frankfurt to each, then top with the onions, a squeeze of American mustard, sliced pickles and 80g grated cheddar.
M: Frost family roast beef and Yorkshires
the family Christmas Jack finally gets to share

Herb-crusted roast beef with puffed Yorkshire puddings, crunchy roast potatoes, honey carrots and a jug of rich gravy. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with mustard, rosemary and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour for medium rare, with 1.2kg parboiled potatoes in oil on another tray. Rest 15 minutes. Turn the oven to 220C. Whisk 2 eggs, 100g plain flour and 150ml milk. Heat 1 tsp oil in each of 8 muffin holes for 5 minutes, pour in the batter and bake 20 minutes without opening. Make gravy from the juices with 1 tbsp flour and 400ml stock.
W: Jack coming back as a snowman

Light vanilla cupcakes with fluffy white buttercream rolled in coconut, with chocolate chip eyes and a little orange lolly nose. Beat 125g butter and 150g caster sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 120ml milk. Divide between 12 cases and bake at 180C for 18 minutes. Cool. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla until fluffy and white. Dome onto each cupcake and roll in 80g desiccated coconut. Press in 2 chocolate chips for eyes and a small orange lolly for a nose.
K: the magic harmonica that brings Jack back

Creamy white hot chocolate with vanilla and a hint of cinnamon, topped with whipped cream and a snowfall of desiccated coconut. Heat 1L full cream milk with 1 cinnamon stick until steaming. Remove the cinnamon and whisk in 150g chopped white chocolate and 1 tsp vanilla until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 mugs, top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream and sprinkle with 2 tbsp desiccated coconut so it looks like fresh snow.
T: Dad's back. He's a snowman.
D: A dad who missed too much of his son's life comes back as a snowman for one last Christmas.
P: Serve the snacks when the snowman comes to life.

title: Deck the Halls
S: Buddy's house lit up bright enough to see from space

Red cherry tomatoes, white bocconcini and green basil threaded on skewers like a string of Christmas lights, with balsamic glaze and basil oil. Blitz a handful of basil leaves with 60ml olive oil and a pinch of salt, then strain. Halve 24 baby bocconcini. Thread 24 skewers with a cherry tomato, a basil leaf and a bocconcini half, then another tomato, from 250g cherry tomatoes. Lay them in rows on a long platter like strings of lights. Drizzle with the basil oil and balsamic glaze and finish with cracked pepper and sea salt.

Little pork and beef meatballs baked golden and tossed in a sticky cranberry, chilli and soy glaze, served on toothpicks. Mix 300g beef mince, 200g pork mince, 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 crushed garlic clove and salt. Roll into 24 balls and bake on a lined tray at 200C for 15 minutes. Simmer 200g cranberry sauce, 3 tbsp sweet chilli sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp lemon juice for 3 minutes until glossy. Toss the meatballs through, scatter with sliced spring onion and serve on toothpicks.
M: Steve and Buddy's families at Christmas

Roast turkey breast with a sticky cranberry and orange glaze, sage stuffing, roast potatoes and buttery green beans. Rub a 1.5kg turkey breast with 40g butter and salt and roast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Simmer 150g cranberry sauce with the juice of 1 orange and 1 tbsp honey and brush over for the last 20 minutes. Mix 150g breadcrumbs, 1 fried diced onion, 2 tbsp chopped sage, 1 egg and 30g melted butter and bake in a dish for 30 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes in oil. Toss 300g green beans in butter.
W: the two families finally celebrating together

Sponge soaked in orange juice with strawberry jelly, mixed berries, thick custard and whipped cream, topped with crushed honeycomb. Make 1 packet strawberry jelly with 500ml boiling water and cool. Break a 300g sponge cake into a glass bowl and drizzle with 100ml orange juice. Add 250g mixed berries and pour over the jelly. Chill 2 hours until set. Spoon over 600ml thick vanilla custard. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and spread on top. Scatter with 40g crushed honeycomb just before serving.
K: Steve and Buddy making up as neighbours

Creamy homemade eggnog with vanilla, cinnamon and fresh nutmeg, cooked gently and served chilled. Alcohol-free for the whole street. Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g caster sugar. Heat 700ml milk, 200ml cream, 1 cinnamon stick and 1 tsp vanilla until steaming. Slowly whisk into the yolks, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon, about 5 minutes. Strain and chill 2 hours. Pour into 4 glasses and grate fresh nutmeg over the top.
T: Lights out. Snacks on.
D: Two neighbours go to war over a house full of Christmas lights bright enough to be seen from space.
P: Serve the snacks when the lights go on.

title: Nativity!
S: the staffroom at St Bernadette's at Christmas

Buttery mince pies with crumbly star lids, dusted with icing sugar and served warm with orange-scented whipped cream. Cut 12 rounds from 2 sheets shortcrust pastry and press into a greased patty pan tin. Fill each with 1 heaped tbsp fruit mince from a 400g jar. Cut 12 stars from a third sheet and lay on top. Brush with beaten egg and bake at 190C for 18 minutes until golden. Whip 200ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and the zest of 1 orange. Dust the pies with icing sugar and serve warm with the cream.
Christmas fair pork and apple rolls
the school Christmas fair bake sale

Golden puff pastry rolls of pork, apple and sage, glazed with egg and sprinkled with seeds, with a tangy tomato relish for dipping. Mix 500g pork sausage mince with 1 grated apple, 1 grated onion, 2 tbsp chopped sage and 30g breadcrumbs. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each and roll up, sealing underneath. Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with 1 tbsp sesame seeds and cut each into 4. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Serve with 200g tomato relish.
M: Roast chicken with pigs in blankets, crunchy roast potatoes, maple-glazed Brussels sprouts with bacon and plenty of gravy. Rub a 1.8kg chicken with butter and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes. Wrap 12 chipolatas in half rashers of streaky bacon and add for the last 30 minutes. Roast 1kg parboiled potatoes in oil for 50 minutes. Halve 400g Brussels sprouts and fry with 2 diced rashers bacon for 6 minutes, then toss with 1 tbsp maple syrup. Make gravy from the pan juices with 1 tbsp flour and 350ml chicken stock.
W: Mr Poppy, the classroom assistant who is a big kid
