Warm crumbled Christmas pudding layered with vanilla ice cream, custard, toffee sauce and crushed honeycomb in tall sundae glasses. Warm an 800g Christmas pudding in the microwave or steamer as the packet says, then break half of it into chunks. Warm 300ml thick vanilla custard. In 4 sundae glasses, layer pudding chunks, a scoop of vanilla ice cream, a spoon of custard and a drizzle of toffee sauce, then repeat. Finish with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream and 40g crushed honeycomb.
K: a cold December night at the school nativity

Blackcurrant cordial warmed with cloudy apple juice, cinnamon, orange and ginger, served steaming in mugs for the kids. Pour 1L cloudy apple juice and 400ml water into a saucepan with 150ml blackcurrant cordial, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 cloves, 2 slices fresh ginger and 1 sliced orange. Heat gently for 10 minutes without boiling. Strain into 4 mugs and add an orange slice to each.
T: The school nativity, Hollywood style.
D: A primary school teacher accidentally promises that Hollywood is coming to see his school's nativity play.
P: Serve the sweets when the nativity play starts.

title: Miracle on 34th Street
S: the Thanksgiving Day parade in New York

Fluffy hot donut holes rolled in cinnamon sugar, served in paper bags with a little pot of warm chocolate sauce for dunking. Mix 250g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar, 1 egg, 150ml milk and 30g melted butter into a soft dough. Roll into 24 balls and fry at 175C for 3 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Drain and toss in 100g caster sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon. Heat 100ml cream and pour over 100g chopped dark chocolate, stirring until smooth, for dunking.
the line to see Kriss Kringle at Cole's

Soft spiced gingerbread cut into Santas, stars and toy soldiers, iced in white and red, the treats handed out in Santa's line. Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar. Mix in 300g self-raising flour, 2 tsp ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 egg. Chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm, cut out shapes and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool. Mix 200g icing sugar with 2 tbsp water, tint a third red, and pipe on outlines and details.
M: Herb-butter roast turkey breast with cornbread stuffing, creamy mash, gravy and a bright cranberry orange relish. Push 60g herb butter under the skin of a 1.5kg turkey breast and roast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Crumble 300g cornbread with 1 fried onion, 2 celery sticks, 2 tbsp sage, 1 egg and 150ml stock and bake 30 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and milk. Simmer 150g cranberry sauce with orange zest. Make gravy from the juices with 1 tbsp flour and 300ml stock.
W: New York pumpkin pie with maple cream

Silky spiced pumpkin pie in a crisp pastry shell, topped with maple whipped cream and toasted pecans. Line a 23cm pie dish with 1 sheet shortcrust pastry and bake blind at 190C for 12 minutes. Steam 600g peeled pumpkin until soft, drain well and mash smooth. Beat with 150g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 200ml cream, 2 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp ginger and a pinch of nutmeg. Pour into the case and bake at 170C for 45 minutes until just set. Cool. Whip 200ml cream with 2 tbsp maple syrup and serve with toasted pecans.
K: a cold New York night after the parade

Cloudy apple juice simmered with cinnamon, cloves, star anise, orange and a little maple, served steaming with a cinnamon stick. Pour 1.2L cloudy apple juice into a saucepan with 2 tbsp maple syrup, 4 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 2 star anise and 1 sliced orange. Heat gently for 15 minutes without boiling so the spices infuse. Strain into 4 mugs and add a cinnamon stick and an orange slice to each.
T: Believe in Santa. Believe in dinner.
D: A department store Santa claims he is the real thing, and a court case decides it.
P: Serve the snacks after the Thanksgiving parade.

title: Hop
S: Milk chocolate rocky road packed with marshmallows, jellybeans, crunchy pretzels and coconut, cut into chunky squares. Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Melt 400g milk chocolate with 20g butter in a bowl over simmering water. Cool for 5 minutes. Stir in 100g mini marshmallows, 100g jellybeans, 60g broken pretzels and 30g shredded coconut. Spread into the tin, press another handful of jellybeans on top and chill for 2 hours until set. Cut into 16 squares with a hot knife.
Rainbow carrots with green goddess dip

Rainbow baby carrots and snow peas with a bright green herb, avocado and yoghurt dip and a sprinkle of toasted seeds. Trim 2 bunches rainbow baby carrots, leaving a little green top, and halve any big ones lengthways. Blanch 150g snow peas for 30 seconds and cool in iced water. Blitz 1 avocado, 150g Greek yoghurt, a handful each of basil, parsley and chives, the juice of 1 lemon and salt until smooth. Spoon into a bowl, scatter with 1 tbsp toasted sunflower seeds and serve with the vegetables.
M: Fred O'Hare's Hollywood loaded hot dogs
E.B. and Fred's adventure in Hollywood

Grilled frankfurts in toasted buns loaded with cheesy sauce, crispy fried onions, sweet corn relish and a squeeze of tomato sauce. Simmer 8 frankfurts for 5 minutes, then grill 2 minutes until marked. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp flour, whisk in 200ml milk and simmer until thick, then stir in 100g grated cheddar. Mix 200g drained corn kernels with 2 tbsp tomato relish. Toast 8 hot dog buns and fill with frankfurts, cheese sauce, corn relish and tomato sauce, then top with 4 tbsp crispy fried onions.
W: the candy factory on Easter Island

Crunchy milk chocolate and cornflake nests filled with mini speckled eggs, with a little fluffy chick on top of a few. Melt 200g milk chocolate with 30g butter and 1 tbsp golden syrup. Stir in 80g cornflakes until coated. Spoon into 12 paper cases in a muffin tin, pressing a dip in the centre of each with the back of a teaspoon. Chill for 1 hour until set. Fill each nest with 3 mini chocolate eggs from a 150g bag and add a little decoration chick to a few.
K: Freshly juiced carrot and orange with a touch of ginger, poured over ice with a splash of raspberry cordial sinking to the bottom like a sunrise. Juice 6 carrots, 4 oranges and a 2cm piece of ginger, or blend with 200ml water and strain through a sieve. Chill for 20 minutes. Fill 4 glasses with ice and pour in the juice. Slowly pour 1 tbsp raspberry cordial down the inside of each glass so it sinks to the bottom. Garnish with an orange wheel.
T: The Easter Bunny's son wants to drum.
D: The Easter Bunny's son runs away to Hollywood to be a drummer instead of taking over the family business.
P: Serve the sweets when the Easter Island candy factory comes into view.

title: Peter Rabbit
S: the radishes Peter pinches from Mr. McGregor's garden

Crisp breakfast radishes with whipped salted butter, flaky sea salt and chives for dragging through, plus warm crusty bread. Wash and trim 2 bunches radishes, leaving a little stem on, and halve the bigger ones. Keep in iced water for 15 minutes so they crunch. Whip 120g soft salted butter with an electric beater for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy. Spread the butter in a dish, sprinkle with sea salt flakes and snipped chives. Serve with the drained radishes and a warmed baguette.
Cottontail's garden crudités with herb dip
Peter, Benjamin and the girls raiding the garden

Baby carrots, snow peas, cucumber and little lettuce cups with a cool, garlicky yoghurt and dill dip for the young raiders. Trim 1 bunch baby carrots and 150g snow peas. Cut 1 Lebanese cucumber into batons and separate 2 baby cos lettuces into small leaves. Mix 250g Greek yoghurt with 1 small crushed garlic clove, 2 tbsp chopped dill, 1 tbsp chopped mint, the zest of 1 lemon and a pinch of salt. Arrange the vegetables around the bowl of dip on a big board.
M: Mr. McGregor's vegetable garden in the Lake District

Leek, carrot, potato and pea in a cheddar and mustard sauce under golden puff pastry, a pie straight out of the garden. Boil 500g diced potato and 2 diced carrots for 8 minutes and drain. Fry 2 sliced leeks in 40g butter for 6 minutes, stir in 3 tbsp plain flour, then whisk in 500ml milk and simmer until thick. Stir in 120g grated cheddar, 1 tsp Dijon, the vegetables and 150g peas. Tip into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.
W: Peter's blackberry attack on Thomas McGregor

Jammy blackberries and apple under a crunchy oat and brown sugar crumble, served warm with thick vanilla custard. Toss 500g blackberries, fresh or frozen, with 2 peeled diced apples, 60g caster sugar and 1 tbsp cornflour and tip into a baking dish. Rub 100g cold butter into 100g plain flour, then stir in 60g rolled oats and 80g brown sugar. Scatter over the fruit. Bake at 180C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve warm with 600ml vanilla custard.
K: Mrs. Rabbit's chamomile apple iced tea
the chamomile tea from the Peter Rabbit stories

Chamomile tea brewed with honey, chilled and mixed with apple juice and lemon, poured over ice with apple slices and mint. Steep 4 chamomile tea bags in 600ml boiling water with 2 tbsp honey for 5 minutes. Remove the bags and cool, then chill for 1 hour. Stir in 400ml cold apple juice and the juice of 1 lemon. Fill 4 glasses with ice and thin apple slices, pour over the tea and add a mint sprig to each.
T: Raid the garden.
D: Peter Rabbit and his family battle the new Mr. McGregor for the vegetable garden and a neighbour's affection.
P: Serve the snacks when Peter raids the garden.

title: Big Daddy
S: Sonny taking Julian out to the sports bar

Sticky smoky barbecue wings with a sweet heat glaze, scattered with spring onion and served with a cool ranch dip. Toss 1.2kg chicken wings with 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika and salt. Bake on a rack at 220C for 40 minutes, turning once. Simmer 200ml barbecue sauce with 2 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp hot sauce for 3 minutes and toss the wings through, then bake 5 minutes more. Mix 100g sour cream, 3 tbsp mayonnaise, chopped chives and garlic powder for the ranch. Scatter wings with spring onion.

Toasted mini bagels with whipped scallion cream cheese, crisp bacon and a sprinkle of homemade everything seasoning. Mix 1 tbsp sesame seeds, 1 tsp poppy seeds, 1 tsp dried onion flakes, 1/2 tsp garlic flakes and 1/2 tsp sea salt. Beat 200g cream cheese with 2 sliced spring onions until fluffy. Grill 4 rashers bacon until crisp and crumble. Split and toast 12 mini bagels. Spread with the cream cheese, top with bacon and sprinkle with the seasoning.
M: Sonny's one day a week at the tollbooth

Smashed beef patties with melted cheese in toasted buns, with a build-your-own bar of pickles, bacon, onion rings, sauces and crinkle fries. Bake 800g frozen crinkle-cut chips and 300g frozen onion rings at 220C for 25 minutes. Grill 6 rashers bacon. Roll 800g beef mince into 8 balls, smash flat in a very hot oiled pan, season and cook 2 minutes. Flip, top with cheese and cook 1 minute. Toast 4 buns. Set out lettuce, tomato, pickles, bacon, onion rings, tomato sauce, mustard and mayonnaise and let everyone build their own.
W: Julian and his favourite toy, Scuba Steve

Vanilla ice cream with blue jelly cubes, whipped cream, crushed biscuit sand, gummy fish and chocolate sauce, an under-the-sea sundae. Make 1 packet blue jelly with 500ml boiling water, set in a shallow dish for 3 hours and cut into cubes. Crush 6 plain sweet biscuits into sand. In 4 tall glasses, layer jelly cubes, 2 scoops vanilla ice cream and more jelly. Top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream, a sprinkle of biscuit sand, a few gummy fish and a drizzle of chocolate sauce.
K: Julian, who wants to be called Frankenstein

Thick chocolate malt milkshakes with ice cream, whipped cream and a drizzle of chocolate sauce, served with striped straws. Chill 4 glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes and drizzle chocolate sauce down the insides. Blend 600ml cold milk, 6 scoops vanilla ice cream, 4 tbsp chocolate malt powder and 2 tbsp cocoa until thick. Pour into the glasses, top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream and sprinkle with a little more malt powder.
T: Adopt a kid. Feed him whatever he wants.
D: A lazy New Yorker adopts a five-year-old to win back his girlfriend and makes up the parenting rules as he goes.
P: Serve the wings when Sonny takes Julian out to the sports bar.

title: Valentine's Day
S: Fresh strawberries dipped in dark chocolate, rolled in crushed pistachios and freeze-dried raspberry, then drizzled with white chocolate. Wash and dry 500g strawberries completely, keeping the stalks on. Melt 150g dark chocolate in a bowl over simmering water. Dip each berry two-thirds of the way in, let the excess drip off and roll the base in 50g finely chopped pistachios. Lay on baking paper. Melt 50g white chocolate and drizzle over with a fork, then dust with a pinch of crushed freeze-dried raspberry. Chill 20 minutes until set.
Reed's flower shop goat's cheese toasts
Reed's flower shop on the busiest day of the year

Heart-shaped sourdough toasts with whipped goat's cheese, hot honey, thyme and edible flowers, pretty enough for the shop counter. Cut 8 hearts from 8 slices sourdough, brush with olive oil and toast at 190C for 8 minutes until crisp. Whip 150g soft goat's cheese with 50g cream cheese until smooth. Warm 3 tbsp honey with 1/2 tsp chilli flakes. Spread the toasts with the cheese, drizzle with hot honey, scatter with thyme leaves and finish with a few edible flowers or pomegranate seeds.
M: Pan-seared sirloin basted in garlic thyme butter, with crispy smashed potatoes, buttered greens and a red wine jus. Boil 800g baby potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, smash flat on a tray, drizzle with oil and roast at 220C for 30 minutes. Season 4 sirloin steaks and sear in a hot pan for 3 minutes a side. Add 50g butter, 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme and baste for 1 minute. Rest the steaks. Add 150ml red wine and 150ml beef stock to the pan and reduce by half. Sauté 300g green beans in butter.
W: Soft red velvet cupcakes with a hint of cocoa and buttermilk, topped with tangy cream cheese icing and red velvet crumbs. Beat 115g butter with 200g caster sugar, add 2 eggs, then 1 tsp vanilla and 1 tsp red colouring paste. Fold in 200g plain flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, 1 tsp bicarb and 160ml buttermilk mixed with 1 tsp vinegar. Divide between 12 cases and bake at 180C for 20 minutes. Cool. Beat 200g cream cheese, 60g butter and 250g icing sugar and pipe on. Crumble one cupcake over the rest.
K: Kara's I Hate Valentine's Day party

Sparkling rosé with fresh raspberries, a splash of pink grapefruit and a rosemary sprig. Pink lemonade with the same garnish for non-drinkers. Drop 3 raspberries into each of 4 flutes. Add 30ml pink grapefruit juice to each glass. Slowly top with chilled sparkling rosé, about 120ml per glass. Rub a small rosemary sprig between your hands and add one to each glass. For anyone not drinking, use pink lemonade instead of rosé.
T: Love is in the air. So is dinner.
D: One busy Valentine's Day in Los Angeles follows a florist and a big tangle of couples falling in and out of love.
P: Serve dessert when Reed's flower shop closes for the night.

title: Mother's Day
S: the classic Mother's Day breakfast in bed

Day-old croissants soaked in vanilla syrup, filled and topped with almond cream and flaked almonds, baked golden and dusted with icing sugar. Simmer 100g caster sugar with 100ml water and 1 tsp vanilla for 2 minutes. Beat 80g soft butter, 80g caster sugar, 1 egg and 100g almond meal into a paste. Split 4 croissants, brush the insides with syrup and spread with half the almond cream. Close, spread the rest on top and scatter with 30g flaked almonds. Bake at 180C for 15 minutes. Dust with icing sugar and serve with jam.

Southern pimento cheese of sharp cheddar, roasted red capsicum, mayonnaise and cayenne, served with crackers, celery and pickled okra or cornichons. Finely grate 200g vintage cheddar. Mix with 100g mayonnaise, 80g chopped roasted red capsicum from a jar, 1 tsp Worcestershire, a pinch of cayenne and black pepper until combined but still chunky. Chill 30 minutes. Spoon into a bowl, dust with paprika and serve with 200g crackers, celery sticks and a few cornichons.
M: Mother's Day ham and spinach frittata
the big family Mother's Day lunch

A thick oven-baked frittata of ham, spinach, potato and feta, served in wedges with a lemony rocket salad and tomato relish. Boil 300g diced potato for 8 minutes and drain. Fry 1 sliced onion in 1 tbsp oil in a 26cm ovenproof pan for 5 minutes, add the potato, 150g diced ham and 100g baby spinach and stir until wilted. Whisk 8 eggs with 100ml cream and salt, pour over and scatter with 100g crumbled feta. Cook on low for 5 minutes, then bake at 180C for 15 minutes until set. Serve with rocket dressed in lemon and relish.
W: a sweet thank you to Mum

Fluffy buttery shortcake biscuits split and filled with vanilla whipped cream and balsamic macerated strawberries. Slice 300g strawberries and toss with 1 tbsp caster sugar and 1 tsp balsamic vinegar and leave 20 minutes. Rub 80g cold butter into 250g self-raising flour and 2 tbsp sugar, add 150ml milk and pat out to 2cm. Cut 6 rounds, brush with milk and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Whip 300ml cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla. Split the shortcakes and fill with cream and strawberries.
K: Chilled sparkling wine topped with fresh blood orange juice and a splash of orange liqueur. Blood orange and soda for the kids. Juice 6 blood oranges or regular oranges and strain. Pour 60ml juice and 10ml orange liqueur into each of 4 flutes. Slowly top with chilled sparkling wine, about 100ml per glass. Garnish with a thin orange wheel on the rim. For the kids, mix the rest of the juice with soda water.
T: For every kind of mum.
D: A handful of Atlanta families, each with its own mum drama, collide in the days before Mother's Day.
P: Serve breakfast in bed food when Mother's Day finally arrives.

title: New Year's Eve
S: Laura's prawn and avocado tostada bites
Laura catering Jensen's big New Year's Eve party

Crisp mini tortilla rounds with smashed avocado, chilli lime prawns, pickled onion and coriander, the kind of bite a chef sends out first. Cut 16 rounds from 4 corn tortillas with a 6cm cutter, brush with oil and bake at 200C for 8 minutes until crisp. Toss 16 peeled cooked prawns with the juice of 1 lime and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes. Mash 2 avocados with lime juice and salt. Thinly slice half a red onion and soak in lime juice for 10 minutes. Top each crisp with avocado, a prawn, a few onion slivers and a coriander leaf.
Times Square halal cart chicken skewers
the street carts around Times Square

Cumin and turmeric marinated chicken skewers, chargrilled and drizzled with garlicky white sauce and red chilli sauce on warm pita. Toss 600g diced chicken thigh with 2 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 crushed garlic clove and salt. Marinate 30 minutes, thread onto 8 skewers and grill 10 minutes, turning. Mix 100g mayonnaise, 100g Greek yoghurt, 1 tsp white vinegar, 1 crushed garlic clove and a pinch of sugar. Warm 4 pita breads. Serve skewers on pita with white sauce, hot chilli sauce and shredded lettuce.
M: a big New York night out before the ball drops

Linguine tossed with garlic butter king prawns, chilli, white wine, lemon and parsley, finished with toasted breadcrumbs for crunch. Cook 400g linguine in salted water. Toast 40g panko in 1 tbsp oil until golden. Heat 40g butter and 2 tbsp oil, add 4 sliced garlic cloves and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes for 1 minute, then add 600g peeled green prawns and cook 2 minutes. Add 100ml white wine and bubble 1 minute. Toss in the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water, the zest and juice of 1 lemon and chopped parsley. Top with the crumbs.
W: Paul ticking off Ingrid's list before midnight

Warm dark chocolate fondue with a hint of orange, for dunking strawberries, marshmallows, brownie cubes and pretzels as the clock runs down. Heat 200ml thickened cream until steaming. Pour over 200g chopped dark chocolate, leave 1 minute, then stir until glossy. Stir in the zest of 1 orange and a pinch of salt. Keep warm in a fondue pot or a bowl over hot water. Serve with 250g strawberries, 100g marshmallows, a 300g brownie cut into cubes and a handful of pretzels on skewers.
K: the ball stuck halfway up the pole

Gin, fresh lemon and sugar syrup shaken cold and topped with champagne, with a long lemon twist. Chill 4 flutes. For each drink, shake 30ml gin, 15ml lemon juice and 10ml sugar syrup with ice and strain into a flute. Top slowly with about 90ml chilled champagne or sparkling wine. Add a long twist of lemon peel. For anyone not drinking, mix lemon juice and syrup with sparkling white grape juice.
T: Ten, nine, eight, dinner.
D: A mess of New Yorkers chase love and second chances in the hours before the ball drops in Times Square.
P: Serve the drinks as the ball drops at midnight.

title: Time Bandits
S: King Agamemnon's feast in ancient Greece

Whipped feta with honey and oregano, marinated olives, cucumber, cherry tomatoes and warm pita, a Greek spread fit for a king. Blitz 200g feta with 100g Greek yoghurt and 2 tbsp olive oil until smooth. Spread in a shallow bowl, drizzle with 1 tbsp honey and sprinkle with dried oregano. Cut 1 Lebanese cucumber into batons and halve 250g cherry tomatoes. Warm 4 pita breads, brush with oil and cut into wedges. Arrange everything on a big platter with 150g kalamata olives.
Robin Hood and his merry men

Crusty bread with sharp cheddar, leg ham, crisp apple, pickled onions and a sticky homemade apple and onion chutney. Simmer 1 diced apple, 1 diced onion, 3 tbsp brown sugar, 3 tbsp cider vinegar and a pinch of mixed spice for 20 minutes until thick and sticky, then cool. Slice 1 crusty loaf. Cut 200g vintage cheddar into wedges and 2 apples into slices. Arrange on a board with 150g sliced leg ham, a few pickled onions and the chutney.
M: Winston the ogre's beef and barley stew
Winston the ogre and his wife cooking on their ship

A big pot of slow-braised beef with barley, carrots and mushrooms in a rich gravy, served with crusty bread and horseradish butter. Toss 1kg diced chuck steak in 2 tbsp flour and brown in batches in oil. Add 1 diced onion, 2 carrots, 200g mushrooms and 2 garlic cloves and cook 5 minutes. Add 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1.2L beef stock, 100g pearl barley and 2 bay leaves. Simmer covered for 2 hours until the beef is tender. Mash 60g butter with 1 tbsp horseradish cream and serve with a crusty loaf.
W: Tiny flaky custard tarts with caramelised tops and a dusting of cinnamon, small enough to please a general obsessed with little things. Roll 1 sheet puff pastry into a tight log and cut into 12 rounds. Press each into a greased mini muffin tin. Whisk 3 egg yolks, 80g caster sugar, 1 tbsp cornflour, 250ml milk and 1 tsp vanilla in a pan and stir over medium heat until thick. Spoon into the cases. Bake at 230C for 12 to 15 minutes until the tops blister. Cool and dust with cinnamon.
K: the bandits' stop aboard the Titanic

Homemade fresh ginger and lemon syrup topped with soda over a big block of ice, with mint and lemon. Alcohol-free. Simmer 100g caster sugar, 100ml water and a 5cm piece of sliced ginger for 5 minutes, then cool and strain. Freeze water in a small container to make 4 big ice blocks, or use large ice cubes. Put a block in each glass, add 30ml ginger syrup and the juice of half a lemon, then top with 200ml soda water. Garnish with mint and a lemon wheel.
T: Steal through time. Stop for dinner.
D: A boy joins a gang of time-travelling thieves on a wild run through history with a stolen map of holes in time.
P: Serve the main when the boys reach Agamemnon's feast.

title: About Time
S: Cornish beach crab and cress sandwiches
the family's tea on the beach in Cornwall

Soft white bread with lemony crab mayonnaise, fresh cress and cucumber, crusts off and cut into fingers for a windy Cornish beach. Mix 250g crab meat with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, the zest and juice of half a lemon, a pinch of cayenne and salt. Butter 8 slices of soft white bread. Spread the crab over 4 slices, add thin cucumber slices and a handful of cress, then close. Press gently, trim the crusts and cut each sandwich into 3 fingers.

Little crimped pasties of diced beef, potato, swede and onion with plenty of pepper, baked golden and served with brown sauce. Mix 300g finely diced rump, 1 small diced potato, 100g finely diced swede, 1 diced onion, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp cracked pepper. Cut 8 rounds from 4 sheets shortcrust pastry. Spoon filling onto one half of each, add a small knob of butter, fold over and crimp the edge. Brush with beaten egg, cut a small slit and bake at 190C for 35 minutes until golden. Serve with brown sauce.
M: Tim and Mary meeting at the restaurant in the dark

Lamb shanks braised in red wine, rosemary and tomato until falling off the bone, over buttery mash, a dish you could eat with your eyes shut. Brown 4 lamb shanks in 2 tbsp oil. Add 1 diced onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks and 3 garlic cloves and cook 5 minutes. Add 250ml red wine, 400g tin crushed tomatoes, 500ml beef stock, 2 rosemary sprigs and 2 bay leaves. Cover and braise at 160C for 2 hours 30 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Reduce the sauce and spoon over.
W: Tim and Mary's wedding in the storm

Crushed meringue, strawberries and passionfruit folded through vanilla whipped cream, an English dessert that is meant to look a mess. Slice 400g strawberries and toss with 1 tbsp caster sugar and the pulp of 2 passionfruit. Leave 15 minutes. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 1 tsp vanilla to soft peaks. Roughly break 6 meringue nests. Gently fold the meringue, most of the strawberries and their juices through the cream so it streaks. Spoon into 4 glasses and top with the rest of the berries.
K: Dad's ping pong Earl Grey iced tea
Tim and his dad's games of ping pong

Earl Grey brewed strong with honey, chilled and poured over ice with lemon and a splash of soda for a bit of fizz. Steep 5 Earl Grey tea bags in 800ml boiling water with 3 tbsp honey for 5 minutes. Remove the bags, cool, then chill for 1 hour. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice and lemon slices. Pour in the tea to three-quarters full and top each with a splash of soda water. Garnish with a lemon wheel.
T: Go back. Stay for dinner.
D: A young man finds out the men in his family can travel back in time and uses it to find love and make the most of life.
P: Serve the main when Tim and Mary meet at the dinner in the dark.

title: Muppet Treasure Island
S: the Admiral Benbow Inn where Jim works

Little chipolatas roasted in a sticky honey and wholegrain mustard glaze, sprinkled with thyme and served on toothpicks. Twist 20 chipolatas in half to make 40 little sausages and snip apart. Roast on a lined tray at 200C for 15 minutes. Mix 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp wholegrain mustard and 1 tsp soy sauce. Pour over the sausages, toss and roast 8 minutes more until sticky and glazed. Scatter with thyme leaves and serve on toothpicks.

Homemade crunchy cheddar and pepper crackers, served with sliced apple and pickled onions like sea rations from the ship's stores. Rub 80g cold butter into 150g plain flour, then stir in 120g grated vintage cheddar, 1/2 tsp cracked pepper and a pinch of salt. Add 2 tbsp cold water and press into a dough. Chill 20 minutes. Roll to 3mm, cut into 5cm squares, prick with a fork and bake at 180C for 14 minutes until golden. Cool. Serve with 2 sliced apples and a few pickled onions.
M: Long John Silver's galley fish stew
Long John Silver, the ship's cook

Chunks of white fish and prawns in a smoky tomato, potato and paprika broth, served with garlic toast for dunking. Fry 1 diced onion, 1 diced capsicum and 2 garlic cloves in 2 tbsp oil for 5 minutes. Add 1 tsp smoked paprika, 400g tin crushed tomatoes, 500ml fish stock and 400g diced potatoes and simmer 15 minutes. Add 500g firm white fish chunks and 200g peeled green prawns and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in parsley. Rub toasted sourdough with garlic and serve alongside.
W: the buried treasure on the island

Fudgy brownies dusted with cocoa sand and piled with gold-wrapped chocolate coins and gold sprinkles, a treasure chest in every square. Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g caster sugar, then 3 eggs. Fold in 100g plain flour and 30g cocoa. Spread into a lined 20cm square tin and bake at 170C for 25 minutes until just set. Cool, then crush 4 plain biscuits and sprinkle over like sand. Cut into 16 squares and top each with a gold chocolate coin and gold sprinkles.
K: Captain Smollett's crew on the Hispaniola

Spicy ginger beer with fresh lime, orange and a splash of pineapple juice over ice, a rum-free grog for the whole crew. In a jug, mix 1L cold ginger beer, 300ml pineapple juice, the juice of 2 limes and the juice of 1 orange. Fill 4 tall glasses or tin mugs with ice and pour over. Garnish with lime wedges and orange slices.
T: Shiver me timbers. Pass the stew.
D: Young Jim Hawkins and his Muppet friends sail off with a treasure map and a ship's cook named Long John Silver.
P: Serve the main when Long John Silver cooks in the ship's galley.

title: The Blind Side
S: Wings rubbed with smoked paprika, brown sugar and garlic, baked crisp and served with a tangy mustard barbecue sauce. Mix 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp cayenne and 2 tsp salt. Toss 1.2kg chicken wings with 2 tsp baking powder and the rub. Bake on a rack at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once. Mix 150ml barbecue sauce with 2 tbsp American mustard and 1 tbsp cider vinegar for dipping.

Southern devilled eggs with a creamy mustard and pickle filling, topped with crisp bacon, smoked paprika and chives. Cook 8 eggs in boiling water for 10 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Halve and scoop the yolks into a bowl. Mash with 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp American mustard, 1 tbsp finely chopped pickles and salt. Pipe back into the whites. Grill 3 rashers bacon until crisp and crumble. Top the eggs with bacon, a dusting of smoked paprika and chives.
M: Tuohy Thanksgiving turkey at the table
the Thanksgiving Michael eats at the table

Herb roast turkey breast with cornbread stuffing, creamy mash, buttery green beans, gravy and cranberry sauce. Push 60g herb butter under the skin of a 1.5kg turkey breast and roast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Crumble 300g cornbread with 1 fried onion, 2 celery sticks, chopped sage, 1 egg and 150ml stock and bake 30 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with butter and milk. Blanch 300g green beans and toss in butter. Make gravy from the juices with 1 tbsp flour and 300ml stock. Serve with cranberry sauce.
W: the story Leigh Anne reads at bedtime

A sticky golden syrup and brown sugar pecan pie in a crisp pastry case, served warm with vanilla ice cream. Line a 23cm pie dish with 1 sheet shortcrust pastry and bake blind at 190C for 12 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs, 150g brown sugar, 150ml golden syrup, 50g melted butter, 1 tsp vanilla and a pinch of salt. Stir in 200g pecans. Pour into the case and bake at 170C for 40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Cool 1 hour and serve with ice cream.
K: a Memphis afternoon with the Tuohys

Black tea brewed strong and sweet, chilled with peach and lemon and poured over ice with fresh mint. Steep 6 black tea bags in 1L boiling water with 120g sugar for 5 minutes. Remove the bags, cool and chill. Stir in 300ml peach nectar and the juice of 1 lemon. Fill 4 glasses with ice and peach slices, pour over the tea and finish with mint sprigs and lemon wheels.
T: Everyone at the table.
D: A Memphis family takes in a homeless teenager who goes on to become a star football player.
P: Serve the main when Leigh Anne switches off the football and gets everyone to the table.

title: The Farewell
S: the family making dumplings around Nai Nai's table

Pork, cabbage and ginger dumplings pan-fried until crisp on the bottom, with a black vinegar, soy and chilli oil dipping sauce. Salt 200g finely chopped wombok for 10 minutes and squeeze dry. Mix with 400g pork mince, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 sliced spring onions, 2 tbsp soy and 1 tsp sesame oil. Fill 30 round dumpling wrappers, wet the edges and pleat closed. Fry in 2 tbsp oil for 2 minutes until golden underneath, add 100ml water, cover and steam 6 minutes until dry. Mix 3 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp soy and 1 tbsp chilli oil for dipping.
Changchun smashed cucumber with chilli oil

Cold smashed cucumbers in a punchy dressing of garlic, black vinegar, soy and chilli oil, topped with toasted sesame and coriander. Lay 4 Lebanese cucumbers on a board and smash with the flat of a knife until they split, then cut into bite-size chunks. Toss with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp sugar and drain in a sieve for 15 minutes. Mix 3 crushed garlic cloves, 2 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil and 2 tbsp chilli oil. Toss the cucumbers in the dressing and top with toasted sesame seeds and coriander.
M: Wedding banquet crispy sweet and sour pork
Hao Hao's wedding banquet for Nai Nai

Northeast Chinese style crispy pork in a glossy tangy sauce with capsicum, pineapple and carrot, served with steamed jasmine rice. Cut 600g pork scotch fillet into thin slices, season and toss in 1 egg white, then in 100g potato starch. Fry at 180C for 3 minutes, rest, then fry again for 1 minute until very crisp. Stir-fry 1 capsicum, 1 julienned carrot, 2 garlic cloves and 150g pineapple chunks for 2 minutes. Add 4 tbsp rice vinegar, 4 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tbsp soy and 1 tsp cornflour in 60ml water and bubble until glossy. Toss in the pork and serve with 300g rice.
W: the sweet course at the wedding banquet

Chewy glutinous rice balls filled with sweet red bean paste, rolled in sesame seeds and fried until puffed, golden and crisp. Mix 250g glutinous rice flour with 60g caster sugar, then stir in about 200ml hot water and knead to a smooth, soft dough. Divide into 16 balls. Flatten each, fill with 1 tsp red bean paste from a 200g tin and roll closed. Wet lightly and roll in 80g white sesame seeds. Fry in oil at 160C for 6 to 8 minutes, pressing gently against the side of the pot so they puff, until golden.
K: Nai Nai's iced jasmine lychee tea
Nai Nai's tea at the family table

Fragrant jasmine tea brewed gently, chilled with lychee syrup and lime and served over ice with whole lychees. Steep 4 jasmine tea bags in 1L water just off the boil for 3 minutes, then remove the bags and cool. Drain a 565g tin of lychees, keeping 150ml syrup. Stir the syrup and the juice of 1 lime into the tea and chill. Fill 4 glasses with ice and a few lychees and pour over the tea.
T: A family secret and a wedding banquet.
D: A Chinese-American woman travels to China, where her family has organised a fake wedding to say goodbye to their grandmother.
P: Serve the main at the wedding banquet.

title: Easter Sunday
S: Long, thin Filipino spring rolls packed with pork, carrot and garlic, fried shatteringly crisp with sweet chilli and spiced vinegar for dipping. Mix 500g pork mince, 1 grated carrot, 1 finely diced onion, 3 crushed garlic cloves, 2 sliced spring onions, 1 egg, 1 tbsp soy and pepper. Lay 2 tbsp of filling along the edge of each of 20 spring roll wrappers in a thin line and roll up tightly, sealing with water. Fry at 180C for 4 minutes until deep golden. Mix 100ml white vinegar with 1 crushed garlic clove, chilli and pepper. Serve with the vinegar and sweet chilli sauce.

Stir-fried rice noodles with chicken, Chinese sausage, cabbage, carrot and snow peas in soy and oyster sauce, with lime wedges to squeeze. Soak 250g rice vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes and drain. Stir-fry 300g sliced chicken thigh and 1 sliced Chinese sausage in 2 tbsp oil for 4 minutes. Add 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves, 2 cups shredded cabbage, 1 julienned carrot and 100g snow peas for 2 minutes. Add 250ml chicken stock, 3 tbsp soy and 2 tbsp oyster sauce, then the noodles, and toss until absorbed. Serve with lime or calamansi wedges and spring onion.
M: Joe's mum and the family Easter lunch

Chicken thighs braised in vinegar, soy, garlic, bay and black pepper until sticky and glossy, served with garlic fried rice and a fried egg. Brown 1kg bone-in chicken thighs in 1 tbsp oil. Add 8 crushed garlic cloves, 120ml white vinegar, 80ml soy, 3 bay leaves, 1 tsp black peppercorns and 200ml water. Simmer uncovered for 40 minutes, turning, until the sauce is sticky. Fry 600g cold cooked rice with 4 crushed garlic cloves in 2 tbsp oil until crisp in spots. Fry 4 eggs. Serve the adobo over the rice with an egg on top.
W: the aunties' dessert table at the Easter party

Rich, silky Filipino caramel custard made with egg yolks and condensed milk, baked slowly and turned out with a pool of dark caramel. Melt 150g caster sugar in a pan until deep amber and pour into a 20cm dish, tilting to coat. Whisk 6 egg yolks with a 395g tin condensed milk, a 370ml tin evaporated milk and 1 tsp vanilla without making bubbles, then strain over the caramel. Cover with foil and bake in a water bath at 160C for 50 minutes until just set. Cool, chill overnight, then turn out onto a plate.
K: A tangy calamansi and lime cooler sweetened with honey and topped with soda water over crushed ice. Use lime and mandarin if calamansi is hard to find. Stir 4 tbsp honey into 4 tbsp hot water until dissolved. Squeeze 150ml calamansi juice, or use the juice of 3 limes and 1 mandarin. Mix the juice and honey syrup in a jug and chill. Fill 4 glasses with crushed ice, add the juice and top with 800ml cold soda water. Garnish with lime wheels.
T: Easter with the whole Filipino family.
D: A struggling comedian heads home for a chaotic Filipino-American family Easter with his mum and aunties.
P: Serve the main when the whole family sits down for Easter lunch.

title: The Family Stone
S: Christmas Eve at the Stone family house

Chipolatas wrapped in streaky bacon and roasted until crisp and sticky, with a cranberry mustard dip for the family to fight over. Wrap 20 chipolatas in half rashers of streaky bacon from 10 rashers. Lay on a lined tray and roast at 200C for 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Brush with 2 tbsp maple syrup for the last 5 minutes. Mix 150g cranberry sauce with 2 tbsp wholegrain mustard for dipping and serve hot on toothpicks.
the family dinner where everyone talks over each other

A soft bread loaf scored and stuffed with garlic, parsley and parmesan butter, baked until crusty and passed around to tear apart. Cut a 500g crusty loaf in deep diagonal slices every 2cm, without cutting through the base. Mash 100g soft butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves, 3 tbsp chopped parsley and 30g grated parmesan. Push the butter into every cut. Wrap in foil and bake at 190C for 15 minutes, then open the foil and bake 8 minutes more until crisp and golden.
M: Meredith's strata that ends up on the floor

A baked layered bread and egg pudding with ham, gruyère, spinach and Dijon, puffed and golden on top, ideally kept off the floor. Butter a 2L baking dish. Layer 6 thick slices of day-old bread, torn, with 200g diced ham, 100g wilted baby spinach and 150g grated gruyère. Whisk 6 eggs with 500ml milk, 1 tbsp Dijon, salt and pepper and pour over. Press down, cover and chill for at least 2 hours or overnight. Bake at 180C for 45 minutes until puffed and golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with tomato relish.
W: Christmas morning at the Stone house

Soft brioche-style scrolls rolled with brown sugar, cinnamon and butter, baked golden and smothered in tangy cream cheese icing. Roll 500g pizza dough into a 30 x 40cm rectangle. Spread with 60g soft butter, then sprinkle with 80g brown sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon. Roll up from the long side and cut into 12 scrolls. Pack into a greased 24cm tin, cover and rest 30 minutes. Bake at 190C for 22 minutes. Beat 120g cream cheese, 30g butter, 150g icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla and spread over the warm scrolls.
K: Strong coffee topped with steamed spiced eggnog milk and grated nutmeg, with a splash of brandy for the grown-ups. Kids get the eggnog milk on its own. Heat 500ml milk with 150ml thickened cream, 3 tbsp caster sugar, 1 cinnamon stick and 1 tsp vanilla until steaming. Whisk 2 egg yolks in a bowl, pour in the hot milk while whisking, then return to the pan and stir over low heat for 3 minutes until slightly thick. Brew 400ml strong coffee and divide between 4 mugs. Froth the eggnog milk, pour over and grate nutmeg on top. Add 20ml brandy per mug if wanted.
T: Meet the family. Drop the strata.
D: A tightly wound woman meets her boyfriend's free-spirited family over a very awkward Christmas.
P: Serve breakfast when Meredith's strata hits the floor.

title: Last Holiday
S: Georgia's crab cakes with lemon aioli
the dishes in Georgia's Book of Possibilities

Crisp golden crab cakes packed with crab, spring onion and lemon, served with a garlicky lemon aioli and a little herb salad. Mix 400g crab meat with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 egg, 2 sliced spring onions, the zest of 1 lemon, 1 tsp Dijon and 60g panko. Shape into 12 small cakes and chill 30 minutes. Roll in 60g more panko and fry in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat for 3 minutes a side. Mix 100g mayonnaise with 1 crushed garlic clove and lemon juice. Serve with the aioli and a few dressed rocket and parsley leaves.
Grandhotel Pupp mushroom and gruyère tarts
the Grandhotel Pupp in Karlovy Vary

Little puff pastry tarts topped with garlic and thyme mushrooms, melted gruyère and a drizzle of truffle oil. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 16 squares, score a 1cm border on each and prick the middle. Fry 300g sliced mixed mushrooms in 30g butter with 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme for 6 minutes until golden. Spoon onto the pastry centres and top with 100g grated gruyère. Brush the borders with egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Drizzle with a few drops of truffle oil.
M: Chef Didier's duck with orange sauce
Chef Didier's kitchen at the grand hotel

Crisp-skinned pan-roasted duck breast with a glossy orange and orange liqueur sauce, potatoes fried in duck fat and green beans. Score the skin of 4 duck breasts and season. Place skin-side down in a cold pan and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes to render the fat, then flip and roast at 200C for 6 minutes. Rest. Fry 800g par-boiled diced potatoes in 3 tbsp of the duck fat until crisp. Pour off the rest of the fat, add the juice of 3 oranges, 2 tbsp honey, 30ml orange liqueur and 200ml chicken stock and reduce until glossy. Whisk in 20g butter. Serve with green beans.
W: Georgia ordering everything on the menu

Light, rich dark chocolate mousse in little glasses with whipped cream, fresh raspberries and a crisp tuile or wafer on top. Melt 200g dark chocolate with 30g butter and cool slightly. Whisk in 3 egg yolks one at a time. Whip 200ml thickened cream to soft peaks and fold in. Whisk 3 egg whites with 40g caster sugar to soft peaks and fold through gently in two batches. Spoon into 4 glasses and chill 3 hours. Top with whipped cream, raspberries and a thin wafer biscuit.
K: Georgia living it up at the grand hotel

A classic champagne cocktail: a bitters-soaked sugar cube and a dash of brandy topped with champagne and an orange twist. Sparkling apple for non-drinkers. Place a sugar cube in each of 4 champagne flutes and soak it with 2 dashes of aromatic bitters. Add 15ml brandy to each glass. Slowly top with chilled champagne or sparkling wine, about 120ml per glass, and watch the bubbles rise from the sugar. Twist a strip of orange peel over each glass and drop it in.
T: Order everything on the menu.
D: A shy shop assistant told she has weeks to live blows her savings on a luxury holiday in a grand European hotel.
P: Serve the main when Georgia orders everything Chef Didier makes.

title: Storm Boy
S: Fingerbone Bill teaching Mike about the land

Crusty bush damper with a soft inside, torn warm and served with butter, golden syrup and a little dish of lemon myrtle salt. Rub 60g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour and 1 tsp salt until it looks like breadcrumbs. Stir in 300ml milk to make a soft dough and knead briefly. Shape into a round, cut a cross in the top and dust with flour. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped. Mix 1 tsp sea salt with 1/2 tsp ground lemon myrtle. Serve warm with butter, golden syrup and the salt.
the pipis dug from the Coorong beaches

Pipis steamed open with garlic, chilli and a splash of stock, finished with butter, lemon and parsley and served with crusty bread. Soak 1kg pipis in cold salted water for 1 hour to purge the sand, then rinse. Fry 3 sliced garlic cloves and 1 sliced red chilli in 2 tbsp olive oil for 1 minute. Add the pipis and 100ml fish stock, cover and steam 3 to 4 minutes until they open, discarding any that stay shut. Stir in 30g butter, the juice of 1 lemon and chopped parsley. Serve with crusty bread.
M: Hideaway Tom's crisp fish and chips

Crisp battered fish fillets with thick chips, lemon, tartare sauce and chicken salt, eaten out of paper like at the shack. Bake 1kg frozen thick-cut chips at 220C for 30 minutes. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 250ml cold soda water into a batter. Dust 4 firm white fish fillets in flour, dip in the batter and fry at 180C for 5 minutes until golden. Mix 150g mayonnaise with chopped capers, pickles and dill for tartare. Toss the chips in chicken salt and serve wrapped in paper with lemon.
W: a cold night in the beach shack

Soft fluffy dumplings simmered in a buttery golden syrup sauce until sticky, served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, then stir in 1 egg and 80ml milk to a soft dough. In a wide pan, bring 250ml water, 125ml golden syrup, 80g brown sugar and 30g butter to the boil. Drop in tablespoons of dough, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Spoon into bowls with the sauce and serve with vanilla ice cream.
K: the campfire at the beach shack

Black tea brewed strong in a billy with lemon myrtle and a gum leaf, sweetened with honey and served with milk on the side. Bring 1.2L water to the boil in a billy or saucepan. Add 6 black tea bags, 1 tsp dried lemon myrtle and 1 clean gum leaf if you have one, and take off the heat. Steep 5 minutes, then remove the bags and leaf. Stir in 2 tbsp honey. Pour into 4 enamel mugs and serve with milk on the side.
T: A boy, a pelican and the Coorong.
D: A boy living with his reclusive dad on the wild South Australian coast raises an orphaned pelican called Mr Percival.
P: Serve the fish when Hideaway Tom brings in the catch.

title: The Water Diviner
S: Ayshe's hotel meze with smoky eggplant

Smoky charred eggplant dip with tahini and garlic, hummus, olives, feta and warm flatbread brushed with sumac oil. Char 2 eggplants directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning, until collapsed. Cool, scoop out the flesh and mash with 2 tbsp tahini, 1 crushed garlic clove, the juice of 1 lemon and salt. Spoon into a bowl with olive oil and parsley. Brush 4 flatbreads with oil mixed with 1 tsp sumac and grill 1 minute a side. Serve with 200g hummus, 150g olives and 150g feta.

Golden oat, coconut and golden syrup biscuits, crisp at the edges and chewy in the middle, the biscuit Australians bake to remember the Anzacs. Mix 100g rolled oats, 150g plain flour, 80g desiccated coconut and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, then stir in 1 tsp bicarb dissolved in 2 tbsp boiling water so it foams. Pour into the dry mix and stir well. Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly on lined trays, leaving room to spread, and bake at 170C for 12 to 14 minutes until golden. Cool on the trays to crisp up.
M: the Turkish officer who helps Joshua search

Chargrilled lamb kofte spiced with cumin and sumac, on warm flatbread with garlic yoghurt, tomato and onion salad and a drizzle of chilli butter. Mix 600g lamb mince with 1 grated onion, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp sumac, 1 tsp paprika, chopped parsley and salt. Shape onto 8 skewers and grill 8 minutes, turning. Mix 200g Greek yoghurt with 1 crushed garlic clove. Toss 3 diced tomatoes and 1 sliced red onion with parsley and lemon. Melt 30g butter with 1 tsp chilli flakes. Serve on warm flatbread with yoghurt, salad and chilli butter.
W: Crisp layers of buttered filo filled with pistachios, walnuts and cinnamon, soaked in honey and lemon syrup and cut into diamonds. Blitz 150g pistachios and 100g walnuts with 1 tsp cinnamon until finely chopped. Brush a 20 x 30cm tin with melted butter. Layer 6 sheets filo, brushing each with butter from 150g, scatter with half the nuts, add 4 more buttered sheets, the rest of the nuts and a final 6 sheets. Cut into diamonds and bake at 170C for 40 minutes. Simmer 200g sugar, 150ml water, 3 tbsp honey and lemon juice for 5 minutes and pour over the hot baklava.
K: Joshua finding water, and his sons, by feel

Hot apple tea brewed with dried apple, cinnamon and cloves, sweetened with a little honey and served in small glasses with lemon. Simmer 1L water with 2 diced apples, 60g dried apple, 2 cinnamon sticks and 4 cloves for 15 minutes. Take off the heat, add 2 black tea bags and steep 3 minutes. Strain, stir in 2 tbsp honey and a squeeze of lemon. Pour into small heatproof glasses and serve hot with a thin apple slice.
T: A father goes to Gallipoli.
D: After the war, an Australian farmer travels to Turkey to find the sons he lost at Gallipoli.
P: Serve the main when Joshua arrives at Ayshe's hotel in Istanbul.

title: Peter Rabbit 2: The Runaway
S: Market stall fruit skewers with honey dip
the farmers market the gang plans to raid

Strawberries, melon, grapes and kiwi fruit on skewers, served with a honey vanilla yoghurt dip and toasted coconut for rolling. Hull 250g strawberries, cube a quarter rockmelon, peel and cube 2 kiwi fruit and pick 250g grapes. Thread onto 12 skewers in rainbow order. Mix 250g Greek yoghurt with 2 tbsp honey and 1 tsp vanilla. Toast 30g shredded coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden. Serve the skewers with the yoghurt dip and the coconut for dipping and rolling.
Barnabas's big dried fruit heist at the market

Honey-roasted oats, almonds and pumpkin seeds clustered together and tossed with dried apricots, apple and cranberries, the loot from the heist. Mix 100g rolled oats, 100g almonds and 50g pumpkin seeds with 3 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp oil and 1 tsp cinnamon. Spread on a lined tray, press flat and bake at 160C for 20 minutes, stirring once. Cool completely so it clusters. Break up and toss with 80g chopped dried apricots, 60g dried apple and 60g dried cranberries.
M: Gloucester chicken, leek and bacon pie
Peter's trip into the city of Gloucester

Chicken thigh, leek, bacon and carrot in a creamy thyme sauce under golden puff pastry, with buttered peas on the side. Fry 3 diced rashers bacon, then add 800g diced chicken thigh and brown. Add 2 sliced leeks and 2 diced carrots and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 3 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml chicken stock and 150ml cream and simmer 15 minutes with thyme. Pour into a pie dish, top with 1 sheet puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 300g buttered peas.
W: the rabbits and their favourite vegetable

Moist spiced carrot and walnut cake with thick cream cheese icing, topped with little piped carrots and chopped walnuts. Mix 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp bicarb, 2 tsp cinnamon, 180g brown sugar, 3 eggs, 180ml oil, 250g grated carrot and 60g chopped walnuts. Pour into a lined 20cm square tin and bake at 170C for 45 minutes. Cool. Beat 250g cream cheese with 60g butter and 250g icing sugar and spread on top. Tint a little icing orange to pipe small carrots and scatter with walnuts.
K: Cloudy apple and pear juice with fresh lemon and a little ginger, topped with soda water over ice with thin apple slices. In a jug, mix 500ml cloudy apple juice, 300ml pear juice, the juice of 1 lemon and 1 tsp finely grated ginger. Chill 20 minutes. Fill 4 glasses with ice and thin apple slices, pour in the juice to two-thirds and top up with soda water. Stir and serve.
T: The big city fruit heist.
D: Peter runs away to the big city and falls in with a gang of animals planning a heist at the farmers market.
P: Serve the snacks when the farmers market heist begins.

title: Rise of the Guardians
S: North's workshop full of yetis and elves

Spiced gingerbread cut into yetis and elves, iced with fluffy white fur and tiny red hats, the cookies the elves keep sneaking. Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar. Mix in 300g self-raising flour, 2 tsp ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 egg. Chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm, cut into big gingerbread men for yetis and small ones for elves, and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool. Mix 200g icing sugar with 2 tbsp water, pipe shaggy white fur on the yetis and tint a little red for the elves' hats.
Sandy and his golden dream sand

Crunchy homemade honeycomb, half dipped in milk chocolate and dusted with edible gold, glittering like dream sand. Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Heat 200g caster sugar and 5 tbsp golden syrup in a deep pan, stirring until dissolved, then boil without stirring until deep golden, about 5 minutes. Take off the heat, quickly whisk in 2 tsp bicarb and pour into the tin without spreading. Set for 1 hour, then break into chunks. Dip half of each chunk in 100g melted milk chocolate and dust with edible gold glitter.
M: North, the Guardian with the big Russian accent

Seared beef strips and mushrooms in a creamy paprika, mustard and sour cream sauce, over buttery egg noodles with dill. Slice 600g rump into thin strips and sear in batches in a hot pan with oil for 1 minute. Remove. Fry 1 sliced onion and 300g sliced mushrooms in 30g butter for 6 minutes. Add 1 tsp sweet paprika, 1 tbsp Dijon and 300ml beef stock and simmer 3 minutes. Stir in 200g sour cream and the beef and warm through without boiling. Cook 400g egg noodles, toss in butter and dill and serve under the beef.
W: Bunnymund's hot cross bun egg pudding

Hot cross buns baked in a vanilla custard until puffed and golden, studded with melting mini chocolate eggs and served with cream. Butter and halve 6 hot cross buns and lay them in a baking dish, cut-side up and overlapping. Tuck 100g mini chocolate eggs between them. Whisk 3 eggs, 400ml milk, 200ml cream, 60g caster sugar and 1 tsp vanilla and pour over. Stand 15 minutes. Bake at 170C for 35 minutes until set and golden. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm with cream and a few more mini eggs.
K: Jack Frost and his icy staff

Icy blue lemonade slushie with fresh lime and mint, in glasses with sugar-frosted rims that look like Jack's frost. Dip the rims of 4 glasses in lime juice, then in caster sugar, and freeze for 10 minutes. Blend 3 cups ice with 120ml blue cordial, the juice of 2 limes and a few mint leaves until slushy. Add 600ml cold lemonade and pulse twice. Pour into the frosted glasses and garnish with a mint sprig.
T: The Guardians are coming to dinner.
D: Jack Frost joins Santa, the Easter Bunny, the Tooth Fairy and the Sandman to stop the Bogeyman.
P: Serve the sweets when the Easter Bunny's egg hunt begins.

title: Easter Parade
S: the headwaiter's grand salad routine at the restaurant

Crisp cos and butter lettuce tossed at the table with a creamy anchovy and parmesan dressing, garlic croutons and soft-boiled eggs. Tear 1 bread roll into chunks, toss with 2 tbsp olive oil and 1 crushed garlic clove and bake at 190C for 10 minutes. Cook 4 eggs for 7 minutes, cool and halve. Mash 4 anchovies with 1 garlic clove, then whisk in 1 tsp Dijon, the juice of 1 lemon, 4 tbsp mayonnaise and 30g grated parmesan. Tear 1 cos and 1 butter lettuce into a big bowl, toss with the dressing and croutons and top with the eggs and more parmesan.

Warm, airy French cheese puffs made with gruyère and a little mustard and cayenne, served straight from the oven. Bring 250ml water, 100g butter and a pinch of salt to the boil. Beat in 150g plain flour until it forms a ball and cook 1 minute. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time, then 120g grated gruyère, 1 tsp Dijon and a pinch of cayenne. Pipe 24 small mounds on lined trays, sprinkle with more gruyère and bake at 200C for 22 minutes until puffed and golden.
M: Easter Sunday roast lamb with mint sauce
Easter Sunday lunch in New York

Garlic and rosemary studded roast leg of lamb with crunchy roast potatoes, peas with butter and a sharp fresh mint sauce. Make small cuts all over a 2kg lamb leg and push in slivers of 4 garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs. Rub with oil and salt and roast at 190C for 1 hour 30 minutes for medium. Rest 20 minutes. Roast 1.2kg parboiled potatoes in oil alongside. For mint sauce, chop a bunch of mint with 1 tbsp sugar, add 3 tbsp boiling water and 4 tbsp malt vinegar. Serve with 300g buttered peas.
W: Hot cross bun bread and butter pudding

Buttered hot cross buns baked in a rich vanilla custard with orange zest until puffed, then glazed with warm apricot jam. Butter 6 halved hot cross buns and layer them in a baking dish. Whisk 3 eggs, 400ml milk, 200ml cream, 60g caster sugar, 1 tsp vanilla and the zest of 1 orange and pour over. Stand 15 minutes. Bake at 170C for 35 minutes until golden and just set. Warm 3 tbsp apricot jam with a splash of water and brush over the top. Serve warm with cream.
K: the Easter bonnets on Fifth Avenue

Cranberry, pink grapefruit and strawberry punch topped with sparkling wine, with lemonade for anyone not drinking, served with floating berries. In a punch bowl, mix 500ml cranberry juice, 300ml pink grapefruit juice and 200g sliced strawberries and chill 30 minutes. Add plenty of ice. For the adults, top glasses with sparkling wine. For everyone else, top with lemonade. Garnish each glass with a strawberry on the rim.
T: Easter on Fifth Avenue.
D: A Broadway dancer bets he can turn an unknown chorus girl into a star by the next Easter Parade.
P: Serve the sweets when the Easter Parade fills Fifth Avenue.

title: The Lighthorsemen
S: the biscuits baked to remember the troops

Golden oat and coconut biscuits made with golden syrup, crisp at the edges and chewy in the centre, the Australian remembrance biscuit. Mix 100g rolled oats, 150g plain flour, 80g desiccated coconut and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, then stir in 1 tsp bicarb dissolved in 2 tbsp boiling water so it foams. Pour into the dry mix and stir well. Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly on lined trays, leaving room to spread, and bake at 170C for 12 to 14 minutes until golden. Cool on the trays to crisp up.
Beersheba camp damper with honey butter
the light horse camp in the desert

Crusty camp damper with a soft centre, torn warm and slathered with whipped honey butter and a pinch of sea salt. Rub 60g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour and 1 tsp salt. Stir in 300ml milk to a soft dough and knead briefly. Shape into a round, cut a cross on top and dust with flour. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped. Whip 100g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of sea salt. Serve the damper warm with the honey butter.
M: Light horse camp beef and stout stew
the camp before the charge at Beersheba

Chuck steak slow-braised with stout, onion, carrot and thyme until falling apart, with buttery mash to soak up the gravy. Toss 1kg diced chuck in 2 tbsp flour and brown in batches in oil. Add 2 diced onions, 3 carrots and 2 garlic cloves and cook 5 minutes. Add 2 tbsp tomato paste, 375ml stout, 500ml beef stock, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Spoon the stew over the mash.
W: a cold desert night at camp

Fluffy dumplings simmered in a buttery golden syrup and brown sugar sauce until sticky, served hot with thick cream. Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, then stir in 1 egg and 80ml milk to a soft dough. In a wide pan, bring 250ml water, 125ml golden syrup, 80g brown sugar, 30g butter and a squeeze of lemon to the boil. Drop in tablespoons of dough, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Serve in bowls with the sauce and 200ml thick cream.
K: the billy on the campfire before Beersheba

Strong black tea stewed in a billy and sweetened with condensed milk the way the troops drank it, rich and caramel sweet. Bring 1.2L water to the boil in a billy or saucepan. Add 6 black tea bags, take off the heat and steep 5 minutes for a strong brew. Remove the bags. Spoon 1 to 2 tbsp condensed milk into each of 4 enamel mugs, pour over the hot tea and stir until creamy.
T: Beersheba, 1917.
D: Young Australian light horsemen ride into the famous charge at Beersheba during the First World War.
P: Serve the billy tea when the horses line up for the charge.

title: Beneath Hill 60
S: the parcels from home in Queensland

Golden oat, coconut and golden syrup biscuits with chopped Queensland macadamias, crisp at the edges and chewy in the middle. Mix 100g rolled oats, 150g plain flour, 60g desiccated coconut, 60g chopped macadamias and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, then stir in 1 tsp bicarb dissolved in 2 tbsp boiling water so it foams. Stir into the dry mix. Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly on lined trays and bake at 170C for 12 to 14 minutes until golden. Cool on the trays to crisp.
Oliver's home in Charters Towers, Queensland

Soft rolls stacked with thick-sliced corned beef, sweet mustard pickle, sharp cheddar and crisp lettuce, a proper Queensland lunch. Split and butter 4 soft white rolls. Spread each base generously with 1 tbsp sweet mustard pickle. Layer with 300g thickly sliced corned beef, a slice of vintage cheddar from 100g and a few leaves of iceberg lettuce. Add thinly sliced tomato and a crack of pepper, close and cut in half.
M: the tunnellers under Hill 60 at Messines

Crispy pan-fried corned beef and potato hash with onion and Worcestershire, topped with runny fried eggs and a dollop of brown sauce. Boil 800g diced potatoes for 8 minutes and drain well. Fry 1 diced onion in 30g butter and 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes. Add the potatoes and 400g diced corned beef and press flat. Cook over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning in sections, until crusty. Splash with 1 tbsp Worcestershire and add chopped parsley. Fry 4 eggs and sit one on each serve with brown sauce.
W: Fruit cake from home with brandy butter
the parcels sent from home to the front

Thick slices of rich fruit cake, warmed and spread with sweet brandy butter, served with a wedge of sharp cheddar. Beat 100g soft butter with 100g icing sugar until pale, then beat in 2 tbsp brandy a little at a time until fluffy. Chill 20 minutes. Wrap an 800g fruit cake in foil and warm at 160C for 15 minutes. Cut into thick slices and serve with the brandy butter and 150g vintage cheddar cut into wedges.
K: the long nights in the tunnels and dugouts

Hot cocoa made with dark chocolate and sweetened condensed milk, rich and warming the way the troops brewed it at the front. Heat 900ml full cream milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling. Whisk in 3 tbsp cocoa, 80g chopped dark chocolate and 120ml condensed milk until smooth and frothy. Add a pinch of salt to bring out the chocolate. Pour into 4 enamel mugs and serve straight away while it is piping hot.
T: The tunnellers under the line.
D: A Queensland mining engineer leads Australian tunnellers digging under enemy lines on the Western Front.
P: Serve the main when the tunnellers come up for air.

title: Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan
S: Nui Dat concert night satay skewers
the Little Pattie and Col Joye concert at Nui Dat

Chargrilled chicken skewers marinated in lemongrass and turmeric, with a chunky peanut satay sauce, cucumber and lime. Toss 600g diced chicken thigh with 1 chopped lemongrass stalk, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp brown sugar and marinate 30 minutes. Thread onto 12 skewers and grill 8 minutes, turning. Simmer 150g crunchy peanut butter, 200ml coconut milk, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp chilli and lime juice for 3 minutes. Serve with cucumber and lime wedges.
Phuoc Tuy prawn rice paper rolls
the Australians posted in Phuoc Tuy province

Fresh rice paper rolls with prawns, vermicelli, mint, coriander and crunchy vegetables, with a nuoc cham dipping sauce. Soak 100g rice vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes and drain. Halve 12 peeled cooked prawns lengthways. Julienne 1 carrot and 1 cucumber. Dip 12 rice paper sheets one at a time in warm water for a few seconds. Lay prawns, noodles, vegetables, mint and coriander on each and roll tightly. Mix 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp water, 1 garlic clove and chilli for dipping.
M: D Company field kitchen beef and beans
Delta Company out in the field

Chuck steak slow-cooked with smoky paprika, tomato and beans until tender, served with buttered rice and pickled chilli for a kick. Brown 800g diced chuck in batches in 2 tbsp oil. Add 1 diced onion, 2 garlic cloves and 1 diced capsicum and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp cumin, 400g tin crushed tomatoes, 400ml beef stock and a drained 400g tin cannellini beans. Cover and simmer 2 hours until tender. Cook 300g rice and stir through 20g butter. Serve with sliced pickled chilli.
W: the chocolate in the ration packs

Rich dark chocolate and orange pots topped with whipped cream, candied orange zest and a crumble of shortbread for crunch. Heat 300ml thickened cream with the zest of 1 orange until steaming. Pour over 200g chopped dark chocolate, leave 1 minute and stir until smooth. Stir in 1 tbsp orange juice. Pour into 4 small glasses and chill 2 hours. Simmer thin strips of orange zest in 2 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp water for 3 minutes. Top the pots with whipped cream, the candied zest and crumbled shortbread.
K: back at base in Nui Dat

Strong dark-roast coffee dripped over sweetened condensed milk, stirred and poured over ice, the Vietnamese way. Brew 500ml very strong dark-roast coffee, using a Vietnamese phin filter if you have one or a plunger at double strength. Spoon 2 tbsp condensed milk into each of 4 glasses. Pour the hot coffee over and stir until creamy. Fill with ice and stir again until cold.
T: Long Tan, 1966.
D: A company of Australian and New Zealand soldiers fight outnumbered in a rubber plantation in Vietnam.
P: Serve the main after the concert at Nui Dat.

title: Field of Dreams
S: Ray's Iowa cornfield around the diamond

Charred corn cobs slathered in lime mayonnaise, rolled in feta and chilli, finished with coriander and a squeeze of lime. Grill 4 husked corn cobs over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred in spots. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with the zest of 1 lime. Brush the hot cobs all over with the mayonnaise, then roll in 80g finely crumbled feta. Sprinkle with 1/2 tsp chilli powder and chopped coriander and serve with lime wedges.
Ray and Terence Mann at Fenway Park

Grilled Italian sausages in soft rolls piled with sweet fried capsicum and onion and a stripe of spicy brown mustard. Slice 1 red and 1 green capsicum and 2 onions and fry in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and sweet, seasoning with salt and a pinch of oregano. Grill 4 Italian sausages for 12 minutes, turning, then split lengthways. Toast 4 long rolls. Fill with sausage, pile on the peppers and onions and finish with wholegrain or spicy brown mustard.
M: dinner on the Kinsellas' Iowa farm

Iowa's famous oversized crumbed pork schnitzel in a soft bun with pickles, onion, mustard and mayo, served with crunchy slaw. Cut 600g pork fillet into 4 pieces and pound each to 5mm thin and wider than the bun. Dust in 60g flour, dip in 2 beaten eggs and press into 150g crushed crackers mixed with panko. Shallow fry at 180C for 3 minutes a side until golden. Toss shredded cabbage with 3 tbsp mayonnaise and 1 tbsp vinegar. Serve in 4 soft buns with mustard, mayo, pickles and sliced onion and the slaw on the side.
W: Is this heaven? No, it's Iowa

Cinnamon apple pie with a golden sugared crust, served warm with vanilla ice cream and a drizzle of salted caramel. Peel and slice 6 Granny Smith apples and toss with 100g caster sugar, 2 tsp cinnamon, 2 tbsp cornflour and the juice of half a lemon. Line a 23cm pie dish with 1 sheet shortcrust pastry and fill. Cover with a second sheet, crimp and cut slits. Brush with egg and sprinkle with sugar. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes, then 180C for 35 minutes. Serve warm with ice cream and salted caramel sauce.
K: Shoeless Joe stepping out of the corn

Fresh squeezed lemonade blended with ripe strawberries and a little mint, poured over ice on a summer evening on the farm. Simmer 150g caster sugar with 150ml water until dissolved and cool. Blend 250g hulled strawberries with the syrup and strain. Stir in the juice of 6 lemons and 700ml cold water. Chill for 30 minutes. Pour over ice into 4 tall glasses and garnish with sliced strawberries, lemon wheels and mint.
T: If you build it, they will eat.
D: An Iowa farmer builds a baseball diamond in his cornfield after hearing a voice.
P: Serve the main when Ray plays catch with his dad.

title: Father of the Bride
S: George's supermarket meltdown over the hot dog buns

Eight grilled frankfurts in exactly eight toasted buns, with sweet fried onions, mustard, relish and a little grated cheddar. Slowly fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes until golden. Simmer 8 frankfurts for 5 minutes, then grill 2 minutes for colour. Toast 8 hot dog buns, no more and no less. Fill each with a frankfurt, the onions, a squeeze of mustard, a spoon of relish and a sprinkle of 80g grated cheddar.
meeting the MacKenzies in Bel Air

Warm blinis with crème fraîche, smoked salmon, capers, red onion and dill, fancy bites for meeting the very rich in-laws. Warm 16 cocktail blinis at 180C for 4 minutes. Mix 150g crème fraîche with the zest of 1 lemon and a pinch of salt. Top each blini with a spoon of crème fraîche, a ribbon of smoked salmon from 150g, 2 capers and a sliver of red onion. Finish with a dill sprig and cracked pepper and serve with lemon wedges.
M: Franck planning the reception at the Banks house

Pan-roasted chicken breast with a creamy tarragon, white wine and mustard sauce, crispy potatoes and buttered green beans. Roast 800g halved baby potatoes in oil at 220C for 35 minutes. Season 4 chicken breasts with the skin on and sear skin-side down in a hot pan for 5 minutes, flip and roast at 200C for 12 minutes. Rest. Fry 1 diced shallot in the pan, add 100ml white wine and reduce, then 200ml cream, 1 tsp Dijon and 1 tbsp chopped tarragon and simmer 2 minutes. Serve with the potatoes and 300g buttered beans.
W: Annie's wedding cake that cost a fortune

Two layers of lemon butter cake filled with lemon curd and covered in silky white vanilla buttercream, decorated with fresh flowers. Beat 200g butter and 200g caster sugar, add 4 eggs and the zest of 2 lemons, then fold in 250g self-raising flour and 100ml milk. Bake in two lined 20cm tins at 180C for 25 minutes. Cool. Sandwich with 150g lemon curd. Beat 200g butter with 400g icing sugar, 2 tbsp milk and 1 tsp vanilla until white and fluffy and spread over. Decorate with edible flowers.
K: George and Annie's late-night basketball in the driveway

Thick vanilla malted milkshakes with a drizzle of caramel and whipped cream, the kind you'd make after midnight in the kitchen. Chill 4 glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Blend 600ml cold milk, 8 scoops vanilla ice cream, 4 tbsp malted milk powder and 1 tsp vanilla until thick. Drizzle caramel sauce down the insides of the glasses, pour in the shake and top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream and a sprinkle of malt.
T: Eight franks, twelve buns.
D: A dad struggles to let go as his daughter plans her wedding with an over-the-top planner.
P: Serve the hot dogs when George loses it over the buns.

title: Remember the Titans
S: Coach Boone's training camp at Gettysburg

Long rolls stacked with ham, salami, provolone, shredded lettuce, tomato, pickled peppers and a tangy oregano vinaigrette, cut into chunks to share. Whisk 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1/2 tsp dried oregano and pepper. Split 2 long baguettes and drizzle the insides with half the dressing. Layer with 150g sliced ham, 100g salami and 100g provolone. Top with shredded iceberg, sliced tomato, thin red onion and pickled peppers, then the rest of the dressing. Press closed, wrap tightly for 10 minutes and cut each into 4.
Friday night football in Alexandria, Virginia

Grilled frankfurts in toasted buns smothered in beef chilli, diced onion, mustard and melted cheddar. Brown 300g beef mince with 1 diced onion, then add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 200g passata and 100ml water and simmer 15 minutes until thick. Grill 8 frankfurts for 6 minutes. Toast 8 hot dog buns. Fill each with a frankfurt, spoon over the chilli, scatter with 120g grated cheddar and grill 2 minutes to melt. Top with diced white onion and mustard.
M: the Titans' left side, strong side

Buttermilk brined chicken fried crisp and golden, with creamy mash, peppery white gravy and hot honey on the side. Soak 1.2kg chicken pieces in 400ml buttermilk with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp hot sauce for at least 2 hours. Toss in 200g plain flour mixed with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and salt. Fry at 165C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden and cooked through. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with butter and milk. Make gravy with 30g butter, 2 tbsp flour, 400ml milk and lots of pepper. Warm 3 tbsp honey with chilli flakes.
W: Juicy spiced peaches baked under a golden buttermilk biscuit topping with cinnamon sugar crunch, served warm with vanilla ice cream. Toss 2 x 820g tins drained sliced peaches with 60g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tbsp cornflour and a squeeze of lemon and tip into a baking dish. Rub 80g cold butter into 200g self-raising flour and 2 tbsp sugar, then stir in 150ml buttermilk. Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and sprinkle with 1 tbsp sugar mixed with cinnamon. Bake at 190C for 30 minutes until golden. Serve warm with ice cream.
K: Sunshine and the hot Southern summer

Half Southern sweet tea, half fresh lemonade, poured over ice with lemon wheels and mint for a hot Virginia afternoon. Steep 6 black tea bags in 700ml boiling water with 80g sugar for 5 minutes, then remove the bags and chill. Stir 80g sugar into the juice of 5 lemons and 500ml cold water until dissolved. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour in the tea to halfway and top with the lemonade. Garnish with lemon wheels and mint.
T: Strong side. Left side. Dinner side.
D: A newly integrated high school football team in 1971 Virginia comes together under a new coach.
P: Serve the main after the big game.

title: Rudy
S: Rudy's shifts at the steel mill in Joliet

Thick slices of cold glazed meatloaf on toasted white bread with sharp cheddar, pickles and a smear of tomato relish. Mix 500g beef mince, 1 grated onion, 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 tsp Worcestershire and salt. Press into a lined loaf tin, spread with 3 tbsp tomato sauce mixed with 1 tbsp brown sugar and bake at 180C for 50 minutes. Cool completely and slice thickly. Toast 8 slices white bread. Fill with the meatloaf, 4 slices cheddar, pickles and tomato relish and cut in half.
game day tailgating at Notre Dame

Bratwurst simmered in lager and onions, then grilled until snappy, in toasted rolls with the beer onions and spicy brown mustard. Simmer 8 bratwurst in 375ml lager with 2 sliced onions and 20g butter for 15 minutes. Lift out the brats and grill for 6 minutes, turning, until charred. Keep boiling the onions until the liquid reduces and they turn sticky. Toast 8 rolls, fill with a brat and a pile of beer onions and finish with wholegrain mustard.
M: the Ruettiger family table in Joliet

Chuck roast braised low and slow with onions, carrots and potatoes in a rich gravy, served with horseradish cream and crusty bread. Season a 1.5kg chuck roast and brown all over in 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot. Add 2 quartered onions, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 500ml beef stock, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and cook at 160C for 2 hours. Add 4 carrots and 800g halved potatoes and cook 1 hour more. Thicken the juices with 1 tbsp cornflour. Mix 150g sour cream with 2 tbsp horseradish cream.
W: Cinnamon apples under a crunchy pecan and oat crumble, baked bubbling and served with warm vanilla custard. Peel and slice 6 Granny Smith apples and toss with 60g caster sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and lemon juice. Tip into a baking dish. Rub 100g cold butter into 100g plain flour, then stir in 60g rolled oats, 80g brown sugar and 50g chopped pecans. Scatter over the apples and bake at 180C for 40 minutes until golden. Serve with 600ml warm custard.
K: the Golden Dome at Notre Dame on a cold autumn day

Cloudy apple juice warmed with cinnamon, cloves, orange and a little maple syrup, served steaming in mugs for a cold game day. Pour 1.2L cloudy apple juice into a saucepan with 2 tbsp maple syrup, 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 1 star anise and 1 sliced orange. Heat gently for 15 minutes without boiling. Strain into 4 mugs and add a cinnamon stick and orange slice to each.
T: Never give up. Never skip dessert.
D: A working-class kid from a steel town chases his dream of playing football for Notre Dame.
P: Serve the main when Rudy finally runs onto the field.

title: Phar Lap
S: Flemington Cup day beef party pies

Homemade little pies of peppery beef mince in rich gravy under a puff pastry lid, served hot with tomato sauce. Brown 500g beef mince with 1 diced onion. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml beef stock, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and plenty of pepper and simmer 15 minutes until thick. Cool. Cut 12 bases from 2 sheets shortcrust pastry and press into a greased patty pan tin. Fill, top with 12 rounds of puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 20 minutes. Serve with tomato sauce.

Crisp toasts with vintage cheddar, thin apple slices, fruit chutney and a few thyme leaves, apples for Tommy and Big Red alike. Slice 1 baguette into 20 rounds, brush with oil and bake at 190C for 8 minutes. Thinly slice 2 red apples and toss in lemon juice. Spread each toast with a little fruit chutney, top with a slice of 200g vintage cheddar and a slice of apple. Finish with thyme leaves and cracked pepper.
M: Big Red's Cup day roast beef rolls

Soft rolls piled with rare roast beef, horseradish cream, caramelised onion, rocket and pickled beetroot, the grand picnic for Cup Day. Rub a 1kg beef eye fillet or rump with oil, salt and pepper, sear all over and roast at 200C for 20 minutes for rare. Rest and chill, then slice thinly. Slowly fry 2 sliced onions in butter for 20 minutes. Mix 150g sour cream with 2 tbsp horseradish cream. Split 4 soft rolls, spread with horseradish cream and fill with beef, onions, rocket and sliced pickled beetroot.
W: Phar Lap, the horse they called Big Red

Sponge squares split and filled with raspberry jam and cream, dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in coconut. Cut a 20cm square sponge cake into 16 squares and freeze 30 minutes. Mix 400g icing sugar, 40g cocoa, 20g melted butter and 150ml boiling water into a thin icing. Dip each square in the icing, let it drip, then roll in 150g desiccated coconut. Set for 30 minutes. Split each in half and fill with raspberry jam and whipped cream from 200ml thickened cream.
K: Phar Lap's big win at Agua Caliente in Mexico

Tequila and fresh pink grapefruit with lime and soda in a salt-rimmed glass. Leave out the tequila for a grapefruit spritz. Rub a lime wedge around the rims of 4 tall glasses and dip in sea salt. Fill with ice. Add 45ml tequila, 90ml pink grapefruit juice and the juice of half a lime to each glass. Top with 60ml soda water and stir gently. Garnish with a grapefruit wedge.
T: The race that stops a nation.
D: The story of the champion racehorse who won the hearts of Depression-era Australia.
P: Serve the snacks when the Melbourne Cup starts.

title: Seabiscuit
S: Tick Tock McGlaughlin calling the races on the radio

Warm roasted peanuts tossed with butter, smoked paprika, brown sugar and sea salt, served in paper bags like at the track. Toss 400g raw unsalted peanuts with 30g melted butter, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cayenne and 1 tsp salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes so the coating crisps, then serve in paper bags.
Seabiscuit's apple and cheddar hand pies

Flaky little hand pies filled with cinnamon apple and sharp cheddar, baked golden and sprinkled with sugar. Cook 3 peeled diced apples with 30g butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon for 6 minutes until soft, then cool. Cut 8 rounds from 2 sheets shortcrust pastry. Put a spoon of apple and a few cubes of cheddar from 100g on each, fold over and crimp with a fork. Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with sugar and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until golden.
M: the match race against War Admiral at Pimlico

Maryland-style crab cakes seasoned with celery salt and paprika, seared golden and served with crunchy slaw, lemon and spiced chips. Mix 500g crab meat with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 egg, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp celery salt, 1/2 tsp paprika, chopped parsley and 60g panko. Shape into 8 cakes and chill 30 minutes. Fry in oil over medium heat for 3 minutes a side. Bake 800g frozen chips and toss with paprika salt. Toss shredded cabbage with 3 tbsp mayonnaise and vinegar. Serve with lemon wedges.
W: Deep cinnamon apple pie with a crumbly brown sugar streusel top, served warm with vanilla ice cream. Peel and slice 6 Granny Smith apples and toss with 80g caster sugar, 2 tsp cinnamon and 2 tbsp cornflour. Line a 23cm pie dish with 1 sheet shortcrust pastry and fill. Rub 60g butter into 80g plain flour and 60g brown sugar and scatter over the top. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes until golden and bubbling. Cool 20 minutes and serve with ice cream.
K: George Woolf, the jockey they called the Iceman

Black tea brewed with honey and orange peel, chilled and mixed with fresh orange juice, poured over plenty of ice with mint. Steep 5 black tea bags in 800ml boiling water with 3 tbsp honey and strips of peel from 1 orange for 5 minutes. Remove the bags and peel, then chill for 1 hour. Stir in the juice of 3 oranges. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour over the tea and garnish with orange slices and mint.
T: The little horse that could.
D: An undersized racehorse and a team of broken men become a symbol of hope during the Depression.
P: Serve the snacks before the big match race against War Admiral.
